```json
      "value": "Lamp",
      "type": "text"
    },
    {
      "value": "?",
      "error": 1207,
      "message": "The function \"Nonsense\" cannot be found"
    }
  ]
}
```

Let ( $$name = … ) sets the session's variable, as FileMaker's Data Viewer does. No layout: 400, code 105; a layout that isn't there: code 105; a record id that isn't a whole number: 400, code 101, and a record that is gone: code 101. No formulas list: 400, code 960.

<a id="debug-get-tabularius-debug-v1-databases-database-current"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/debug/v1/databases/{database}/current`

The Data Viewer's Current tab: the record's fields and the session's $$variables.

**Permissions:** A session token for this file (Authorization: Bearer …, or X-FM-Data-Access-Token), from a Data API sign-in (which needs fmrest) or the web client's (fmapp or fmwebdirect), or a scoped API token (ohbt_…) for this file; a token scoped to surfaces must include fmrest, and one for a local-only account works only from the server itself. The account must have the [Full Access] privilege set; any other set gets 403, code 9 ("Account "…" doesn't have full access, which the script debugger needs").

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | path | string | yes | The hosted file's name (URL-encoded). |
| `layout` | query | string | yes | The layout the web client shows. |
| `recordId` | query | number | no | The record it shows. |

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/debug/v1/databases/Invoices/current?layout=Items&recordId=1
Authorization: Bearer 3f1d0c6e8a…
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "layout": "Items",
  "occurrence": "Items",
  "table": "Items",
  "recordId": 1,
  "fields": {
    "Name": "Lamp",
    "Price": 10,
    "Status": "open"
  },
  "variables": {}
}
```

Without recordId, fields is {}. Errors as for POST /evaluate.

<a id="debug-post-tabularius-debug-v1-databases-database-recordings"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/debug/v1/databases/{database}/recordings`

Time travel: runs the script to the end on a throwaway copy, offline, recording each step (where it stood, its variables and found set, what it did to records) for stepping back and forth afterwards.

**Permissions:** A session token for this file (Authorization: Bearer …, or X-FM-Data-Access-Token), from a Data API sign-in (which needs fmrest) or the web client's (fmapp or fmwebdirect), or a scoped API token (ohbt_…) for this file; a token scoped to surfaces must include fmrest, and one for a local-only account works only from the server itself. The account must have the [Full Access] privilege set; any other set gets 403, code 9 ("Account "…" doesn't have full access, which the script debugger needs").

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | path | string | yes | The hosted file's name (URL-encoded). |
| `script` | body | string | yes | The script's name. |
| `parameter` | body | string | no | The script parameter. |
| `layout` | body | string | no | The layout it starts on. |
| `foundSet` | body | array of number | no | Record ids of the starting found set. |
| `recordId` | body | number | no | The current record. |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/debug/v1/databases/Invoices/recordings
Authorization: Bearer 3f1d0c6e8a…
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "script": "Finish",
  "layout": "Items"
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "script": "Finish",
  "steps": [
    {
      "script": "Finish",
      "index": 0,
      "line": "Exit Script [ Result: \"ok\" ]",
      "stack": [
        {
          "script": "Finish",
          "index": 0
        }
      ],
      "lastError": 0,
      "layout": "Items",
      "mode": "browse",
      "foundCount": 1,
      "foundSet": [
        1
      ],
      "recordId": 1,
      "variables": {
        "locals": {},
        "globals": {}
      }
    }
  ],
  "done": {
    "result": "ok",
    "error": 0,
    "halted": false,
    "layout": "Items",
    "foundCount": 3,
    "recordId": 1,
    "mode": "browse",
    "steps": 2,
    "foundSet": [
      1,
      2,
      3
    ]
  }
}
```

The session's globals are copied for the run, not changed. A file over 1 GB: 400, code 960. Only POST.

<a id="security"></a>

## Manage Security

Accounts, privilege sets, extended privileges, API tokens, two-factor sign-in and approval of AI agents' proposed changes, at /tabularius/security/v1/databases/{database}. Like design mode it is a GET for the whole picture and a POST of all-or-none changes, signs in with the Data API's session tokens, and needs [Full Access]. Most replies carry the whole security picture again (security). Errors come back as {"error": {"code", "message"}} with an HTTP status: a missing, expired or other file's token is 401 with code 952 (a session token sent for another file also ends that session), an account without [Full Access] is 403 with code 9, a file that is no longer open is 404 with code 802, a method a path does not answer is 405 with code 3 ("Command is unavailable"), a body that isn't JSON is 400 with code 960, and an error from the file itself (a bad change, a missing name) is 400 with its FileMaker error code.

Source: `packages/server/src/security.ts`, `packages/server/src/account-provisioning.ts`

| Method | Path | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| POST | [`/tabularius/security/v1/databases/{database}/accounts/import/preview`](#security-post-tabularius-security-v1-databases-database-accounts-import-preview) | Preview desired local-account assignment and active state from CSV without account or audit writes. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/security/v1/databases/{database}/accounts/import/apply`](#security-post-tabularius-security-v1-databases-database-accounts-import-apply) | Revalidate and apply a previewed CSV in one transaction, with a durable sanitized idempotency receipt. |
| GET | [`/tabularius/security/v1/databases/{database}`](#security-get-tabularius-security-v1-databases-database) | The whole security picture: accounts, privilege sets, API tokens, pending agent changes, the password policy and two-factor switch, and the lists the privilege pickers choose from. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/security/v1/databases/{database}`](#security-post-tabularius-security-v1-databases-database) | Applies a list of security changes, all or none, and returns the new picture. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/security/v1/databases/{database}/tokens`](#security-post-tabularius-security-v1-databases-database-tokens) | Mints a scoped API token for an account; the token is shown this once. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/security/v1/databases/{database}/migrate`](#security-post-tabularius-security-v1-databases-database-migrate) | First sign-in for a converted file: gives each account still on the file's own password (or the ones named) a temporary password it must change, and returns them this once. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/security/v1/databases/{database}/record-rule/preview`](#security-post-tabularius-security-v1-databases-database-record-rule-preview) | Tries a limited-access record rule before saving it: whether it works, which sample records it allows, and how many of the table it allows. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/security/v1/databases/{database}/totp/{account}`](#security-post-tabularius-security-v1-databases-database-totp-account) | Starts a second factor for an account: a new secret and its otpauth:// URI to show as a QR code, pending until confirmed. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/security/v1/databases/{database}/totp/{account}/confirm`](#security-post-tabularius-security-v1-databases-database-totp-account-confirm) | Confirms a pending second factor with a code from the authenticator app. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/security/v1/databases/{database}/pending/{id}/approve`](#security-post-tabularius-security-v1-databases-database-pending-id-approve) | Approves an approval-gated AI agent's proposed record change: it is applied as the agent, with the agent's own privileges. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/security/v1/databases/{database}/pending/{id}/reject`](#security-post-tabularius-security-v1-databases-database-pending-id-reject) | Rejects an AI agent's proposed change: it is discarded without being applied. |

<a id="security-post-tabularius-security-v1-databases-database-accounts-import-preview"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/security/v1/databases/{database}/accounts/import/preview`

Preview desired local-account assignment and active state from CSV without account or audit writes.

**Permissions:** An interactive session Authorization: Bearer token bound to this database, active and unexpired, with current Full Access and no owed password change. API tokens (ohbt_) and agent identities are refused. Authorization is checked again after reading the body.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | path | string | yes | The hosted file's name (URL-encoded). |
| `csv` | body | string | yes | UTF-8 CSV with exactly account,privilegeSet,active columns (any order), with explicit true/false active values. No credential columns. |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/security/v1/databases/Invoices/accounts/import/preview
Authorization: Bearer 3f1d0c6e8a…
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "csv": "account,privilegeSet,active\nClerk,Viewers,true"
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "valid": true,
  "rows": [
    {
      "row": 2,
      "account": "Clerk",
      "actions": [
        "no-op"
      ],
      "before": {
        "privilegeSet": "Viewers",
        "active": true
      },
      "after": {
        "privilegeSet": "Viewers",
        "active": true
      },
      "credentialSetupRequired": false
    }
  ],
  "errors": [],
  "previewToken": "signed-preview-binding",
  "expiresAt": "2026-10-14T12:05:00.000Z"
}
```

New identities get source Tabularius, a null password hash and must-change enabled; they cannot password-sign-in until separate admin credential setup. Existing credentials and must-change flags are preserved. Rows are CSV record numbers including the header; quoted line breaks do not add record numbers. BOM, CRLF, commas and escaped quotes are supported; malformed quoting is refused. Account matching follows SQLite NOCASE (ASCII only), resolves stored spelling, and rejects duplicate keys, ambiguous existing names and Unicode case variants that JavaScript folds together but SQLite does not. External mappings, agents, bracketed built-in names, surrounding spaces, control characters, formula prefixes (=, +, -, @), unknown privilege sets, self changes (including a session mapping), and Full Access grants are refused. Missing rows have no effect. There is no delete, rename, type conversion or privilege-set creation. Row validation errors return valid:false and no previewToken; structural CSV errors are 400. The signed preview expires after five minutes and binds actor, mapping, database, parsed input digest and account/privilege snapshot. Account metadata only is returned; never credentials. The JSON body and decoded CSV are each limited to 1 MiB, with at most 1,000 rows (413 when exceeded). Names/sets over 256 characters produce row validation errors. Durable SQLite rate counters allow 20 previews and 5 applies per minute per actor/file, plus 60 requests per minute per IP/file before authentication. Four concurrent import requests per serving process are allowed. Throttling returns 429 with Retry-After:60. Rate counters are the only preview-side writes and are shared across processes.

<a id="security-post-tabularius-security-v1-databases-database-accounts-import-apply"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/security/v1/databases/{database}/accounts/import/apply`

Revalidate and apply a previewed CSV in one transaction, with a durable sanitized idempotency receipt.

**Permissions:** The same interactive Full Access session gate as preview, rechecked on apply and under the transaction. API tokens and owed password changes are refused, including on receipt replay.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | path | string | yes | The hosted file's name (URL-encoded). |
| `csv` | body | string | yes | The same parsed desired-state input used for preview. |
| `previewToken` | body | string | yes | The short-lived signed preview binding. |
| `idempotencyKey` | body | string | yes | 1–128 ASCII letters, digits, underscores or hyphens; use a new key for a new operation, retain it for retries. |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/security/v1/databases/Invoices/accounts/import/apply
Authorization: Bearer 3f1d0c6e8a…
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "csv": "account,privilegeSet,active\nClerk,Viewers,true",
  "previewToken": "signed-preview-binding",
  "idempotencyKey": "import-20261014-1"
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "valid": true,
  "rows": [
    {
      "row": 2,
      "account": "Clerk",
      "actions": [
        "no-op"
      ],
      "before": {
        "privilegeSet": "Viewers",
        "active": true
      },
      "after": {
        "privilegeSet": "Viewers",
        "active": true
      },
      "credentialSetupRequired": false
    }
  ],
  "errors": [],
  "batchId": "c844ae89-d5ab-4218-a421-97934fa5802c"
}
```

BEGIN IMMEDIATE covers authorization, snapshot validation, planning, all account API mutations, successful account events, batch summary and receipt. Any failure rolls them back; a separate rejection event records only a reason code. Same key, actor and parsed input returns the original sanitized result after restart, even when the old preview expired. Changed input or actor under that key returns 409. A stale, altered or wrong-file preview returns 409 and requires another preview. Reimporting unchanged desired state with a new key yields no-op rows and no duplicate account-change events. Deactivation keeps the password and passkeys, ends sessions and deletes the API tokens of the account after commit; inactive accounts cannot authenticate by password, passkey or API token. Reactivation does not bring tokens or sessions back; the account signs in again and creates new tokens. Deletion, demotion and deactivation share a store guard under the write lock: keep an active local non-agent Full Access account with a working password credential or passkey. Imported verifiers that cannot authenticate do not qualify. Recovery administrators must have unambiguous sign-in names and all MFA required by account or file policy enrolled (confirmed TOTP or a registered passkey); pending enrollment is insufficient. These checks include accounts absent from the CSV. Inactive accounts, external mappings and credential-free placeholders do not count as alternatives. CSV account events record the actor, batch ID, source csv, target, row and before/after state. Responses and receipts contain no passwords, credential hashes or authentication tokens. Credential setup uses the separate admin password-reset flow with must-change enabled. Same limits as preview; unrecognized JSON fields are refused.

<a id="security-get-tabularius-security-v1-databases-database"></a>

<a id="security-post-tabularius-security-v1-databases-database"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/security/v1/databases/{database}`

Applies a list of security changes, all or none, and returns the new picture.

**Permissions:** A session token for this file (Authorization: Bearer …, or X-FM-Data-Access-Token), from a Data API sign-in (which needs fmrest) or the web client's (fmapp or fmwebdirect), or a scoped API token (ohbt_…) for this file; a token scoped to surfaces must include fmrest, and one for a local-only account works only from the server itself. The account must have the [Full Access] privilege set; any other set gets 403, code 9 ("Account "…" doesn't have full access, which security changes need").

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | path | string | yes | The hosted file's name (URL-encoded). |
| `changes` | body | array of object | yes | Each one of: setAccount {name, password?, privilegeSet?, mustChange?, localOnly?, require2fa?}, setExternalAccount {name, privilegeSet}, setAgentAccount {name, privilegeSet, needsApproval?}, deleteAccount {name}, savePrivilegeSet {set}, deletePrivilegeSet {name}, setPasswordPolicy {policy}, setRequireTotpForFullAccess {on}, disableTotp {account}, revokeApiToken {id}. |

```json
      "fmmcp"
    ]
  }
}
```

No account: 400, code 960 ("account is required"). An account, surface or layout that isn't there: 400, code 960.

<a id="security-post-tabularius-security-v1-databases-database-record-rule-preview"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/security/v1/databases/{database}/record-rule/preview`

Tries a limited-access record rule before saving it: whether it works, which sample records it allows, and how many of the table it allows.

**Permissions:** A session token for this file (Authorization: Bearer …, or X-FM-Data-Access-Token), from a Data API sign-in (which needs fmrest) or the web client's (fmapp or fmwebdirect), or a scoped API token (ohbt_…) for this file; a token scoped to surfaces must include fmrest, and one for a local-only account works only from the server itself. The account must have the [Full Access] privilege set; any other set gets 403, code 9 ("Account "…" doesn't have full access, which security changes need").

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | path | string | yes | The hosted file's name (URL-encoded). |
| `table` | body | string | yes | The base table. |
| `rule` | body | string | yes | The rule's formula. |
| `account` | body | string | no | The account it is evaluated as (Get ( AccountName )). |
| `limit` | body | number | no | Sample records (default 10, at most 200). |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/security/v1/databases/Invoices/record-rule/preview
Authorization: Bearer 3f1d0c6e8a…
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "table": "Items",
  "rule": "Status = \"open\"",
  "limit": 2
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "table": "Items",
  "rule": "Status = \"open\"",
  "account": "",
  "valid": true,
  "total": 3,
  "allowed": 3,
  "samples": [
    {
      "recordId": 1,
      "allowed": true,
      "label": "Lamp"
    },
    {
      "recordId": 2,
      "allowed": true,
      "label": "Desk"
    }
  ]
}
```

A rule that fails on every sample (or doesn't compile, on an empty table) gives valid: false and error, and no allowed count; a row it fails on counts as not allowed. No table or rule: 400, code 960. A table that isn't there: 400, code 100.

<a id="assistant"></a>

## AI assistant

The web client's and design mode's AI assistant, at /tabularius/assistant/v1/databases/{database}. It signs in with the same session tokens as the Data API, and answers as the signed-in account: the model reads the file only through the MCP tools, run in-process with that account's privileges. It is off unless the server was started with an API key (tabularius serve --ai, key in ANTHROPIC_API_KEY). Errors come back as {"error": {"code", "message"}}; a missing or expired token is 401 with code 952, and a file that isn't hosted is 404 with code 802.

Source: `packages/server/src/assistant.ts`

| Method | Path | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | [`/tabularius/assistant/v1/databases/{database}`](#assistant-get-tabularius-assistant-v1-databases-database) | Whether the assistant can be used on this file by this account, which models answer, and what it may do. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/assistant/v1/databases/{database}`](#assistant-post-tabularius-assistant-v1-databases-database) | Asks the assistant a question about the file; the answer comes back whole, or streamed as JSON lines. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/assistant/v1/databases/{database}/handover`](#assistant-post-tabularius-assistant-v1-databases-database-handover) | A handover memo for whoever takes the solution over, written from the file's design alone, as a Markdown or HTML download. Given a memo in the body, it only packages that text for download. |
| GET | [`/tabularius/assistant/v1/databases/{database}/connections/{name}`](#assistant-get-tabularius-assistant-v1-databases-database-connections-name) | An AI-drafted connection for this file, as the card under the assistant's answer shows it: its settings, every place the keys would go (scheme, host and port: an OAuth 2 token address counts), which secrets are set (never their values) and the last test. |
| PUT | [`/tabularius/assistant/v1/databases/{database}/connections/{name}/secrets/{field}`](#assistant-put-tabularius-assistant-v1-databases-database-connections-name-secrets-field) | Types one secret of the draft (an access key, say). It goes straight into the server's sealed store; DELETE on the same path clears it. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/assistant/v1/databases/{database}/connections/{name}/test`](#assistant-post-tabularius-assistant-v1-databases-database-connections-name-test) | Signs in to the service with the draft's secrets and asks something harmless (for S3, a one-object listing), without changing anything. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/assistant/v1/databases/{database}/connections/{name}/approve`](#assistant-post-tabularius-assistant-v1-databases-database-connections-name-approve) | A person's go-ahead: the draft becomes usable by scripts of this file, by name. |
| DELETE | [`/tabularius/assistant/v1/databases/{database}/connections/{name}`](#assistant-delete-tabularius-assistant-v1-databases-database-connections-name) | Discards the draft. |

<a id="assistant-get-tabularius-assistant-v1-databases-database"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/assistant/v1/databases/{database}`

Whether the assistant can be used on this file by this account, which models answer, and what it may do.

**Permissions:** A Data API session token (Authorization: Bearer, or X-FM-Data-Access-Token) for this file, from a Data API or web client sign-in, or a scoped API token (ohbt_…) for this file allowed Data API access (fmrest). The account's privilege set needs fmrest (fmapp or fmwebdirect for a web client session). Nothing else is checked: an account without fmmcp, or a file with AI turned off, gets available: false.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | path | string | yes | The hosted file's name. |

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/assistant/v1/databases/Invoices
Authorization: Bearer 3f1d0c6e8a…
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "available": true,
  "model": "claude-opus-5-5",
  "price": {
    "input": 4,
    "output": 20
  },
  "fastModel": "claude-haiku-5-5",
  "canDesign": false,
  "canExplainScripts": false
}
```

available is true only when the server has an API key, the privilege set has fmmcp and AI is not turned off for the file (or for a file it uses); aiOff: true is added when AI is turned off. price is the model's list price in US dollars per million tokens, left out for a model without one. fastModel is left out when the fast model is set to off. canDesign is [Full Access]; canExplainScripts is [Full Access], or a set that can modify scripts and reads everything. [Full Access] also gets usageToday {tokens, limit?} for the server and usageMonth {month, tokens, costUsd, questions, unpriced, budgetUsd?} for the month so far (UTC), and when the server has a per-account daily token limit, an account that can use the assistant gets accountUsageToday {tokens, limit}.

<a id="assistant-post-tabularius-assistant-v1-databases-database"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/assistant/v1/databases/{database}`

Asks the assistant a question about the file; the answer comes back whole, or streamed as JSON lines.

**Permissions:** A Data API session token (Authorization: Bearer, or X-FM-Data-Access-Token) for this file, from a Data API or web client sign-in, or a scoped API token (ohbt_…) for this file allowed Data API access (fmrest). The account's privilege set needs fmrest (fmapp or fmwebdirect for a web client session), and the fmmcp extended privilege (AI access). Refused with 503 (code 3) when the server has no API key, 403 (code 9) when AI is turned off for the file or a file it uses, 401 (code 9) without fmmcp, and 429 (code 3) once the server's or the account's daily token limit, or the monthly budget, is used. The assistant only reads: design tools are offered to [Full Access] only, and design changes come back as proposals, never applied. The model is given a masked field's stand-in, never its value, and a chart by a masked field is refused.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | path | string | yes | The hosted file's name. |
| `Accept` | header | string | no | application/x-ndjson streams the answer as one JSON object per line; anything else gets one JSON reply. |
| `messages` | body | array of object | yes | The conversation so far, [{role: "user" \| "assistant", content}], ending with the user's question. Other roles and empty messages are dropped; long histories are cut to the latest messages. |
| `context` | body | object | no | What the window is looking at: layout, recordId, field, mode (browse, find, design, debug, security, viewer), foundSet, design, security, debug, draft, failure. |
| `image` | body | object | no | {mediaType, data}: a picture to design a layout from. mediaType is image/png, image/jpeg, image/gif or image/webp; data is the picture in base64, up to about 3.7 MB. Only accounts with [Full Access] may send one (401, code 9, otherwise); a bad type or data is 400 (code 5), a picture too big 413. |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/assistant/v1/databases/Invoices
Authorization: Bearer 3f1d0c6e8a…
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "messages": [
    {
      "role": "user",
      "content": "How many invoices are open?"
    }
  ],
  "context": {
    "layout": "Invoices",
    "recordId": 3,
    "mode": "browse"
  }
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "reply": "There are 12 open invoices.",
  "proposals": [],
  "foundSets": [],
  "drafts": [],
  "charts": [],
  "dashboards": [],
  "cleanups": [],
  "automations": [],
  "tools": [
    "summarize_records"
  ],
  "usage": {
    "inputTokens": 5120,
    "cachedTokens": 4800,
    "cacheWriteTokens": 0,
    "outputTokens": 42,
    "costUsd": 0.0021
  },
  "model": "claude-haiku-5-5",
  "ms": 1830
}
```

With Accept: application/x-ndjson the reply is a stream (content-type application/x-ndjson), one JSON object per line: {"step": "Looking at layout \"Invoices\""} for each tool used, {"tool": {"id", "name", "label", "args", "result", "resultLength", "error"?}} once the tool has answered (its arguments with secrets hidden and long values cut, the start of the result on one line with secrets hidden; both for the person to read, not for scripts to rely on), {"text": "…"} for pieces of the reply as the model writes them, then {"done": <the object above>}, or {"error": {"code", "message", "status"}} if it fails after the stream started (status is the HTTP status the failure would have had). Closing the connection stops the work. Messages not ending with a user question are 400 (code 5, "Send messages ending with the user's question"); a failure reaching the model is 502 (code -1). usage.costUsd is there only when every model used has a known price. plans is there when the assistant planned a task of several steps: [{plan, lines}], each plan to be run with the agent routes (see Agent mode). connections is there when the assistant drafted a connection to an outside service: [{name}], one per draft, for the web client to show a card (see the connection routes below); the draft's settings and secrets are not in the answer.

<a id="assistant-post-tabularius-assistant-v1-databases-database-handover"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/assistant/v1/databases/{database}/handover`

A handover memo for whoever takes the solution over, written from the file's design alone, as a Markdown or HTML download. Given a memo in the body, it only packages that text for download.

**Permissions:** A Data API session token (Authorization: Bearer, or X-FM-Data-Access-Token) for this file, from a Data API or web client sign-in, or a scoped API token (ohbt_…) for this file allowed Data API access (fmrest). The account's privilege set needs fmrest (fmapp or fmwebdirect for a web client session), and [Full Access], because the design is read in full: any other account gets 403 (code 9). Any method but POST is 405 (code 3). Writing the memo needs the same as a question to the assistant: 503 (code 3) when the server has no API key, 403 (code 9) when AI is turned off for the file, 401 (code 9) without fmmcp, and 429 (code 3) once a daily limit or the monthly budget is used. None of that applies when the body brings its own memo.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | path | string | yes | The hosted file's name. |
| `format` | query | string | no | html for a self-contained page; anything else gives Markdown. |
| `memo` | body | string | no | A memo already written (up to 200,000 characters): it is given back as the download, and no model is called. Without it, the model writes one from the design. |
| `scripts` | body | boolean | no | true to add plain-words documentation of every script (what starts it and what it does), written by the model from the script steps with secrets hidden. Takes more model calls. |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/assistant/v1/databases/Invoices/handover?format=html
Authorization: Bearer 3f1d0c6e8a…
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "scripts": false
}
```

Response `200`:

```text
(text/html, Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="Invoices_handover.html": the memo as a page, sent with a Content-Security-Policy that allows no scripts. With Markdown it is text/markdown and Invoices_handover.md, starting "# Invoices: handover")
```

The memo is built from the design only (tables, fields, relationships, scripts, layouts, privilege sets), never from record data, and secrets are hidden before the model sees it. Closing the connection stops the work. Errors, unlike the download, are JSON {"error": {"code", "message"}}.

<a id="assistant-get-tabularius-assistant-v1-databases-database-connections-name"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/assistant/v1/databases/{database}/connections/{name}`

An AI-drafted connection for this file, as the card under the assistant's answer shows it: its settings, every place the keys would go (scheme, host and port: an OAuth 2 token address counts), which secrets are set (never their values) and the last test.

**Permissions:** A Data API session token (Authorization: Bearer, or X-FM-Data-Access-Token) for this file, from a Data API or web client sign-in, or a scoped API token (ohbt_…) for this file allowed Data API access (fmrest). The account's privilege set needs fmrest (fmapp or fmwebdirect for a web client session) as a person at the web client (sent with X-Tabularius-Client: web) and [Full Access]: a Data API sign-in, an API token (ohbt_…), an AI agent account or an account owing a password change gets 403 (code 9), as does a non-Full-Access account. Only a connection the AI drafted for this very file is reachable: any other name, a connection a person made in the console or one for other files is 404 (code 3), as is any connection of a capture-only file. allowed says whether this server lets the person finish the draft here: it is true only on a server started with --allow-app-connections.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | path | string | yes | The hosted file's name. |
| `name` | path | string | yes | The connection's name, as the assistant's answer gave it. |

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/assistant/v1/databases/Invoices/connections/invoices-bucket
Authorization: Bearer 3f1d0c6e8a…
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "allowed": true,
  "connection": {
    "name": "invoices-bucket",
    "type": "S3-compatible storage",
    "status": "draft",
    "note": "Scanned invoices",
    "settings": [
      {
        "label": "Bucket",
        "value": "acme-invoices"
      },
      {
        "label": "Region",
        "value": "us-east-1"
      }
    ],
    "reaches": [
      "https://s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com"
    ],
    "secrets": [
      {
        "name": "accessKey",
        "label": "Access key ID",
        "required": true,
        "set": false
      },
      {
        "name": "secretKey",
        "label": "Secret access key",
        "required": true,
        "set": false
      },
      {
        "name": "sessionToken",
        "label": "Session token",
        "required": false,
        "set": false
      }
    ],
    "ready": false
  }
}
```

status is draft, active or disabled; lastTest {ok, message} is there once it was tested. The steps below are refused with 403 (code 9) when allowed is false, and with 409 (code 3) once the connection is approved: later changes are the console's.

<a id="assistant-put-tabularius-assistant-v1-databases-database-connections-name-secrets-field"></a>

### `PUT /tabularius/assistant/v1/databases/{database}/connections/{name}/secrets/{field}`

Types one secret of the draft (an access key, say). It goes straight into the server's sealed store; DELETE on the same path clears it.

**Permissions:** A Data API session token (Authorization: Bearer, or X-FM-Data-Access-Token) for this file, from a Data API or web client sign-in, or a scoped API token (ohbt_…) for this file allowed Data API access (fmrest). The account's privilege set needs fmrest (fmapp or fmwebdirect for a web client session), [Full Access], an AI draft for this file, and a server started with --allow-app-connections. The same checks as the admin console: the field must be one the connection's type uses with its settings, one line of at most 4096 characters.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | path | string | yes | The hosted file's name. |
| `name` | path | string | yes | The connection's name. |
| `field` | path | string | yes | The secret's name from the connection's secrets (accessKey, secretKey, …). |
| `value` | body | string | yes | The secret, typed by the person. It is never returned, shown again or logged; the server log says only that it was set, by which account. |

**Example:**

```http
PUT /tabularius/assistant/v1/databases/Invoices/connections/invoices-bucket/secrets/accessKey
Authorization: Bearer 3f1d0c6e8a…
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "value": "(typed by the person)"
}
```

Response `200`:

```text
{"allowed": true, "connection": {…as above, with that secret set: true…}}
```

A bad field or value is 400 (code 3) with the console's message.

<a id="assistant-post-tabularius-assistant-v1-databases-database-connections-name-test"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/assistant/v1/databases/{database}/connections/{name}/test`

Signs in to the service with the draft's secrets and asks something harmless (for S3, a one-object listing), without changing anything.

**Permissions:** A Data API session token (Authorization: Bearer, or X-FM-Data-Access-Token) for this file, from a Data API or web client sign-in, or a scoped API token (ohbt_…) for this file allowed Data API access (fmrest). The account's privilege set needs fmrest (fmapp or fmwebdirect for a web client session), [Full Access], an AI draft for this file, and a server started with --allow-app-connections.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | path | string | yes | The hosted file's name. |
| `name` | path | string | yes | The connection's name. |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/assistant/v1/databases/Invoices/connections/invoices-bucket/test
Authorization: Bearer 3f1d0c6e8a…
```

Response `200`:

```text
{"allowed": true, "result": {"ok": true, "message": "Reached bucket acme-invoices; it is empty there. (210 ms)"}, "connection": {…}}
```

A failed test is still 200 with result.ok false and the reason; secrets are masked out of the message. Refused with 403 (code 9) when AI is turned off for the file.

<a id="assistant-post-tabularius-assistant-v1-databases-database-connections-name-approve"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/assistant/v1/databases/{database}/connections/{name}/approve`

A person's go-ahead: the draft becomes usable by scripts of this file, by name.

**Permissions:** A Data API session token (Authorization: Bearer, or X-FM-Data-Access-Token) for this file, from a Data API or web client sign-in, or a scoped API token (ohbt_…) for this file allowed Data API access (fmrest). The account's privilege set needs fmrest (fmapp or fmwebdirect for a web client session), [Full Access], an AI draft for this file, and a server started with --allow-app-connections. Refused with 400 (code 3) until every required secret is set (the console's check).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | path | string | yes | The hosted file's name. |
| `name` | path | string | yes | The connection's name. |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/assistant/v1/databases/Invoices/connections/invoices-bucket/approve
Authorization: Bearer 3f1d0c6e8a…
```

Response `200`:

```text
{"allowed": true, "connection": {…, "status": "active"}}
```

The server log records the approval with the account. The connection stays limited to this file; turning it off, changing it or widening its files is the admin console's.

<a id="assistant-delete-tabularius-assistant-v1-databases-database-connections-name"></a>

### `DELETE /tabularius/assistant/v1/databases/{database}/connections/{name}`

Discards the draft.

**Permissions:** A Data API session token (Authorization: Bearer, or X-FM-Data-Access-Token) for this file, from a Data API or web client sign-in, or a scoped API token (ohbt_…) for this file allowed Data API access (fmrest). The account's privilege set needs fmrest (fmapp or fmwebdirect for a web client session), [Full Access], an AI draft for this file that is not approved yet, and a server started with --allow-app-connections.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | path | string | yes | The hosted file's name. |
| `name` | path | string | yes | The connection's name. |

**Example:**

```http
DELETE /tabularius/assistant/v1/databases/Invoices/connections/invoices-bucket
Authorization: Bearer 3f1d0c6e8a…
```

Response `200`:

```json
{}
```

<a id="automations"></a>

## Automations

Automations run a script on the server when a table's records are created, changed or deleted, whoever made the change. The routes are under /tabularius/automations/v1/databases/{database}, sign in with Data API session tokens, and are for [Full Access] only. Errors come back as {"error": {"code", "message"}}: 401 (code 952) without a valid token, 403 (code 9) without [Full Access], 404 (code 401) for an unknown automation id, and 400 (code 960) for an automation that doesn't check out (no such layout, field, script or account, a formula with a problem).

Source: `packages/server/src/automations.ts`

| Method | Path | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | [`/tabularius/automations/v1/databases/{database}`](#automations-get-tabularius-automations-v1-databases-database) | Lists the file's automations, each with its trigger in words and its last 10 runs. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/automations/v1/databases/{database}`](#automations-post-tabularius-automations-v1-databases-database) | Saves a new automation (and writes its script, when one comes with it), or with ?dryRun=1 tries it once on a copy of the file instead. |
| GET | [`/tabularius/automations/v1/databases/{database}/{id}`](#automations-get-tabularius-automations-v1-databases-database-id) | One automation, with its trigger in words and its last 50 runs. |
| PUT | [`/tabularius/automations/v1/databases/{database}/{id}`](#automations-put-tabularius-automations-v1-databases-database-id) | Changes an automation: the fields sent replace its own, and the whole is checked again. |
| DELETE | [`/tabularius/automations/v1/databases/{database}/{id}`](#automations-delete-tabularius-automations-v1-databases-database-id) | Deletes an automation and its runs (its script stays). |

<a id="automations-get-tabularius-automations-v1-databases-database"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/automations/v1/databases/{database}`

Lists the file's automations, each with its trigger in words and its last 10 runs.

**Permissions:** A Data API session token (Authorization: Bearer, or X-FM-Data-Access-Token) for this file, from a Data API or web client sign-in, or a scoped API token (ohbt_…) for this file allowed Data API access (fmrest). The account's privilege set needs fmrest (fmapp or fmwebdirect for a web client session), and [Full Access].

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | path | string | yes | The hosted file's name. |

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/automations/v1/databases/Invoices
Authorization: Bearer 3f1d0c6e8a…
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "automations": [
    {
      "name": "Invoice paid",
      "enabled": true,
      "layout": "Invoices",
      "on": "update",
      "fields": [
        "Status"
      ],
      "condition": "Status = \"Paid\"",
      "script": "Mark invoice paid",
      "account": "Admin",
      "id": "3f9a1c0b7d2e",
      "created": "2026-10-12T09:15:02.114Z",
      "updated": "2026-10-12T09:15:02.114Z",
      "createdBy": "Admin",
      "trigger": "When a record in Invoices is changed, and the change is to Status, if Status = \"Paid\": run \"Mark invoice paid\" on that record (from layout Invoices) as Admin",
      "runs": [
        {
          "at": "2026-10-13T08:41:20.031Z",
          "recordId": 17,
          "outcome": "ok",
          "steps": 4
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "network": false,
  "outbound": false
}
```

network says whether the server lets scripts reach the network; outbound whether it has outbound mail settings. A run is {at, recordId, outcome (ok, error or skipped), error?, steps?, ms?, message?}.

<a id="automations-post-tabularius-automations-v1-databases-database"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/automations/v1/databases/{database}`

Saves a new automation (and writes its script, when one comes with it), or with ?dryRun=1 tries it once on a copy of the file instead.

**Permissions:** A Data API session token (Authorization: Bearer, or X-FM-Data-Access-Token) for this file, from a Data API or web client sign-in, or a scoped API token (ohbt_…) for this file allowed Data API access (fmrest). The account's privilege set needs fmrest (fmapp or fmwebdirect for a web client session), and [Full Access]. A capture-only file (outbound captureOnly) never has automations.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | path | string | yes | The hosted file's name. |
| `dryRun` | query | string | no | 1 tries the automation once on a throwaway copy of the file, offline, and saves nothing. |
| `automation` | body | object | yes | {name, description?, enabled? (default true), layout, on (create, update, createOrUpdate or delete; default update), fields?, condition?, script, parameter?, account? (default the signed-in account), network?, replace?}. replace: true overwrites an automation of the same name. |
| `script` | body | object | no | {name, text}: a script to create (or replace) with the automation; its steps are checked first. |
| `test` | body | object | no | Dry run only: field values to set on a record to set it off, e.g. {"Status": "Paid"}. |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/automations/v1/databases/Invoices
Authorization: Bearer 3f1d0c6e8a…
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "automation": {
    "name": "Invoice paid",
    "layout": "Invoices",
    "on": "update",
    "fields": [
      "Status"
    ],
    "condition": "Status = \"Paid\"",
    "script": "Mark invoice paid"
  }
}
```

Response `201`:

```json
{
  "automation": {
    "name": "Invoice paid",
    "enabled": true,
    "layout": "Invoices",
    "on": "update",
    "fields": [
      "Status"
    ],
    "condition": "Status = \"Paid\"",
    "script": "Mark invoice paid",
    "account": "Admin",
    "id": "3f9a1c0b7d2e",
    "created": "2026-10-12T09:15:02.114Z",
    "updated": "2026-10-12T09:15:02.114Z",
    "createdBy": "Admin",
    "trigger": "When a record in Invoices is changed, and the change is to Status, if Status = \"Paid\": run \"Mark invoice paid\" on that record (from layout Invoices) as Admin",
    "runs": []
  },
  "scriptChanged": false
}
```

With ?dryRun=1 the reply is 200 {automation, trigger, dryRun}, where dryRun is {recordId?, setOff?, conditionTrue?, outcome (ok, error, stalled or skipped), error?, message?, steps?, changes, outbound}: changes lists what the script changed in the copy, outbound the mail and web requests it would have made (none are sent). A file too large to copy is skipped. A name already used, without replace: true, is 400 (code 960).

```http
Authorization: Bearer 3f1d0c6e8a…
```

```json
{
  "automation": {
    "name": "Invoice paid",
    "enabled": true,
    "layout": "Invoices",
    "on": "update",
    "fields": [
      "Status"
    ],

    "runs": [
```

<a id="automations-put-tabularius-automations-v1-databases-database-id"></a>

### `PUT /tabularius/automations/v1/databases/{database}/{id}`

Changes an automation: the fields sent replace its own, and the whole is checked again.

**Permissions:** A Data API session token (Authorization: Bearer, or X-FM-Data-Access-Token) for this file, from a Data API or web client sign-in, or a scoped API token (ohbt_…) for this file allowed Data API access (fmrest). The account's privilege set needs fmrest (fmapp or fmwebdirect for a web client session), and [Full Access].

<a id="cleanup"></a>

## Data cleanup

Finds likely duplicate records, values not in a field's value list, and malformed phone numbers and email addresses on a layout, and applies the fixes and merges picked, all or none. The routes are under /tabularius/cleanup/v1/databases/{database} and sign in with Data API session tokens; everything runs as the signed-in account, so its privileges apply and every change goes in the audit log. Errors come back as {"error": {"code", "message"}}: 401 (code 952) without a valid token, 400 (code 960) for a request that can't be applied, and 403 when the account may not make a change (store error 200 or 201).

Source: `packages/server/src/cleanup.ts`

| Method | Path | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| POST | [`/tabularius/cleanup/v1/databases/{database}/scan`](#cleanup-post-tabularius-cleanup-v1-databases-database-scan) | Scans a layout's records for what looks wrong, with a suggested fix for each; changes nothing. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/cleanup/v1/databases/{database}/apply`](#cleanup-post-tabularius-cleanup-v1-databases-database-apply) | Applies fixes and merges as one batch, all or none, and journals it so it can be undone. |
| GET | [`/tabularius/cleanup/v1/databases/{database}/history`](#cleanup-get-tabularius-cleanup-v1-databases-database-history) | The batches applied to the file, newest first (up to 50). |
| POST | [`/tabularius/cleanup/v1/databases/{database}/history/{id}/undo`](#cleanup-post-tabularius-cleanup-v1-databases-database-history-id-undo) | Takes a batch back, all or none; fields changed again since are left alone and listed. |

<a id="cleanup-post-tabularius-cleanup-v1-databases-database-scan"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/cleanup/v1/databases/{database}/scan`

Scans a layout's records for what looks wrong, with a suggested fix for each; changes nothing.

**Permissions:** A Data API session token (Authorization: Bearer, or X-FM-Data-Access-Token) for this file, from a Data API or web client sign-in, or a scoped API token (ohbt_…) for this file allowed Data API access (fmrest). The account's privilege set needs fmrest (fmapp or fmwebdirect for a web client session). Only records and fields the account can see are scanned: a masked field is not compared or fixed, and an account can't merge related records through a key field it cannot read (hidden or masked).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | path | string | yes | The hosted file's name. |
| `layout` | body | string | yes | The layout whose table is scanned. |
| `checks` | body | array of string | no | Any of duplicates, valueLists, phones, emails (default all). |
| `fields` | body | array of string | no | Text or number fields to check (default every one the account can see). |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/cleanup/v1/databases/Contacts/scan
Authorization: Bearer 3f1d0c6e8a…
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "layout": "Customers"
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "layout": "Customers",
  "table": "Customers",
  "scanned": 6,
  "compared": [
    "Name",
    "Email",
    "Phone"
  ],
  "duplicates": [
    {
      "reason": "same phone (5552013344); names nearly alike",
      "score": 92,
      "records": [
        {
          "recordId": 1,
          "values": {
            "Name": "Acme Corp",
            "Email": "sales@acme.example",
            "Phone": "(555) 201-3344"
          }
        },
        {
          "recordId": 2,
          "values": {
            "Name": "ACME Corp.",
            "Email": null,
            "Phone": "555.201.3344"
          }
        }
      ],
      "keep": 1,
      "fill": {},
      "related": [
        {
          "table": "Orders",
          "via": "CustomerID = Customers::CustomerID",
          "records": 2
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "fixes": [
    {
      "check": "valueLists",
      "field": "Status",
      "from": "actve",
      "to": "Active",
      "reason": "not in the value list Statuses; looks like a typo for \"Active\"",
      "count": 1,
      "recordIds": [
        2
      ]
    },
    {
      "check": "phones",
      "field": "Phone",
      "from": "555.201.3344",
      "to": "(555) 201-3344",
      "reason": "written differently from most numbers here, which look like (000) 000-0000",
      "count": 1,
      "recordIds": [
        2
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

At most 20,000 records are scanned; notScanned counts the rest. A fix without to needs a person to decide. A field named in fields that isn't a text or number field the account can see is 400 (code 102).

<a id="cleanup-post-tabularius-cleanup-v1-databases-database-apply"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/cleanup/v1/databases/{database}/apply`

Applies fixes and merges as one batch, all or none, and journals it so it can be undone.

**Permissions:** A Data API session token (Authorization: Bearer, or X-FM-Data-Access-Token) for this file, from a Data API or web client sign-in, or a scoped API token (ohbt_…) for this file allowed Data API access (fmrest). The account's privilege set needs fmrest (fmapp or fmwebdirect for a web client session). Changes are made with the account's privileges: an account that can't edit or delete the records gets 403 and nothing is applied.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | path | string | yes | The hosted file's name. |
| `layout` | body | string | yes | The layout the scan was on. |
| `fixes` | body | array of object | no | [{field, from, to, recordIds?}]: sets from to to in the records that still have it (only those ids, when given). |
| `merges` | body | array of object | no | [{keep, remove, fill?}]: moves related records to keep, fills its empty fields from fill, then deletes remove. |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/cleanup/v1/databases/Contacts/apply
Authorization: Bearer 3f1d0c6e8a…
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "layout": "Customers",
  "fixes": [
    {
      "field": "Status",
      "from": "actve",
      "to": "Active"
    }
  ],
  "merges": [
    {
      "keep": 1,
      "remove": [
        2
      ],
      "fill": {
        "Notes": "Prefers phone"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "id": "0d4e9b2a71c3",
  "at": "2026-10-13T10:12:44.507Z",
  "account": "Admin",
  "layout": "Customers",
  "summary": "1 value fixed, 1 set of duplicates merged",
  "changes": 6,
  "fixed": 1,
  "merged": 1
}
```

At most 500 fixes and 200 merges at once. Nothing to apply, a record that is missing, or a merge that would lose related records is 400 (code 960), and nothing is changed.

<a id="cleanup-get-tabularius-cleanup-v1-databases-database-history"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/cleanup/v1/databases/{database}/history`

The batches applied to the file, newest first (up to 50).

**Permissions:** A Data API session token (Authorization: Bearer, or X-FM-Data-Access-Token) for this file, from a Data API or web client sign-in, or a scoped API token (ohbt_…) for this file allowed Data API access (fmrest). The account's privilege set needs fmrest (fmapp or fmwebdirect for a web client session).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | path | string | yes | The hosted file's name. |

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/cleanup/v1/databases/Contacts/history
Authorization: Bearer 3f1d0c6e8a…
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "history": [
    {
      "id": "0d4e9b2a71c3",
      "at": "2026-10-13T10:12:44.507Z",
      "account": "Admin",
      "layout": "Customers",
      "summary": "1 value fixed, 1 set of duplicates merged",
      "changes": 6
    }
  ]
}
```

A batch that has been undone has undone, the time it was. The history also holds bulk changes journalled elsewhere (Replace Field Contents, Replace All, Delete All Records).

<a id="cleanup-post-tabularius-cleanup-v1-databases-database-history-id-undo"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/cleanup/v1/databases/{database}/history/{id}/undo`

Takes a batch back, all or none; fields changed again since are left alone and listed.

**Permissions:** A Data API session token (Authorization: Bearer, or X-FM-Data-Access-Token) for this file, from a Data API or web client sign-in, or a scoped API token (ohbt_…) for this file allowed Data API access (fmrest). The account's privilege set needs fmrest (fmapp or fmwebdirect for a web client session). The undo is made with the account's privileges.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | path | string | yes | The hosted file's name. |
| `id` | path | string | yes | The batch's id, 12 hex characters. |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/cleanup/v1/databases/Contacts/history/0d4e9b2a71c3/undo
Authorization: Bearer 3f1d0c6e8a…
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "undone": 6,
  "skipped": []
}
```

An unknown batch ("No such cleanup") or one already undone ("Already undone") is 400 (code 960). A skipped field reads like "Customers::Status of record 4 (changed since)".

<a id="dashboards"></a>

## Dashboards

Dashboards are charts, summary tables and single numbers, each a find on a layout broken down by fields, saved in the file and worked out again each time they are read. The routes are under /tabularius/dashboards/v1/databases/{database} and sign in with Data API session tokens. Numbers are worked out as the signed-in account: records it can't view are left out, and a widget that can't be worked out carries an error. Errors come back as {"error": {"code", "message"}}: 401 (code 952) without a valid token, 404 (code 401) for an unknown id, 400 (code 960) for a dashboard that doesn't check out.

Source: `packages/server/src/dashboards.ts`

| Method | Path | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | [`/tabularius/dashboards/v1/databases/{database}`](#dashboards-get-tabularius-dashboards-v1-databases-database) | Lists the file's dashboards, by name, without their numbers. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/dashboards/v1/databases/{database}`](#dashboards-post-tabularius-dashboards-v1-databases-database) | Saves a new dashboard and returns it worked out, or with ?preview=1 works it out without saving. |
| GET | [`/tabularius/dashboards/v1/databases/{database}/{id}`](#dashboards-get-tabularius-dashboards-v1-databases-database-id) | One dashboard, with each widget worked out now as the signed-in account. |
| PUT | [`/tabularius/dashboards/v1/databases/{database}/{id}`](#dashboards-put-tabularius-dashboards-v1-databases-database-id) | Changes a dashboard's name, description or widgets and returns it worked out. |
| DELETE | [`/tabularius/dashboards/v1/databases/{database}/{id}`](#dashboards-delete-tabularius-dashboards-v1-databases-database-id) | Deletes a dashboard. |

<a id="dashboards-get-tabularius-dashboards-v1-databases-database"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/dashboards/v1/databases/{database}`

Lists the file's dashboards, by name, without their numbers.

**Permissions:** A Data API session token (Authorization: Bearer, or X-FM-Data-Access-Token) for this file, from a Data API or web client sign-in, or a scoped API token (ohbt_…) for this file allowed Data API access (fmrest). The account's privilege set needs fmrest (fmapp or fmwebdirect for a web client session). Every signed-in account sees every dashboard; canChange says whether it may change one.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | path | string | yes | The hosted file's name. |

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/dashboards/v1/databases/Invoices
Authorization: Bearer 3f1d0c6e8a…
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "dashboards": [
    {
      "id": "5be0a7c3d11f",
      "name": "Sales",
      "widgets": 1,
      "account": "Admin",
      "updated": "2026-10-12T09:10:00.000Z",
      "canChange": true
    }
  ]
}
```

widgets is the number of widgets. description is there when the dashboard has one.

<a id="dashboards-post-tabularius-dashboards-v1-databases-database"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/dashboards/v1/databases/{database}`

Saves a new dashboard and returns it worked out, or with ?preview=1 works it out without saving.

**Permissions:** A Data API session token (Authorization: Bearer, or X-FM-Data-Access-Token) for this file, from a Data API or web client sign-in, or a scoped API token (ohbt_…) for this file allowed Data API access (fmrest). The account's privilege set needs fmrest (fmapp or fmwebdirect for a web client session). Any signed-in account may make dashboards; the account is recorded as the dashboard's.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | path | string | yes | The hosted file's name. |
| `preview` | query | string | no | 1 works the widgets out and saves nothing. |
| `name` | body | string | yes | Up to 120 characters, unique in the file. |
| `description` | body | string | no | Up to 1,000 characters. |
| `widgets` | body | array of object | yes | 1 to 24 widgets: {title, kind (chart, table or number), chart? (column, bar, line, pie), layout, query? (find requests; dates may be relative, e.g. "this year"), groupBy? (a chart needs 1 or 2), by? (day, week, month, quarter, year), measure? {field, fn: count, sum, average, min, max or distinct}, top? {field, n}, limit?}. |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/dashboards/v1/databases/Invoices
Authorization: Bearer 3f1d0c6e8a…
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "Sales",
  "widgets": [
    {
      "title": "Revenue this year",
      "kind": "number",
      "layout": "Invoices",
      "query": [
        {
          "Date": "this year"
        }
      ],
      "measure": {
        "field": "Amount",
        "fn": "sum"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Response `201`:

```json
{
  "dashboard": {
    "id": "5be0a7c3d11f",
    "name": "Sales",
    "widgets": [
      {
        "title": "Revenue this year",
        "kind": "number",
        "layout": "Invoices",
        "query": [
          {
            "Date": "this year"
          }
        ],
        "measure": {
          "field": "Amount",
          "fn": "sum"
        }
      }
    ],
    "account": "Admin",
    "created": "2026-10-12T09:10:00.000Z",
    "updated": "2026-10-12T09:10:00.000Z"
  },
  "canChange": true,
  "data": [
    {
      "title": "Revenue this year",
      "kind": "number",
      "layout": "Invoices",
      "find": [
        "Find Date this year (2026-01-01...2026-12-31)"
      ],
      "grouping": "Sum of Amount",
      "foundCount": 42,
      "value": 7800
    }
  ]
}
```

With ?preview=1 the reply is 200 {name, widgets, data}. data has one entry per widget: {title, kind, chart?, layout, find, grouping, foundCount?, value? (number), categories?, series?, xTitle?, yTitle? (chart), columns?, rows? (table), top?, groupCount?, error?}. A name already used, no widgets or a chart without groupBy is 400 (code 960).

<a id="digests"></a>

## Scheduled digests

A digest works a dashboard out on a schedule, as the account that set it up, and (when the server has the AI assistant) adds a short summary written by it. Runs are kept in the file; nothing is emailed. The routes are under /tabularius/digests/v1/databases/{database} and sign in with Data API session tokens. A digest and its runs are for the account that set it up, or [Full Access]. Errors come back as {"error": {"code", "message"}}: 401 (code 952) without a valid token, 403 (code 9) for someone else's digest, 404 (code 401) for an unknown id, 400 (code 960) for a digest that doesn't check out.

Source: `packages/server/src/digests.ts`

| Method | Path | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | [`/tabularius/digests/v1/databases/{database}`](#digests-get-tabularius-digests-v1-databases-database) | Lists the file's digests with their schedule in words, next run and (for those the account may read) latest run. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/digests/v1/databases/{database}`](#digests-post-tabularius-digests-v1-databases-database) | Sets up a digest of a dashboard, run as the signed-in account. |
| GET | [`/tabularius/digests/v1/databases/{database}/{id}`](#digests-get-tabularius-digests-v1-databases-database-id) | One digest with its runs, newest first (the last 20 are kept). |
| PUT | [`/tabularius/digests/v1/databases/{database}/{id}`](#digests-put-tabularius-digests-v1-databases-database-id) | Changes a digest's name, schedule, prompt, webhook or whether it is on. |
| DELETE | [`/tabularius/digests/v1/databases/{database}/{id}`](#digests-delete-tabularius-digests-v1-databases-database-id) | Deletes a digest and its runs. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/digests/v1/databases/{database}/{id}/run`](#digests-post-tabularius-digests-v1-databases-database-id-run) | Runs a digest now and returns the run, which is kept with the others. |
| GET | [`/tabularius/digests/v1/databases/{database}/{id}/runs`](#digests-get-tabularius-digests-v1-databases-database-id-runs) | A digest's recent runs, newest first. |

<a id="digests-get-tabularius-digests-v1-databases-database"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/digests/v1/databases/{database}`

Lists the file's digests with their schedule in words, next run and (for those the account may read) latest run.

**Permissions:** A Data API session token (Authorization: Bearer, or X-FM-Data-Access-Token) for this file, from a Data API or web client sign-in, or a scoped API token (ohbt_…) for this file allowed Data API access (fmrest). The account's privilege set needs fmrest (fmapp or fmwebdirect for a web client session). Every digest is listed; last is included only on the account's own digests, or all of them for [Full Access]. Only [Full Access] sees webhook and the webhooks list.

**Parameters:**

| `database` | path | string | yes | The hosted file's name. |

**Example:**

```http

Authorization: Bearer 3f1d0c6e8a…
```

```json
      "dashboard": "5be0a7c3d11f",
      "days": [

      ],

      "prompt": "new and overdue invoices",

      "account": "Admin",
      "created": "2026-10-12T09:20:00.000Z",
      "updated": "2026-10-12T09:20:00.000Z",
      "schedule": "Mondays at 08:00",
      "dashboardName": "Sales",
      "next": "2026-10-19T08:00:00.000Z",
      "canChange": true,
      "last": {
        "id": "a1b2c3d4e5f6",
        "digest": "8c41d07e2a95",
        "at": "2026-10-13T10:02:11.402Z",
        "outcome": "ok",
        "highlights": [
          "Revenue this year: 7,800"
        ],
        "data": [
          {
            "title": "Revenue this year",
            "kind": "number",
            "layout": "Invoices",
            "find": [
              "Find Date this year (2026-01-01...2026-12-31)"
            ],
            "grouping": "Sum of Amount",
            "foundCount": 42,
            "value": 7800
          }
        ],
        "ms": 2140,
        "summaryNote": "No AI summary: the assistant is off on this server (start it with --ai)"
      }
    }
  ],
  "webhooks": [
    {
      "id": "wh_1",
      "url": "https://hooks.example.com/digest",
      "enabled": true
    }
  ]
}
```

webhooks are the admin console's webhooks for this file (never their secrets), for [Full Access] to pick one. next is left out for a digest that is turned off.

<a id="digests-post-tabularius-digests-v1-databases-database"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/digests/v1/databases/{database}`

Sets up a digest of a dashboard, run as the signed-in account.

**Permissions:** A Data API session token (Authorization: Bearer, or X-FM-Data-Access-Token) for this file, from a Data API or web client sign-in, or a scoped API token (ohbt_…) for this file allowed Data API access (fmrest). The account's privilege set needs fmrest (fmapp or fmwebdirect for a web client session), and either the account that made the dashboard or [Full Access] (403, code 9, otherwise). A webhook takes [Full Access].

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | path | string | yes | The hosted file's name. |
| `dashboard` | body | string | yes | The dashboard's id or name. |
| `name` | body | string | no | Up to 100 characters (default the dashboard's name). |

| `at` | body | string | yes | Time of day, HH:MM, in the server's local time. |
| `prompt` | body | string | no | What the summary should cover (under 2,000 characters). |
| `webhook` | body | string | no | An admin console webhook for this file to post each run to (sent only on a server started with --allow-webhooks). |
| `enabled` | body | boolean | no | Default true. |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/digests/v1/databases/Invoices
Authorization: Bearer 3f1d0c6e8a…
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "dashboard": "Z Reference digest",
  "name": "Weekly revenue",
  "days": [
    1
  ],
  "at": "23:59",
  "prompt": "new and overdue invoices"
}
```

Response `201`:

```json
{
  "digest": {
    "id": "8c41d07e2a95",

      1
```

A time that has just passed doesn't count: the first run is the next one. Bad days or at, or an unknown dashboard or webhook, is 400 (code 960).
