<a id="agent"></a>

## Agent mode

The assistant can plan a task of several steps (find records, set a field in them, make or delete records, run a script); the plan comes back from the assistant routes in plans. These routes under /tabularius/agent/v1/databases/{database} check a plan, try it, run it and take it back. A plan is {summary, layout, steps}; each step is one of {kind: "find", layout, query?}, {kind: "set", field, value}, {kind: "create", fieldData}, {kind: "delete"} or {kind: "script", script, parameter?}, each with an optional why. A plan has 1 to 20 steps and every layout, field and script in it must exist and be allowed to the signed-in account. Every route is a POST and signs in with Data API session tokens; steps run as the signed-in account, so its privileges apply to each one, offline (no network, mail or plug-ins), and every change goes in the audit log. The routes are refused with 403 (code 960) when AI is turned off for the file or a file it uses. Errors come back as {"error": {"code", "message"}}: 401 (code 952) without a valid token, 400 (code 960) for a plan or step that can't be applied (the message says why), 403 when the account may not make a change (store error 200 or 201), and 405 (code 3) for any method but POST.

Source: `packages/server/src/agent.ts`

| Method | Path | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| POST | [`/tabularius/agent/v1/databases/{database}/dry-run`](#agent-post-tabularius-agent-v1-databases-database-dry-run) | Runs every step of a plan on a throwaway copy of the file, as the signed-in account, and says what each would do; nothing is kept. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/agent/v1/databases/{database}/step`](#agent-post-tabularius-agent-v1-databases-database-step) | Runs one approved step of a plan for real, as the signed-in account, and says where the run is afterwards. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/agent/v1/databases/{database}/runs/{id}/undo`](#agent-post-tabularius-agent-v1-databases-database-runs-id-undo) | Takes a whole run back, all or none: made records removed, changed fields set back, deleted records put back. |

<a id="agent-post-tabularius-agent-v1-databases-database-dry-run"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/agent/v1/databases/{database}/dry-run`

Runs every step of a plan on a throwaway copy of the file, as the signed-in account, and says what each would do; nothing is kept.

**Permissions:** A Data API session token (Authorization: Bearer, or X-FM-Data-Access-Token) for this file, from a Data API or web client sign-in, or a scoped API token (ohbt_…) for this file allowed Data API access (fmrest). The account's privilege set needs fmrest (fmapp or fmwebdirect for a web client session). The plan is checked against the account's privileges, and the copy is worked on as that account. What a delete step reports leaves out the fields the account can't read (hidden or masked).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | path | string | yes | The hosted file's name. |
| `plan` | body | object | yes | {summary, layout, steps}, as described above. |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/agent/v1/databases/Invoices/dry-run
Authorization: Bearer 3f1d0c6e8a…
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "plan": {
    "summary": "Mark overdue invoices late",
    "layout": "Invoices",
    "steps": [
      {
        "kind": "find",
        "layout": "Invoices",
        "query": [
          {
            "Status": "Overdue"
          }
        ],
        "why": "Only the overdue ones"
      },
      {
        "kind": "set",
        "field": "Status",
        "value": "Late"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "results": [
    {
      "step": 0,
      "outcome": "ok",
      "found": 7,
      "created": 0,
      "changed": 0,
      "deleted": 0
    },
    {
      "step": 1,
      "outcome": "ok",
      "found": 7,
      "created": 0,
      "changed": 7,
      "deleted": 0,
      "records": {
        "records": [
          {
            "table": "Invoices",
            "recordId": 1042,
            "kind": "update",
            "fields": [
              {
                "field": "Status",
                "before": "Overdue",
                "after": "Late"
              }
            ]
          }
        ],
        "more": 6,
        "truncated": []
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

results has one entry per step, in order, and stops after the first step that fails (outcome "error", with a message). records lists what the step made, changed or deleted, field by field (the first 50 records; more counts the rest; truncated lists tables emptied at once), and is left out when nothing changed. A file larger than 200 MB is too large to copy: the answer is {"results": [], "skipped": "The file is larger than 200 MB, too large to copy for a dry run"}.

<a id="agent-post-tabularius-agent-v1-databases-database-step"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/agent/v1/databases/{database}/step`

Runs one approved step of a plan for real, as the signed-in account, and says where the run is afterwards.

**Permissions:** A Data API session token (Authorization: Bearer, or X-FM-Data-Access-Token) for this file, from a Data API or web client sign-in, or a scoped API token (ohbt_…) for this file allowed Data API access (fmrest). The account's privilege set needs fmrest (fmapp or fmwebdirect for a web client session). The step is made with the account's privileges; it only reaches records and fields the account can see.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | path | string | yes | The hosted file's name. |
| `plan` | body | object | yes | The whole plan, as for the dry run. |
| `step` | body | number | yes | Which step to run, counting from 0 ("No such step" otherwise). |
| `state` | body | object | no | Where the run is after the step before: the {layout, foundSet} that step answered with. Needed for every step after the first; the first starts on the plan's layout with all its records. |
| `run` | body | string | no | The run id (12 hex characters) the first step answered with, so this step's changes join that run. Leave it out on the first step. |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/agent/v1/databases/Invoices/step
Authorization: Bearer 3f1d0c6e8a…
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "plan": {
    "summary": "Mark invoices paid",
    "layout": "Invoices",
    "steps": [
      {
        "kind": "set",
        "field": "Status",
        "value": "Paid"
      }
    ]
  },
  "step": 0
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "result": {
    "step": 0,
    "outcome": "ok",
    "found": 8,
    "created": 0,
    "changed": 8,
    "deleted": 0
  },
  "state": {
    "layout": "Invoices",
    "foundSet": [
      1,
      2,
      3
    ]
  },
  "run": "7e1d4a09c3b2"
}
```

result is the same as a dry run's entry for the step. A step that fails part way still keeps what it did, so Undo takes it back (outcome "error", with a message). run is there once any step has changed something; the changes of all the steps of a run are one batch. At most 5,000 records are changed by a set step and 500 deleted by a delete step; deleting records that take related records with them is refused, as Undo could not bring those back. Script steps run offline, for at most 60 seconds. A run to add to that isn't yours, was undone, or doesn't match the plan is 400 "No such run to add to".

<a id="agent-post-tabularius-agent-v1-databases-database-runs-id-undo"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/agent/v1/databases/{database}/runs/{id}/undo`

Takes a whole run back, all or none: made records removed, changed fields set back, deleted records put back.

**Permissions:** A Data API session token (Authorization: Bearer, or X-FM-Data-Access-Token) for this file, from a Data API or web client sign-in, or a scoped API token (ohbt_…) for this file allowed Data API access (fmrest). The account's privilege set needs fmrest (fmapp or fmwebdirect for a web client session). Only the account that made the run, or a [Full Access] account, can undo it; the undo is made with the account's privileges. It needs no body.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | path | string | yes | The hosted file's name. |
| `id` | path | string | yes | The run id the step answered with, 12 hex characters. |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/agent/v1/databases/Invoices/runs/7e1d4a09c3b2/undo
Authorization: Bearer 3f1d0c6e8a…
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "undone": 3,
  "skipped": []
}
```

Fields changed again since are left alone and listed in skipped. An unknown run ("No such cleanup"), one already undone ("Already undone") and one made by another account are 400 (code 960). The run is the same kind of batch as a data cleanup's, so it also shows in that history.

<a id="inbound-hooks"></a>

## Inbound hooks

Another service (a payment provider, a form, a CI job) calls the server and a chosen script runs with the JSON it sent as Get ( ScriptParameter ). Each hook has its own address, /tabularius/hooks/v1/{id}, and its own secret; nothing else is reachable with it. Hooks are set up in the admin console (see Admin console: webhooks, inbound hooks and the outbox), which shows each one's recent calls. Calls are answered only on a server started with --allow-inbound-hooks. Every call is signed: X-Tabularius-Timestamp is the time in Unix seconds, and X-Tabularius-Signature is "sha256=" and the hex HMAC-SHA256, with the hook's secret, of the timestamp, a ".", and the body exactly as sent. A call whose time is more than five minutes from the server's clock, or one already seen, is refused, so a captured call can't be sent again. The script runs as the hook's account, within its privileges, as an automation does: offline unless the server and the hook both allow the network, no AI steps, and for at most 30 seconds. A hook that doesn't exist, is turned off, or a server with hooks off all answer the same 404 {"error": "No such hook"}.

Source: `packages/server/src/inbound-hooks.ts`

| Method | Path | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| POST | [`/tabularius/hooks/v1/{id}`](#inbound-hooks-post-tabularius-hooks-v1-id) | Calls a hook: runs its script with the body as the script parameter and answers with the script's result. |

<a id="inbound-hooks-post-tabularius-hooks-v1-id"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/hooks/v1/{id}`

Calls a hook: runs its script with the body as the script parameter and answers with the script's result.

**Permissions:** No sign-in: the signature made with the hook's secret is the credential (headers X-Tabularius-Timestamp and X-Tabularius-Signature). The script then runs as the hook's account.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | string | yes | The hook's id, as the admin console shows it. |
| `X-Tabularius-Timestamp` | header | string | yes | The current time in Unix seconds. |
| `X-Tabularius-Signature` | header | string | yes | "sha256=" and the hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<timestamp>.<body>" with the hook's secret. |
| `body` | body | object | yes | JSON of up to 256 KB. It is passed to the script, re-written without extra white space, as Get ( ScriptParameter ). |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/hooks/v1/9c2e5b7a1f40d3e816
X-Tabularius-Timestamp: 1791886800
X-Tabularius-Signature: sha256=5d41402abc4b2a76b9719d911017c592ae2f6b5c0d1e8d3a4f7b9c2e6a10d8f3
Content-Type: application/json

{"event":"payment.succeeded","invoice":"INV-1042"}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "result": "Invoice INV-1042 marked paid"
}
```

result is the script's result, cut to 10,000 characters. A script that ends with an error is still 200, with {"ok": false, "error": <error code>, "result": …}; a script that can't start or crashes is 500 {"ok": false, "error": <code>}. Refused calls: 404 (see above), 405 "Send a POST" for another method, 401 for a missing or old timestamp or a wrong signature, 409 "This call was already received", 413 over 256 KB, 400 for a body that isn't JSON, 403 for a capture-only file, 503 when the file isn't open, and 429 over the hook's calls a minute (60 unless changed, up to 6000) or for an address that sends 20 bad calls in a minute. The last 20 calls of each hook (time, status, outcome, size, sender; never the body) are in the admin console.

<a id="admin-sign-in"></a>

## Admin console: page and sign-in

The admin console is the page at /admin/ and a JSON API under /tabularius/admin/v1/. The page itself and the sign-in calls are open to everyone; every other call is let in by a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, 12 hours, renewed as it is used), the admin password set with `tabularius admin-password <folder>` sent as HTTP Basic (any user name), or the x-tabularius-local token that the running server writes to <folder>/.openhbam.local for Tabularius commands on the same machine. Until an admin password is set, only loopback requests (127.0.0.1, ::1) get in, and others get 403. Five wrong passwords from one address within 15 minutes lock that address out for 15 minutes (429 with Retry-After). A refused call gets {"error": "…", "signIn": true|false}, with a Basic challenge on 401 unless the request carries x-tabularius-console: 1 (the page's own calls). Every call that isn't GET or HEAD needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1, which a page on another site can't send.

Source: `packages/server/src/admin.ts`

| Method | Path | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | [`/admin/`](#admin-sign-in-get-admin) | The admin console page (HTML); it signs in and loads everything else from the JSON API. |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in-info`](#admin-sign-in-get-tabularius-admin-v1-sign-in-info) | What the sign-in page shows: whether an admin password is set, whether this is the server machine, and the command that sets or resets the password. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in`](#admin-sign-in-post-tabularius-admin-v1-sign-in) | Signs in to the console with the admin password and sets the tabularius_admin cookie. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/passkey-sign-in`](#admin-sign-in-post-tabularius-admin-v1-passkey-sign-in) | Signs in to the console with a passkey registered for it, in two calls: the first asks for a challenge, the second sends the passkey's answer and sets the tabularius_admin cookie. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/sign-out`](#admin-sign-in-post-tabularius-admin-v1-sign-out) | Ends the console sign-in the cookie names and clears the cookie. |

<a id="admin-sign-in-get-admin"></a>

### `GET /admin/`

The admin console page (HTML); it signs in and loads everything else from the JSON API.

**Permissions:** None: the page is only HTML, and its data needs signing in. Any method gets the page.

**Example:**

```http
GET /admin/
```

Response `200`:

```text
(the admin console's HTML page, sent with X-Frame-Options: DENY and a Content-Security-Policy)
```

GET /admin (no trailing slash) answers 301 with Location: /admin/.

<a id="admin-sign-in-get-tabularius-admin-v1-sign-in-info"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in-info`

What the sign-in page shows: whether an admin password is set, whether this is the server machine, and the command that sets or resets the password.

**Permissions:** None.

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in-info
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "passwordSet": true,
  "ai": {
    "state": "no-key"
  },
  "local": false,
  "command": "tabularius admin-password /srv/fm",
  "https": true,
  "hasPasskey": false
}
```

local is true for a request from this computer itself: a loopback address, not passed on by a proxy (no X-Forwarded-For, Forwarded or X-Real-IP), and addressed to localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1]. Only then does command name the folder; otherwise it reads `tabularius admin-password <folder>`. https is true over TLS or behind a proxy that sends X-Forwarded-Proto: https. hasPasskey is true when a passkey is registered for the console (see Admin console: accounts and passkeys), so the page can offer it. ai is only the assistant's state (connected, checking, no-key, credit-low, needs-workspace, bad-key or unreachable); its message and model are in the signed-in status.

<a id="admin-sign-in-post-tabularius-admin-v1-sign-in"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in`

Signs in to the console with the admin password and sets the tabularius_admin cookie.

**Permissions:** None, but it needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 without it) and an admin password to be set (403 "No admin password is set yet.", with the sign-in-info fields, when none is).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `password` | body | string | yes | The admin console password. |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in
x-tabularius-admin: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "password": "admin secret"
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "signedIn": true
}
```

Sets tabularius_admin=<64 hex>; Path=/; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Max-Age=43200 (plus Secure over HTTPS). A wrong password is 401 {"error": "Wrong admin password"}; the fifth miss within 15 minutes is 429 "Too many failed attempts. Try again in N seconds." with Retry-After.

<a id="admin-sign-in-post-tabularius-admin-v1-passkey-sign-in"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/passkey-sign-in`

Signs in to the console with a passkey registered for it, in two calls: the first asks for a challenge, the second sends the passkey's answer and sets the tabularius_admin cookie.

**Permissions:** None, but it needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it) and at least one registered console passkey (403 "No passkey is registered for this console yet." when there is none).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `response` | body | object | no | Left out on the first call. On the second: {credentialId, clientDataJSON, authenticatorData, signature, challenge}, the WebAuthn assertion with its fields in base64url and the challenge the first call gave. |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/passkey-sign-in
x-tabularius-admin: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "challenge": "qT9mK2vN7xLd0aWc4Hs8ZyB1eRfU3pJg5oVnCiXtMkA",
  "rpId": "fm.example.com",
  "allowCredentials": [
    "AaBbCcDdEeFfGgHhIiJjKk"
  ]
}
```

With a response the answer is 200 {"signedIn": true} and the same cookie as POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in sets. A challenge is good once, for five minutes: an unknown or old one is 401 "The sign-in has expired; try again". A passkey that isn't registered or doesn't verify is 401 with the reason, and counts as a failed attempt toward the same lockout as wrong passwords (429 with Retry-After). Any passkey registered for the console signs in, as there is one console password for everyone.

<a id="admin-sign-in-post-tabularius-admin-v1-sign-out"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-out`

Ends the console sign-in the cookie names and clears the cookie.

**Permissions:** None (it ends only the sign-in the request carries).

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-out
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "signedIn": false
}
```

Each file's pii says whether personal data is swapped for stand-ins before anything goes to AI: on is whether that applies to the file, turnedOn whether its own switch is on, and through names the hosted file whose switch applies when it is not the file's own. serverScripts is the same list as GET /tabularius/admin/v1/server-scripts. Fields with nothing to say are left out: a file's reconvert ({version, current, unsafe, unverified}) appears only when an older converter made it; certificate ({domains, expires, problem}) only with automatic HTTPS; standbys only with replication; backups.every, next, last, offsite and progressive only when those are scheduled; server.localCa ({name, fingerprint}) only with --https local. converting entries are {name, table, tablesDone, tables, records, fraction}; locked entries are {file, hint, error}.

## Admin console: script and find profiling

Timings the server keeps since it started (or since the last reset): the slowest scripts with their slowest steps, and slow finds with the indexes that would help. Sign in as for every console call; errors are {"error": "…"}.

Source: `packages/server/src/admin.ts`

| Method | Path | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/profile`](#admin-performance-get-tabularius-admin-v1-profile) | The slowest scripts by total time, each with its slowest steps. |
| DELETE | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/profile`](#admin-performance-delete-tabularius-admin-v1-profile) | Clears the script and find timings, then answers with the (now empty) report. |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/profile/finds`](#admin-performance-get-tabularius-admin-v1-profile-finds) | Finds slow enough to matter, each with the indexes to add and other hints. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/indexes`](#admin-performance-post-tabularius-admin-v1-indexes) | Adds an index on a stored field, as a slow find suggested. |

<a id="admin-files"></a>

## Admin console: files and conversion

Converting hosted files again from their .fmp12, unlocking dropped-in files that use Encryption at Rest, finding missing external container files, reading a file's conversion guide, and bringing stored calculations up to date. Sign in as for every console call; POSTs need x-tabularius-admin: 1. Errors are {"error": "…"}; a conversion that needs an encrypted .fmp12's passphrase answers 409 {"error": "this file uses Encryption at Rest: enter its passphrase", "needsPassphrase": true, "hint": "…"}, and a wrong one 400 {"error": "wrong passphrase", "needsPassphrase": true}.

Source: `packages/server/src/admin.ts`

| Method | Path | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/files/{name}/external-containers`](#admin-files-get-tabularius-admin-v1-files-name-external-containers) | Which container fields keep their files outside the file, and how many of those files are missing: the folder to bring over from FileMaker Server. |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/files/{name}/orphan-containers`](#admin-files-get-tabularius-admin-v1-files-name-orphan-containers) | Stored container data that no record refers to any more (left after records were deleted): how many, and each one's file name, external path and size. Nothing is removed. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/files/{name}/orphan-containers`](#admin-files-post-tabularius-admin-v1-files-name-orphan-containers) | Removes the unreferenced container data the GET lists, including their files stored outside the file. Only with {"purge": true} (400 otherwise); answers what was removed and what is left. |

<a id="admin-files-post-tabularius-admin-v1-files-name-reconvert"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/files/{name}/reconvert`

Converts a hosted file again from its .fmp12, carrying over the records created, edited and deleted since; the store as it was is kept beside it.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | path | string | yes | Hosted file (404 when it isn't). |
| `force` | body | boolean | no | Convert without carrying edits over (when carrying them over isn't safe). |
| `sameFile` | body | boolean | no | As for reconvert-preview. |
| `passphrase` | body | string | no | As for reconvert-preview; checked before anyone is disconnected. |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/files/Invoices/reconvert
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "stats": {
    "tables": 12,
    "records": 250000
  },
  "backup": "Invoices.openhbam.sqlite.before-reconvert-2026-10-13_082500",
  "created": 4,
  "edited": 1,
  "deleted": 0
}
```

<a id="admin-files-post-tabularius-admin-v1-reconvert-all"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/reconvert-all`

Every file an older converter made: {"preview": true} dry-runs each one; {"files": [...]} converts the named ones again.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `preview` | body | boolean | no | Dry-run every outdated file instead of converting. |
| `files` | body | array of string | no | Files to convert again; names that aren't outdated are skipped. |
| `sameFile` | body | boolean | no | As for reconvert-preview. |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/reconvert-all
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "files": [
    "Invoices"
  ]
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "files": [
    {
      "name": "Invoices",
      "stats": {
        "tables": 12,
        "records": 250000
      },
      "backup": "Invoices.openhbam.sqlite.before-reconvert-2026-10-13_082500",
      "created": 4,
      "edited": 1,
      "deleted": 0
    }
  ]
}
```

Each file is done on its own: one that fails is {"name": …, "error": "…"} in the list. A preview entry is {name, check, preview}, as reconvert-preview gives. A file whose edits can't safely be carried over is converted without them.

<a id="admin-files-post-tabularius-admin-v1-locked-file-unlock"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/locked/{file}/unlock`

Hosts a dropped-in or uploaded .fmp12 that uses Encryption at Rest: the passphrase is checked at once, then the file is converted in the background.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it). The passphrase is never logged, stored or kept once the conversion is done.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `file` | path | string | yes | The waiting file, as status.locked[].file names it (404 "<file> isn't waiting for a passphrase" otherwise). |
| `passphrase` | body | string | yes | The file's passphrase; a wrong or missing one is 400 with the reason. |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/locked/Payroll.fmp12/unlock
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "passphrase": "correct horse"
}
```

Response `202`:

```json
{
  "file": "Payroll.fmp12",
  "converting": true
}
```

<a id="admin-files-get-tabularius-admin-v1-optimization-database"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/admin/v1/optimization/{database}`

Ways to make a converted file smaller and faster, worst first: container files kept inside the file (size by field), sorts and matches no index serves, and fields, scripts, table occurrences and value lists nothing uses. Changes nothing.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | path | string | yes | Hosted file (404 "No such hosted file" when it isn't). |

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/admin/v1/optimization/Invoices
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "database": "Invoices",
  "made": "2026-10-15T01:00:00.000Z",
  "storeBytes": 27000000,
  "spaceByTable": [
    {
      "name": "_fm_containers",
      "bytes": 25000000
    }
  ],
  "containers": {
    "files": 8,
    "bytes": 22000000,
    "images": 5,
    "imageBytes": 6400000,
    "outsideFiles": 0
  },
  "findings": [
    {
      "id": "embedded-container:Assets::Photo",
      "impact": "high",
      "title": "Container files inside the file: Assets::Photo",
      "what": "8 files totalling 21.0 MB (81% of the converted file) are stored in the database itself.",
      "instead": "Move them to S3-compatible storage and keep only a link in the record.",
      "savesBytes": 22000000,
      "count": 8,
      "where": [
        "Assets::Photo"
      ],
      "actions": [
        {
          "id": "container-to-s3",
          "label": "Move these files to S3 and keep a link",
          "available": false,
          "unavailable": "Needs an S3 connection (admin console, Connections), which isn't set up yet."
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "headline": "Invoices: 1 suggestion (1 high impact), 21.0 MB of container files stored inside the file (81% of 25.7 MB)",
  "text": "# Invoices: ways to make it smaller and faster\n…"
}
```

A finding's actions say what can be done and, when it can be done now, the request that does it (an index is added with POST /tabularius/admin/v1/indexes; container files are moved with POST …/containers); none runs by itself. The response also has containerMoves, the moves made so far that can still be undone. Methods other than GET and the two POSTs below are 405.

<a id="admin-files-post-tabularius-admin-v1-optimization-database-containers"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/optimization/{database}/containers`

Moves the container files a field keeps inside the database out to managed external storage (its folder beside the hosted file), sets the field to store its files outside the file if it doesn't, and rewrites the file so it shrinks. With preview: true it only says what would happen.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | path | string | yes | Hosted file (404 "No such hosted file" when it isn't). |
| `table` | body | string | yes | Table of the container field. |
| `field` | body | string | yes | The container field. |
| `preview` | body | boolean | no | true describes the move and changes nothing. |
| `expect` | body | number | no | How many files the report said the field keeps inside the file; a different count now is 400 and nothing changes. |
| `compact` | body | boolean | no | false leaves the file as large as it was (the space is reused by later records); default true. |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/optimization/Invoices/containers
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "table": "Assets",
  "field": "Photo",
  "expect": 8
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "plan": {
    "table": "Assets",
    "field": "Photo",
    "files": 8,
    "bytes": 22100000,
    "folder": "RC_Data_FMS/Invoices/Assets/Photo/",
    "setsStorage": true,
    "preview": [
      "Move 8 files (21 MB) of Assets::Photo out of the database into the folder RC_Data_FMS/Invoices/Assets/Photo/ beside the hosted file."
    ]
  },
  "move": {
    "id": 1,
    "at": "2026-10-15T09:00:00.000Z",
    "table": "Assets",
    "field": "Photo",
    "moved": 8,
    "bytes": 22100000,
    "containerIds": [
      11,
      12,
      13,
      14,
      15,
      16,
      17,
      18
    ],
    "setStorage": true,
    "compacted": true
  }
}
```

All or nothing: a file that can't be written leaves the file and the folder as they were. A field that keeps nothing inside the file, a missing table or field, or one that isn't a container is 400 with the reason. Back up the field's folder with the file from then on.

<a id="admin-files-post-tabularius-admin-v1-optimization-database-containers-undo"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/optimization/{database}/containers/undo`

Puts the files of an earlier move back in the database (and the field's storage setting back, if the move changed it).

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | path | string | yes | Hosted file (404 "No such hosted file" when it isn't). |
| `id` | body | number | yes | The move's number, from containerMoves. |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/optimization/Invoices/containers/undo
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "id": 1
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "moved": 8,
  "bytes": 22100000,
  "missing": 0,
  "undone": 1
}
```

A file the folder has lost since stays as it was and is counted in missing (the field's storage setting is then left alone). GET …/containers lists the moves that can be undone.

<a id="admin-files-post-tabularius-admin-v1-optimization-database-fix"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/optimization/{database}/fix`

Makes one fix from the report: hides or removes the scripts, value lists or table occurrences nothing uses, or stores an unstored calculation a sort depends on. With preview: true it only lists what it would do.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | path | string | yes | Hosted file (404 "No such hosted file" when it isn't). |
| `fix` | body | string | yes | hide-scripts, remove-scripts, remove-value-lists, remove-table-occurrences or store-calculation (the id of the report's action). Anything else is 400. |
| `items` | body | string[] | no | Which ones, by name (a calculation as Table::Field). All that the report lists when left out; required for store-calculation. A name that is used now, or gone, is 409. |
| `count` | body | number | no | How many changes the person was shown. When the file has a different number now, nothing is changed and the answer is 409. |
| `preview` | body | boolean | no | true lists exactly what the fix would do, one line each, and changes nothing. |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/optimization/Invoices/fix
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "fix": "remove-value-lists",
  "count": 1
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "fix": "remove-value-lists",
  "label": "Remove 1 value list",
  "done": 1,
  "will": [
    "Remove the value list \"Colours\"."
  ],
  "undo": 1
}
```

One change: all of it is made or none. The answer's undo is the id to send to /undo. A preview answers {fix, label, count, will, undoable: true}.

<a id="admin-files-post-tabularius-admin-v1-optimization-database-undo"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/optimization/{database}/undo`

Puts a fix from the report back: the latest one not yet undone, or the one with the id the fix answered.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | path | string | yes | Hosted file (404 "No such hosted file" when it isn't). |
| `id` | body | number | no | The fix to undo; the latest not yet undone when left out. |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/optimization/Invoices/undo
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "undone": "Remove 1 value list"
}
```

Puts back exactly what the fix took out, where it was. Anything changed since is left as it is; if something now stands in the way (a script of the same name was made), nothing is undone and the answer is 409 saying why. Nothing to undo is 404; the last 20 fixes keep their undo.

<a id="admin-files-get-tabularius-admin-v1-stale-calcs"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/admin/v1/stale-calcs`

Stored calculations whose stored values differ from what their formula gives now, with examples, and the refreshes made so far. Changes nothing.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | query | string | yes | Hosted file, any case (404 "\"<name>\" is not hosted" otherwise). |
| `limit` | query | number | no | Records looked at per table (default 10,000). |

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/admin/v1/stale-calcs?database=Invoices
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "fields": [
    {
      "table": "Orders",
      "field": "Customer Total",
      "cause": "other records (ExecuteSQL)",
      "records": 1200,
      "looked": 1200,
      "stale": 1,
      "wasEmpty": 1,
      "nowEmpty": 0,
      "failing": 0,
      "recordIds": [
        1
      ],
      "examples": [
        {
          "recordId": 1,
          "stored": null,
          "now": "7"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "skipped": [],
  "looked": 1200,
  "stale": 1,
  "note": "Nothing was changed. \"other records\" and \"fields named at run time\" are expected to drift in FileMaker too; …",
  "history": []
}
```

<a id="admin-files-post-tabularius-admin-v1-stale-calcs-refresh"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/stale-calcs/refresh`

Brings the chosen stored calculations up to date, all or none, as one batch written to the audit log as "admin console".

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | body | string | yes | Hosted file, any case (404 when it isn't). |
| `fields` | body | array of object | yes | [{table, field, recordIds?}]: the fields to refresh, optionally only some records. An empty list is 400 "Nothing to refresh: pick fields". |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/stale-calcs/refresh
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "database": "Invoices",
  "fields": [
    {
      "table": "Orders",
      "field": "Customer Total"
    }
  ]
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "id": "4be1c09a2f3d",
  "at": "2026-10-13T08:31:00.000Z",
  "account": "admin console",
  "summary": "1 stored value brought up to date in Orders::Customer Total",
  "changes": 1,
  "perField": [
    {
      "table": "Orders",
      "field": "Customer Total",
      "refreshed": 1,
      "failing": 0,
      "skipped": 0
    }
  ],
  "history": [
    {
      "id": "4be1c09a2f3d",
      "at": "2026-10-13T08:31:00.000Z",
      "account": "admin console",
      "summary": "1 stored value brought up to date in Orders::Customer Total",
      "changes": 1
    }
  ]
}
```

<a id="admin-files-post-tabularius-admin-v1-stale-calcs-undo"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/stale-calcs/undo`

Undoes a refresh: puts back the values it replaced, where they haven't changed again since.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | body | string | yes | Hosted file, any case. |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/stale-calcs/undo
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "database": "Invoices",
  "id": "4be1c09a2f3d"
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "undone": 1,
  "skipped": 0,
  "history": [
    {
      "id": "4be1c09a2f3d",
      "at": "2026-10-13T08:31:00.000Z",
      "account": "admin console",
      "summary": "1 stored value brought up to date in Orders::Customer Total",
      "changes": 1,
      "undone": "2026-10-13T08:35:00.000Z"
    }
```

<a id="admin-uploads"></a>

## Admin console: uploading files to host

Hosting an .fmp12 sent from the browser: start an upload, send the file in pieces of up to 64 MB, then finish it; the server converts it in the background and hosts it. Sign in as for every console call; all but GET need x-tabularius-admin: 1. Errors are {"error": "…"} with the status the upload code gives (400, 404, 409 or 413); a method the path doesn't take is 405.

Source: `packages/server/src/admin.ts`

| Method | Path | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/uploads`](#admin-uploads-get-tabularius-admin-v1-uploads) | Uploads and their progress, newest first. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/uploads`](#admin-uploads-post-tabularius-admin-v1-uploads) | Starts an upload. |
| PUT | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/uploads/{id}`](#admin-uploads-put-tabularius-admin-v1-uploads-id) | Sends the next piece of the file as raw bytes; offset must be what has arrived so far (resending the last piece is fine). |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/uploads/{id}/finish`](#admin-uploads-post-tabularius-admin-v1-uploads-id-finish) | Every byte is there: converts and hosts the file in the background. |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/uploads/{id}`](#admin-uploads-get-tabularius-admin-v1-uploads-id) | One upload and its progress. |
| DELETE | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/uploads/{id}`](#admin-uploads-delete-tabularius-admin-v1-uploads-id) | Stops an upload in progress, or forgets a finished one. |

<a id="admin-uploads-get-tabularius-admin-v1-uploads"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/admin/v1/uploads`

Uploads and their progress, newest first.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in.

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/admin/v1/uploads
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "uploads": []
}
```

phase is uploading, waiting, converting (with progress {table, tablesDone, tables, records, fraction}), hosted, failed (with error) or locked (the file uses Encryption at Rest and waits for its passphrase: see POST /tabularius/admin/v1/locked/{file}/unlock).

<a id="admin-uploads-post-tabularius-admin-v1-uploads"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/uploads`

Starts an upload.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | body | string | yes | The file name, ending .fmp12; it is hosted under the name without it. |
| `size` | body | number | yes | The file's size in bytes; at most TABULARIUS_MAX_UPLOAD (10 GiB by default; 0 disables the per-file cap). Reserved against TABULARIUS_MAX_UPLOAD_IN_PROGRESS (20 GiB by default) across uploads and queued/running conversions; over-quota starts receive 413. |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/uploads
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "Contacts.fmp12",
  "size": 67108864
}
```

Response `201`:

```json
{
  "id": "q3ZlR8x1mT0a",
  "name": "Contacts",
  "size": 67108864,
  "received": 0,
  "phase": "uploading",
  "started": "2026-10-13T08:40:00.000Z"
}
```

400 for a name that isn't .fmp12 or can't be hosted, or a bad size; 413 over the size limit; 409 "A file named Contacts is already hosted or being uploaded" followed by what to do. Every refusal says what happened and what to do next, in words for the person dropping the file; a size of 0 is a 400 "… is empty (0 bytes)".

<a id="admin-uploads-put-tabularius-admin-v1-uploads-id"></a>

### `PUT /tabularius/admin/v1/uploads/{id}`

Sends the next piece of the file as raw bytes; offset must be what has arrived so far (resending the last piece is fine).

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | string | yes | The upload's id (404 "No such upload"). |
| `offset` | query | number | yes | Where this piece starts in the file (default 0). |

**Example:**

```http
PUT /tabularius/admin/v1/uploads/q3ZlR8x1mT0a?offset=0
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
Content-Type: application/octet-stream
Content-Length: 67108864

(the first 64 MB of the file)
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "id": "q3ZlR8x1mT0a",
  "name": "Contacts",
  "size": 67108864,
  "received": 67108864,
  "phase": "uploading",
  "started": "2026-10-13T08:40:00.000Z"
}
```

409 "Send from byte N" for an offset past what has arrived, or "This upload is complete"; 413 for a piece over 64 MB or past the file's size.

<a id="admin-uploads-post-tabularius-admin-v1-uploads-id-finish"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/uploads/{id}/finish`

Every byte is there: converts and hosts the file in the background.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | string | yes | The upload's id. |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/uploads/q3ZlR8x1mT0a/finish
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "id": "q3ZlR8x1mT0a",
  "name": "Contacts",
  "size": 67108864,
  "received": 67108864,
  "phase": "waiting",
  "started": "2026-10-13T08:40:00.000Z"
}
```

409 "Only N of M bytes have arrived" or "This upload is already finished". Poll GET /tabularius/admin/v1/uploads/{id} for the outcome.

<a id="admin-uploads-get-tabularius-admin-v1-uploads-id"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/admin/v1/uploads/{id}`

One upload and its progress.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | string | yes | The upload's id (404 "No such upload"). |

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/admin/v1/uploads/q3ZlR8x1mT0a
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "id": "q3ZlR8x1mT0a",
  "name": "Contacts",
  "size": 67108864,
  "received": 67108864,
  "phase": "waiting"
}
```

<a id="admin-uploads-delete-tabularius-admin-v1-uploads-id"></a>

### `DELETE /tabularius/admin/v1/uploads/{id}`

Stops an upload in progress, or forgets a finished one.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | string | yes | The upload's id. |
