```http
DELETE /tabularius/admin/v1/uploads/q3ZlR8x1mT0a
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
```

Response `200`:

```json
{}
```

409 "It is being converted" while it is waiting or converting.

<a id="admin-backups"></a>

## Admin console: backups and restore

Backing up now, checking and test-restoring backup sets, putting a whole file back as it was at a moment, and putting one record back as it was after an audit entry. Backup sets live in the backup folder (the scheduled backups' destination, else <folder>/Backups) and are named by time, like 2026-10-13_020000. Sign in as for every console call; POSTs need x-tabularius-admin: 1. Errors are {"error": "…"}.

Source: `packages/server/src/admin.ts`

| Method | Path | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/backups`](#admin-backups-get-tabularius-admin-v1-backups) | The backup settings and the sets there are: where they go, how many are kept, the schedule, the last backup, and each set with its size, last check and last test restore (the same as status.backups). |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/backup`](#admin-backups-post-tabularius-admin-v1-backup) | Backs up every hosted file now, keeping as many sets as the schedule (or --backup-keep) says; the new set is checked in the background. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/backup-folder`](#admin-backups-post-tabularius-admin-v1-backup-folder) | Sets the folder backups go to (an empty string goes back to <folder>/Backups). It is saved in the folder's settings, so the next start keeps it. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/backup/stop`](#admin-backups-post-tabularius-admin-v1-backup-stop) | Stops the backups that are running or waiting (Back up now and the scheduled ones). Each ends after the file it is copying; its half-made set is removed and no old set is pruned. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/backups/{set}/verify`](#admin-backups-post-tabularius-admin-v1-backups-set-verify) | Checks a backup set again now: each copy against its checksum and opened. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/backups/{set}/test-restore`](#admin-backups-post-tabularius-admin-v1-backups-set-test-restore) | Restores a set to a scratch folder and opens each file as the server would, as a test; nothing hosted is touched. |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/restore`](#admin-backups-get-tabularius-admin-v1-restore) | How far back each hosted file can be put back, from the backups and point-in-time logs. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/restore`](#admin-backups-post-tabularius-admin-v1-restore) | Puts a file back as it was at a moment while the server keeps running: in place (its users are disconnected, it is closed, restored and opened again) or as a new hosted copy beside it. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/records/restore`](#admin-backups-post-tabularius-admin-v1-records-restore) | Puts one record back as it was after an audit entry; the change is audited as "admin console". |

<a id="admin-backups-get-tabularius-admin-v1-backups"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/admin/v1/backups`

The backup settings and the sets there are: where they go, how many are kept, the schedule, the last backup, and each set with its size, last check and last test restore (the same as status.backups).

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in.

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/admin/v1/backups
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "backups": {
    "dest": "/srv/fm/Backups",
    "keep": 7,
    "encrypted": false,
    "sets": [
      {
        "name": "2026-10-13_084500",
        "bytes": 18874368
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

<a id="admin-backups-post-tabularius-admin-v1-backup"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/backup`

Backs up every hosted file now, keeping as many sets as the schedule (or --backup-keep) says; the new set is checked in the background.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/backup
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "dir": "/srv/fm/Backups/2026-10-13_084500",
  "files": [
    "Invoices.openhbam.sqlite",
    "Contacts.openhbam.sqlite"
  ],
  "removed": [
    "2026-10-06_020000"
  ]
}
```

Also starts an off-site copy when one is set up. The check's outcome shows in status.backups.sets[].check. A body naming a "database" is 400: a backup covers every hosted file, and restores depend on that. 409 {"error": "The backup was stopped"} when POST /backup/stop ended it.

<a id="admin-backups-post-tabularius-admin-v1-backup-folder"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/backup-folder`

Sets the folder backups go to (an empty string goes back to <folder>/Backups). It is saved in the folder's settings, so the next start keeps it.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `folder` | body | string | yes | A full path, made if it is not there and tested by writing to it; not the hosted folder itself (400 with the reason otherwise). |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/backup-folder
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "folder": "/Volumes/Backup/tabularius"
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "folder": "/Volumes/Backup/tabularius",
  "backupDir": "/Volumes/Backup/tabularius",
  "appliesNow": true
}
```

"appliesNow" is false when the server also keeps point-in-time backups or an off-site copy, which follow the old folder until it restarts; backupDir then still shows the old one. 409 when a backup is running, or when the server was started with --backup-dir (that one counts). status.backups.dest, saved and fixed say where backups go, what is saved, and whether --backup-dir fixes it. Sets already taken stay where they are.

<a id="admin-backups-post-tabularius-admin-v1-backup-stop"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/backup/stop`

Stops the backups that are running or waiting (Back up now and the scheduled ones). Each ends after the file it is copying; its half-made set is removed and no old set is pruned.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/backup/stop
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "stopped": 1
}
```

{"stopped": 0} when none was running. The stopped POST /backup answers 409. status.backups.running says whether one is running. The backup taken before a restore is not stoppable.

<a id="admin-backups-post-tabularius-admin-v1-backups-set-verify"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/backups/{set}/verify`

Checks a backup set again now: each copy against its checksum and opened.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `set` | path | string | yes | The set's name (404 "no such backup"). |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/backups/2026-10-13_084500/verify
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "at": "2026-10-13T08:46:00.000Z",
  "ok": true,
  "files": {
    "Invoices.openhbam.sqlite": "ok",
    "Contacts.openhbam.sqlite": "ok"
  },
  "ms": 950
}
```

<a id="admin-backups-post-tabularius-admin-v1-backups-set-test-restore"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/backups/{set}/test-restore`

Restores a set to a scratch folder and opens each file as the server would, as a test; nothing hosted is touched.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `set` | path | string | yes | The set's name (404 "no such backup"). |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/backups/2026-10-13_084500/test-restore
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "at": "2026-10-13T08:47:00.000Z",
  "ok": true,
  "files": {
    "Invoices.openhbam.sqlite": {
      "tables": 12,
      "records": 250000,
      "accounts": 6
    }
  },
  "ms": 2100
}
```

A file that couldn't be opened has a string saying why in place of its counts.

<a id="admin-backups-get-tabularius-admin-v1-restore"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/admin/v1/restore`

How far back each hosted file can be put back, from the backups and point-in-time logs.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in.

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/admin/v1/restore
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "progressive": true,
  "databases": [
    {
      "name": "Invoices",
      "status": "open",
      "from": "2026-10-06T02:00:00.000Z",
      "to": "2026-10-13T08:47:30.000Z",
      "sets": 8
    }
  ]
}
```

from, to and sets are left out for a file with no backup.

<a id="admin-backups-post-tabularius-admin-v1-restore"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/restore`

Puts a file back as it was at a moment while the server keeps running: in place (its users are disconnected, it is closed, restored and opened again) or as a new hosted copy beside it.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | body | string | yes | Hosted file, any case (404 "\"<name>\" is not hosted"). |
| `at` | body | string or number | yes | The moment: milliseconds since 1970, an ISO time with Z or an offset, or a local time like "2026-10-11 14:05" (as it was by the end of that minute). |
| `mode` | body | string | no | "replace" (default) or "copy". |
| `name` | body | string | no | With copy: the new file's name (default "<file> restored <date time>"). |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/restore
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "database": "Invoices",
  "at": "2026-10-11 14:05",
  "mode": "copy",
  "name": "Invoices before mistake"
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "database": "Invoices before mistake",
  "time": "2026-10-11T14:05:41.000Z",
  "mode": "copy"
}
```

400 for a moment that can't be read, is in the future, or has no backup before it; 409 "Another restore is under way", or "A file named … is already hosted" for a copy.

<a id="admin-backups-post-tabularius-admin-v1-records-restore"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/records/restore`

Puts one record back as it was after an audit entry; the change is audited as "admin console".

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | body | string | yes | Hosted file. |
| `table` | body | string | yes | Table name. |
| `recordId` | body | number | yes | The record's id. |
| `seq` | body | number | yes | The audit entry's seq to go back to. |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/records/restore
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "database": "Invoices",
  "table": "Invoices",
  "recordId": 1042,
  "seq": 5531
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "action": "updated",
  "fields": [
    "Status"
  ]
}
```

action is updated, created (the record had been deleted), deleted (it didn't exist yet) or unchanged. 400 "give database, table, recordId and seq" when one is missing or the file isn't hosted; a store error (no such table) is 400.

<a id="admin-security"></a>

## Admin console: audit, security review and access

A hosted file's audit log and security events, "view as" previews, plain-English access explanations and set comparisons, the security health report with its one-click fixes, least-privilege suggestions and unusual-access alerts. Also the checks that an account or SSO mapping gets the access intended (test an account, test an SSO sign-in), who-can and usage questions, an access review for audits, and the few changes the console makes itself: SSO mappings, one field's access for a privilege set, treating an imported set's unverified fields as view-only, and the two fixes. Sign in as for every console call; POSTs and DELETEs need x-tabularius-admin: 1. Most GETs take ?database= (any case); view-as, access, test-account, compare, sso-mapping, field-access, who-can, usage, health, least-privilege and unusual-access answer 200 with {"error": "…"} when the file or a name in the query isn't found (access-review answers 400, and the changes 404 or 400).

Source: `packages/server/src/admin.ts`

| Method | Path | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/audit`](#admin-security-get-tabularius-admin-v1-audit) | A file's audit log, oldest of the selection first: record changes and security events, as JSON or a CSV download. |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/audit/settings`](#admin-security-get-tabularius-admin-v1-audit-settings) | What a file's record audit log never keeps values of: fields named per table, and whether names that look like passwords, keys and card numbers are left out too; also the fields it would suggest. PUT changes them. |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/audit/verify`](#admin-security-get-tabularius-admin-v1-audit-verify) | Checks that a file's record audit log still hangs together: every entry is linked to the one before it by a hash, so one that was edited, removed from the middle, added behind the log's back or cut off the end is found. |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/security-events`](#admin-security-get-tabularius-admin-v1-security-events) | A file's security and sign-in events, each with its group, a plain-English description and a severity, as JSON or a CSV download. |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/security-events/verify`](#admin-security-get-tabularius-admin-v1-security-events-verify) | Checks the complete committed security-event chain in one read-only snapshot, without event filters or a result limit. |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/view-as`](#admin-security-get-tabularius-admin-v1-view-as) | Reads a layout as a privilege set would see it (its visible records, hidden fields left out) without giving the set to an account. Logged as a viewed-as security event. |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/access`](#admin-security-get-tabularius-admin-v1-access) | Everything an account or privilege set can open and change in a file, with a plain reason for every denial. Logged as a viewed-as security event. |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/compare`](#admin-security-get-tabularius-admin-v1-compare) | A plain-English diff of two privilege sets: the changes that would turn set a into set b. |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/health`](#admin-security-get-tabularius-admin-v1-health) | The security health report of one hosted file, or of every one: full-access accounts, accounts without a second factor, dormant accounts, broad or stale API tokens, over-sharing sets, empty passwords, the privilege review's findings, schedules whose last run failed, and scheduled syncs with records changed on both sides. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/health/revoke-token`](#admin-security-post-tabularius-admin-v1-health-revoke-token) | One-click fix: revokes one of a file's API tokens. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/health/fix-account`](#admin-security-post-tabularius-admin-v1-health-fix-account) | One-click fix for an account with an empty password: give it a temporary password it must change, or deactivate it. Answers with the fix and the new health report. |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/least-privilege`](#admin-security-get-tabularius-admin-v1-least-privilege) | Write grants (edit, create, delete) a privilege set holds on a table that no account on it has used in the window: candidates for view-only. And, in `access`, ways in (the extended privileges fmrest, fmapp, fmwebdirect, fmodata, fmxdbc, fmmcp) none of its accounts has used, from the usage counts. A way in is judged only once its use has been counted for the whole window; until then it is listed in `notYetCounted`. |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/unusual-access`](#admin-security-get-tabularius-admin-v1-unusual-access) | Unusual-access alerts from the sign-in log, worst first: failed sign-in bursts, lockouts, sign-ins from a new place, one account from many places, a dormant account waking, protections turned off. |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/test-account`](#admin-security-get-tabularius-admin-v1-test-account) | Signs in as an account on paper: every layout and script in the file as the account's privileges would meet it, including script steps that jump to a layout or script it can't reach. Nothing runs. |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/access-review`](#admin-security-get-tabularius-admin-v1-access-review) | "Who can do what" for an audit: one row per account per table, with the account's extended privileges, last sign-in and two-factor status, and plain-English findings; as JSON or a CSV download. |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/plugin-readiness`](#admin-security-get-tabularius-admin-v1-plugin-readiness) | What a hosted file's plug-in calls will do here: for each plug-in function the file calls, whether it runs, gives ?, gives an error text or goes to the Outbox, how many scripts, calculations and layout objects call it, and what to use instead; as JSON or a CSV download of function names and counts. |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/sso-mapping`](#admin-security-get-tabularius-admin-v1-sso-mapping) | Which privilege set a person signed in through an identity provider gets, by their email, their email's domain or one of their groups, and the sets to pick from. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/sso-mapping`](#admin-security-post-tabularius-admin-v1-sso-mapping) | Adds an SSO mapping, or changes the privilege set of an existing one. |
| DELETE | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/sso-mapping/{name}`](#admin-security-delete-tabularius-admin-v1-sso-mapping-name) | Removes an SSO mapping. |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/sso-mapping/test`](#admin-security-get-tabularius-admin-v1-sso-mapping-test) | Which mapping an email address and groups would resolve to, and what that mapping can do, so it can be checked before anyone signs in with it. |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/field-access`](#admin-security-get-tabularius-admin-v1-field-access) | Which fields of a table a privilege set can change, only view, see only a masked version of, or not see. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/field-access`](#admin-security-post-tabularius-admin-v1-field-access) | Sets one field's access in a privilege set. |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/who-can`](#admin-security-get-tabularius-admin-v1-who-can) | Which accounts can see, change, add to or delete from a table, or see and change one field, grouped by privilege set and said in plain words. |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/usage`](#admin-security-get-tabularius-admin-v1-usage) | What each account has done in the last days: requests by surface, days active, first and last day, and sign-ins and failed sign-ins. Counts only. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/relax-unverified`](#admin-security-post-tabularius-admin-v1-relax-unverified) | Treats as view-only the fields of an imported privilege set that the import hid because their access is only inferred to mean view-only. An explicit choice, one set at a time. |

<a id="admin-security-get-tabularius-admin-v1-audit"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/admin/v1/audit`

A file's audit log, oldest of the selection first: record changes and security events, as JSON or a CSV download.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | query | string | yes | Hosted file, any case (400 "name a hosted database with ?database=" otherwise). |
| `security` | query | boolean | no | 1 or true for security events only; 0 or false for record changes only. |
| `account` | query | string | no | Who did it. |
| `table` | query | string | no | Table name. |
| `recordId` | query | number | no | One record. |
| `surface` | query | string | no | Where record changes came from: web (the web client), rest (Data API), odata, sql, mcp, admin, automation, hook, cleanup, agent, assistant, import (rows imported or an import undone), sync (a sync run). |
| `script` | query | string | no | Record changes a script of this name made. |
| `kind` | query | string | no | create, update, delete, truncate or a security event kind (sign-in, sign-in-failed, …). |
| `since` | query | string | no | ISO time, inclusive. |
| `until` | query | string | no | ISO time, inclusive. |
| `limit` | query | number | no | The latest N entries (default 200, at most 10,000). |
| `format` | query | string | no | csv for a download (audit-<file>.csv). |

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/admin/v1/audit?database=Invoices&limit=2
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "database": "Invoices",
  "audit": [
    {
      "seq": 5530,
      "at": "2026-10-13T08:12:00.000Z",
      "account": null,
      "kind": "sign-in",
      "table": "",
      "security": true
    },
    {
      "seq": 5531,
      "at": "2026-10-13T08:14:03.000Z",
      "account": "Ann",
      "kind": "update",
      "table": "Invoices",
      "recordId": 1042,
      "changes": {
        "Status": [
          "Open",
          "Paid"
        ]
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Time filters use the first audit entry that crosses each boundary, then include or exclude entries by their increasing seq. If the host clock moves backward, later entries remain in a since window even when their at is earlier than the requested time. Until excludes those later entries after its first crossing. The returned at remains the recorded wall-clock time; use seq to order entries reliably. The CSV's columns are seq, at, account, kind, security, table, target, from, recordId, changes, surface, script, copyOf, revertOf; a value starting with =, +, - or @ gets a leading ' so a spreadsheet won't run it.

<a id="admin-security-get-tabularius-admin-v1-audit-settings"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/admin/v1/audit/settings`

What a file's record audit log never keeps values of: fields named per table, and whether names that look like passwords, keys and card numbers are left out too; also the fields it would suggest. PUT changes them.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | query | string | yes | Hosted file, any case (400 otherwise). |

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/admin/v1/audit/settings?database=Invoices
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "database": "Invoices",
  "redactSensitive": false,
  "logReads": false,
  "excludeFields": {},
  "retentionDays": 0,
  "suggested": {
    "Users": [
      "Password"
    ]
  }
}
```

PUT (with x-tabularius-admin: 1) takes logReads (true logs who reads records through the Data API, OData, SQL, the AI tools and the web client: one entry per request with the table and record ids, never values; a SQL query gets one entry for each table it names, with its row count and never its text; the AI tools that read the design, and container reads, get one entry naming the tool or the file; off by default), retentionDays (a whole number; entries older than that are removed hourly, the chain recording that they were; 0 keeps every entry), redactSensitive (true or false) and/or excludeFields ({"Table": ["Field"]}, replacing the list; 400 for a table or field that is missing). A field left out shows ‹not logged› in an entry; Undo and a revert can't put back what was not logged, so both are off until chosen.

<a id="admin-security-get-tabularius-admin-v1-audit-verify"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/admin/v1/audit/verify`

Checks that a file's record audit log still hangs together: every entry is linked to the one before it by a hash, so one that was edited, removed from the middle, added behind the log's back or cut off the end is found.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | query | string | yes | Hosted file, any case (400 otherwise). |

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/admin/v1/audit/verify?database=Invoices
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "database": "Invoices",
  "ok": true,
  "status": "consistent",
  "firstBrokenSeq": null,
  "reason": null,
  "checked": 5530,
  "legacyThroughSeq": 120,
  "head": {
    "chainSeq": 5530,
    "auditSeq": 5651,
    "hash": "9f2c…"
  },
  "pruned": null
}
```

status is consistent, broken (firstBrokenSeq and reason say where) or unprotected. 503 while another check runs. The hashes show the log is consistent, not who wrote it: keep a copy of head.hash elsewhere to notice a rewritten tail. Entries from before the chain started (legacyThroughSeq) are not covered; entries removed by the retention setting show as pruned.

<a id="admin-security-get-tabularius-admin-v1-security-events-verify"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/admin/v1/security-events/verify`

Checks the complete committed security-event chain in one read-only snapshot, without event filters or a result limit.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | query | string | yes | Hosted file, any case (400 otherwise). |

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/admin/v1/security-events/verify?database=Invoices
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "database": "Invoices",
  "ok": true,
  "status": "consistent",
  "firstBrokenSeq": null,
  "reason": null,
  "checked": 10,
  "legacyThroughSeq": "0",
  "head": {
    "chainSeq": "10",
    "auditSeq": "12",
    "hash": "aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa"
  }
}
```

Runs in a worker, at most one verification at a time per serving process; another request gets 503 and can retry. The worker has a 60-second deadline and is terminated on timeout, client disconnect or server shutdown; its slot is released only after it stops. A timeout answers 500 with an error, not a consistency result. A broken chain still answers 200 with ok=false, status=broken, firstBrokenSeq and reason. Sequence ids are decimal strings; firstBrokenSeq is the first failing retained row, or the expected head for a missing tail, and is null for a metadata failure. Missing chain metadata reports unprotected. The legacy baseline protects consistency from migration onward, not earlier authenticity. Consistent proves neither authenticity nor completeness: a database writer can recompute history and the head, shorten history and rewrite the head, or restore an older valid database. No external checkpoint is checked; stronger historical guarantees require independently protected checkpoints and cover only the checkpointed history.

<a id="admin-security-get-tabularius-admin-v1-least-privilege"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/admin/v1/least-privilege`

Write grants (edit, create, delete) a privilege set holds on a table that no account on it has used in the window: candidates for view-only. And, in `access`, ways in (the extended privileges fmrest, fmapp, fmwebdirect, fmodata, fmxdbc, fmmcp) none of its accounts has used, from the usage counts. A way in is judged only once its use has been counted for the whole window; until then it is listed in `notYetCounted`.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | query | string | yes | Hosted file, any case. |
| `unusedDays` | query | number | no | The window in days (default 30, at most 36,500). |

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/admin/v1/least-privilege?database=Invoices&unusedDays=45
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "database": "Invoices",
  "unusedDays": 45,
  "findings": [
    {
      "set": "Sales",
      "table": "Products",
      "grants": [
        "edit",
        "delete"
      ],
      "accounts": [
        "seller"
      ],
      "description": "Sales can edit and delete Products records, but no account on it has in 45 days"
    }
  ],
  "access": [
    {
      "set": "Sales",
      "privilege": "fmodata",
      "what": "OData",
      "accounts": [
        "seller"
      ],
      "description": "\"Sales\" lets its accounts in through OData (fmodata), but none of them has used it in 45 days. Consider taking fmodata off the set."
    }
  ],
  "notYetCounted": [
    "fmxdbc"
  ]
}
```
