**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/admin/v1/unusual-access?database=Invoices
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "database": "Invoices",
  "windowHours": 72,
  "alerts": [
    {
      "kind": "failed-burst",
      "severity": "alert",
      "account": "Ann",
      "from": "203.0.113.9",
      "at": "2026-10-13T03:12:00.000Z",
      "count": 6,
      "description": "6 failed sign-ins for Ann from 203.0.113.9",
      "seqs": [
        5501,
        5502,
        5503,
        5504,
        5505,
        5506
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

<a id="admin-security-get-tabularius-admin-v1-test-account"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/admin/v1/test-account`

Signs in as an account on paper: every layout and script in the file as the account's privileges would meet it, including script steps that jump to a layout or script it can't reach. Nothing runs.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Logged as a viewed-as security event.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | query | string | yes | Hosted file, any case. |
| `account` | query | string | no | The account to test. Without it the answer is {database, accounts} for the picker. |

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/admin/v1/test-account?database=Invoices&account=seller
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "database": "Invoices",
  "account": "seller",
  "privilegeSet": "Sales",
  "layouts": [
    {
      "layout": "Invoice Entry",
      "access": "modifiable",
      "records": "modifiable"
    },
    {
      "layout": "Payroll",
      "access": "none",
      "records": "none"
    }
  ],
  "scripts": [
    {
      "script": "Post Invoice",
      "access": "viewOnly",
      "blocked": [
        {
          "line": 4,
          "step": "Go to Layout",
          "target": "layout",
          "name": "Payroll"
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "script": "Update Totals",
      "access": "none",
      "blocked": []
    }
  ]
}
```

A script the account may run (access other than none) lists in blocked the Go to Layout, Perform Script, Perform Script on Server and Install OnTimer Script steps (by 1-based line) whose layout or script the account can't use; a script it can't run has none listed. It does not follow into the script a step performs: that script has its own entry. An unknown account is {"error": "No account \"…\""}.

<a id="admin-security-get-tabularius-admin-v1-access-review"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/admin/v1/access-review`

"Who can do what" for an audit: one row per account per table, with the account's extended privileges, last sign-in and two-factor status, and plain-English findings; as JSON or a CSV download.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | query | string | yes | Hosted file, any case (400 "name a hosted database with ?database=" otherwise). |
| `unusedDays` | query | number | no | An account that has not signed in for this many days is stale (default 90). |
| `format` | query | string | no | csv for a download (access-review-<file>.csv). |

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/admin/v1/access-review?database=Invoices&unusedDays=60
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "database": "Invoices",
  "unusedDays": 60,
  "rows": [
    {
      "account": "Admin",
      "privilegeSet": "[Full Access]",
      "fullAccess": true,
      "table": "*",
      "view": "yes",
      "edit": "yes",
      "create": "yes",
      "delete": "yes",
      "hiddenFields": 0,
      "viewOnlyFields": 0,
      "maskedFields": 0,
      "extendedPrivileges": [
        "fmrest",
        "fmapp"
      ],
      "lastSignIn": "2026-10-13T08:00:00.000Z",
      "daysSinceSignIn": 0,
      "stale": false,
      "has2fa": true
    },
    {
      "account": "seller",
      "privilegeSet": "Sales",
      "fullAccess": false,
      "table": "Invoices",
      "view": "yes",
      "edit": "limited",
      "create": "yes",
      "delete": "no",
      "hiddenFields": 1,
      "viewOnlyFields": 0,
      "maskedFields": 0,
      "extendedPrivileges": [
        "fmrest"
      ],
      "stale": true,
      "has2fa": false
    }
  ],
  "summary": [
    "1 account has full access: Admin.",
    "1 account has no second factor: seller."
  ]
}
```

A full-access account has one summary row with table "*"; an account with no privilege set has one too, with everything "no". view, edit and delete are yes, limited (by a record rule) or no. maskedFields counts the fields the account sees only a stand-in for (not included in hiddenFields); the CSV has a maskedFields column after viewOnlyFields. lastSignIn and daysSinceSignIn are left out for an account that never signed in, which is stale. Inactive accounts are left out. The CSV has a row per line of rows.

<a id="admin-security-get-tabularius-admin-v1-plugin-readiness"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/admin/v1/plugin-readiness`

What a hosted file's plug-in calls will do here: for each plug-in function the file calls, whether it runs, gives ?, gives an error text or goes to the Outbox, how many scripts, calculations and layout objects call it, and what to use instead; as JSON or a CSV download of function names and counts.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | query | string | yes | Hosted file, any case (400 "name a hosted database with ?database=" otherwise). |
| `format` | query | string | no | csv for a download (plug-ins-<file>.csv). |

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/admin/v1/plugin-readiness?database=Invoices
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "database": "Invoices",
  "line": "1 plug-in function will not run",
  "willNotRun": 1,
  "running": 1,
  "cannotTell": 0,
  "summary": "",
  "functions": [
    {
      "plugIn": "BaseElements",
      "call": "BE_ExecuteSystemCommand",
      "behaviour": "refused",
      "runs": false,
      "what": "Gives ? and error 3. It would reach the clipboard, a file picker, a shell command or FTP, which Tabularius never touches on a server.",
      "instead": "No native step runs a shell command, and Tabularius never does. Move the work into a scheduled script or outside the solution.",
      "scripts": 1,
      "calculations": 0,
      "layouts": 0,
      "other": 0,
      "guide": "/docs/moving-a-solution#plug-ins-are-not-loaded"
    },
    {
      "plugIn": "BaseElements",
      "call": "BE_Version",
      "behaviour": "runs",
      "runs": true,
      "what": "Runs here: Tabularius has its own version, so it works without the plug-in.",
      "instead": "Nothing: drop the \"is the plug-in installed\" check.",
      "scripts": 1,
      "calculations": 0,
      "layouts": 0,
      "other": 0,
      "guide": "/docs/moving-a-solution#plug-ins-are-not-loaded"
    }
  ],
  "guides": [
    {
      "title": "Moving a solution off its plug-ins",
      "href": "/docs/moving-a-solution#plug-ins-are-not-loaded"
    },
    {
      "title": "Which plug-in functions run",
      "href": "/docs/plugin-compatibility"
    }
  ]
}
```

behaviour is runs (Tabularius has its own version, or a plug-in written for Tabularius and turned on for the file supplies it), outbox (inside a script, with the server started with --test-outbound, the request or message is written to the Outbox or the call answers empty; in a calculation, or without test mode, ? and error 3), refused (always ? and error 3: the clipboard, file pickers, shell commands, FTP, opening a file or address on a desktop), unavailable (? as FileMaker gives for a plug-in that is not installed), unrecognised (no function has that name, so a calculation fails with "The function … cannot be found"), mbs-error (an MBS name Tabularius has no version of gives an MBS error text), cannot-tell (an MBS call whose function is named while the calculation runs) or off (a built-in pack turned off for the file). The list is the migration plan's, from the same function tables the engine uses; functions of plug-ins Tabularius does not know by name are not listed. It names functions and counts places (scripts, field and custom-function calculations, layout objects; each place once however often it calls the function) and reads no records; the CSV has the same rows without any script, layout or field names. Like every console call it needs the admin sign-in: an account of the file, whatever its privilege set, cannot read it.

<a id="admin-security-get-tabularius-admin-v1-sso-mapping"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/admin/v1/sso-mapping`

Which privilege set a person signed in through an identity provider gets, by their email, their email's domain or one of their groups, and the sets to pick from.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | query | string | yes | Hosted file, any case. |

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/admin/v1/sso-mapping?database=Invoices
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "database": "Invoices",
  "mappings": [
    {
      "name": "sales-team",
      "privilegeSet": "Sales"
    },
    {
      "name": "@example.com",
      "privilegeSet": "Read Only"
    }
  ],
  "privilegeSets": [
    "[Full Access]",
    "Sales",
    "Read Only"
  ]
}
```

A mapping is an external account: its name is a group, an email address or a domain written "@example.com". Inactive ones are left out.

<a id="admin-security-post-tabularius-admin-v1-sso-mapping"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sso-mapping`

Adds an SSO mapping, or changes the privilege set of an existing one.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | body | string | yes | Hosted file, any case (404 "<name> is not hosted"). |
| `name` | body | string | yes | A group, an email address or "@domain" (400 "name a group, an email address, or \"@domain\"" when empty). |
| `privilegeSet` | body | string | yes | The set people matching it get (400 "No privilege set …" when there is none). |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sso-mapping
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "database": "Invoices",
  "name": "sales-team",
  "privilegeSet": "Sales"
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "ok": true
}
```

A name that is already an account with a password is refused (400 "… is an account with a password, not an external account"). The change is written to the server's log.

<a id="admin-security-delete-tabularius-admin-v1-sso-mapping-name"></a>

### `DELETE /tabularius/admin/v1/sso-mapping/{name}`

Removes an SSO mapping.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | path | string | yes | The mapping's name, URL-encoded ("@example.com" is %40example.com). |
| `database` | query | string | yes | Hosted file, any case (404 "<name> is not hosted"). |

**Example:**

```http
DELETE /tabularius/admin/v1/sso-mapping/sales-team?database=Invoices
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "removed": true
}
```

Only SSO mappings: a name that is not an external account (an unmapped name, or a password account that happens to share it) is 400 "<name> is not an SSO mapping in <file>".

<a id="admin-security-get-tabularius-admin-v1-sso-mapping-test"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/admin/v1/sso-mapping/test`

Which mapping an email address and groups would resolve to, and what that mapping can do, so it can be checked before anyone signs in with it.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Logged as a viewed-as security event when a mapping matches.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | query | string | yes | Hosted file, any case. |
| `email` | query | string | no | The person's email address. |
| `groups` | query | string | no | Their groups, separated by commas. |

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/admin/v1/sso-mapping/test?database=Invoices&email=ann@example.com&groups=sales-team
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "database": "Invoices",
  "matched": false
}
```

The email address is tried first, then its domain, then each group in the order given. With neither email nor groups the answer is just {database}; with no match {database, matched: false}. explanation is the same as GET /tabularius/admin/v1/access gives.

<a id="admin-security-get-tabularius-admin-v1-field-access"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/admin/v1/field-access`

Which fields of a table a privilege set can change, only view, see only a masked version of, or not see.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | query | string | yes | Hosted file, any case. |
| `privilegeSet` | query | string | no | The set. Without it or table the answer is {database, privilegeSets, tables} for the pickers. |
| `table` | query | string | no | The table. |

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/admin/v1/field-access?database=Invoices&privilegeSet=Sales&table=Invoices
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "database": "Invoices",
  "privilegeSet": "Sales",
  "table": "Invoices",
  "canView": true,
  "fields": [
    {
      "name": "Number",
      "access": "modifiable"
    },
    {
      "name": "Total",
      "access": "viewOnly"
    },
    {
      "name": "Cost",
      "access": "none"
    },
    {
      "name": "Tax Id",
      "access": "masked",
      "mask": {
        "kind": "last4"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

access is modifiable, viewOnly, masked or none. A masked field also carries its mask: {kind: "last4"} (the last four characters) or {kind: "placeholder", text?} (a fixed text), and is not reported as none. [Full Access] is {database, privilegeSet, table, fullAccess: true, fields: []}. An unknown set or table is {"error": "No privilege set \"…\""} or {"error": "No table \"…\""}.

<a id="admin-security-post-tabularius-admin-v1-field-access"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/field-access`

Sets one field's access in a privilege set.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | body | string | yes | Hosted file, any case (404 "<name> is not hosted"). |
| `privilegeSet` | body | string | yes | The set (400 "No privilege set …"; [Full Access] is refused, as it always sees and changes every field). |
| `table` | body | string | yes | The table. |
| `field` | body | string | yes | The field (400 "No field \"Table::Field\"" when there is none). |
| `access` | body | string | yes | modifiable, viewOnly, masked or none (400 otherwise). masked shows the account only a stand-in: it can't be changed, searched, sorted, totalled or exported. |
| `mask` | body | object | no | {kind: "last4" \| "placeholder", text?}, for access masked (400 for another kind). A masked field with no mask shows its last four characters; re-saving it as masked without a mask keeps its mask, and naming only the same kind keeps its text. Any other access drops the mask. |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/field-access
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "database": "Invoices",
  "privilegeSet": "Sales",
  "table": "Invoices",
  "field": "Total",
  "access": "viewOnly"
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "access": "viewOnly",
  "mask": null
}
```

access in the answer is what the set now has for the field, and mask its mask (null unless masked). Setting modifiable on a table whose fields are not hidden by default removes the field's own entry rather than adding one. The change is written to the server's log.

<a id="admin-security-get-tabularius-admin-v1-who-can"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/admin/v1/who-can`

Which accounts can see, change, add to or delete from a table, or see and change one field, grouped by privilege set and said in plain words.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | query | string | yes | Hosted file, any case. |
| `table` | query | string | yes | The table, any case. |
| `field` | query | string | no | A field of the table: the answer is about that field alone. |

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/admin/v1/who-can?database=Invoices&table=Invoices
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "database": "Invoices",
  "table": "Invoices",
  "sets": [
    {
      "privilegeSet": "Sales",
      "accounts": [
        "ann",
        "bob"
      ],
      "view": "all records",
      "edit": "some records",
      "create": "yes",
      "delete": "no",
      "hiddenFields": [
        "Cost"
      ],
      "readOnlyFields": [
        "Total"
      ],
      "maskedFields": [],
      "says": "Sales (ann, bob) can see all records, change some records, add new ones and not delete; cannot see Cost."
    }
  ],
  "canSee": [
    "ann",
    "bob"
  ],
  "summary": "2 of 3 active accounts can see Invoices. Sales (ann, bob) can see all records, change some records, add new ones and not delete; cannot see Cost."
}
```

view, edit and delete are "all records", "some records" (a record rule limits them) or "no". Only active accounts with a privilege set are counted. With field, a set that sees only a masked version of it has masked: true and says "can see all records but only a masked version of Invoices::Cost"; its accounts are listed in canSeeMasked, not canSee, and the summary counts them apart. maskedFields lists a set's masked fields. It shows names only, never a record's values. An unknown table or field is {"error": "No table named \"…\""} or {"error": "No field \"…\" in …"}.

<a id="admin-security-get-tabularius-admin-v1-usage"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/admin/v1/usage`

What each account has done in the last days: requests by surface, days active, first and last day, and sign-ins and failed sign-ins. Counts only.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | query | string | yes | Hosted file, any case. |
| `days` | query | number | no | How many days back, from 1 to 400 (default 30). |

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/admin/v1/usage?database=Invoices&days=30
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "database": "Invoices",
  "days": 30,
  "accounts": [
    {
      "account": "ann",
      "requests": 1840,
      "bySurface": {
        "odata": 1,
        "rest": 1,
        "sql": 1
      },
      "daysActive": 19,
      "firstDay": "2026-09-15",
      "lastDay": "2026-10-13",
      "signIns": 22,
      "failedSignIns": 1
    },
    {
      "account": "bob",
      "requests": 0,
      "bySurface": {},
      "daysActive": 0,
      "signIns": 0,
      "failedSignIns": 0
    }
  ]
}
```

Every account in the file is listed, those that did nothing with zero requests, so unused accounts stand out; busiest first. firstDay and lastDay are left out when there were no requests. Sign-in counts come from the audit log.

<a id="admin-security-post-tabularius-admin-v1-relax-unverified"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/relax-unverified`

Treats as view-only the fields of an imported privilege set that the import hid because their access is only inferred to mean view-only. An explicit choice, one set at a time.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | body | string | yes | Hosted file (404 "name a hosted database in {\"database\": ...}" when it isn't). |
| `privilegeSet` | body | string | yes | The set (400 "name the set in {\"privilegeSet\": ...}" when missing, "No privilege set …" when unknown). |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/relax-unverified
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "database": "Invoices",
  "privilegeSet": "Sales"
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "database": "Invoices",
  "privilegeSet": "Sales",
  "relaxed": 3
}
```

relaxed is how many fields became view-only; 0 when the set has none of that kind.

<a id="admin-accounts"></a>

## Admin console: accounts and passkeys

Getting an account back in without Terminal access to the server (a password for any account, lifting a lockout, passwords for every account still on its FileMaker password, letting empty-password accounts in from the LAN), and the passkeys that sign in to the console itself (see POST /tabularius/admin/v1/passkey-sign-in under Admin console: page and sign-in). Sign in as for every console call; POSTs and DELETEs need x-tabularius-admin: 1. Errors are {"error": "…"}: a file that isn't hosted is 404 "<name> is not hosted", and an account or value that can't be used is 400 with the reason. The console has one password for everyone, so a passkey is not tied to a person: any registered passkey signs in.

Source: `packages/server/src/admin.ts`

| Method | Path | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/passkeys`](#admin-accounts-get-tabularius-admin-v1-passkeys) | The passkeys registered for the console, newest first. Never the key material. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/passkeys/register/options`](#admin-accounts-post-tabularius-admin-v1-passkeys-register-options) | Starts registering a passkey for the console: a one-time challenge, good for five minutes. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/passkeys/register`](#admin-accounts-post-tabularius-admin-v1-passkeys-register) | Finishes registering a passkey: checks the browser's answer against the challenge and stores the new passkey. |
| DELETE | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/passkeys/{id}`](#admin-accounts-delete-tabularius-admin-v1-passkeys-id) | Removes a console passkey. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/accounts/set-password`](#admin-accounts-post-tabularius-admin-v1-accounts-set-password) | Sets a password for any existing account of a file, for an account that can't sign in to use Manage Security itself (such as a converted file's account whose FileMaker password couldn't carry over). |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/accounts/unlock`](#admin-accounts-post-tabularius-admin-v1-accounts-unlock) | Lifts a sign-in lockout on an account, from every place it was blocked, or the block on an address. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/accounts/migrate-all`](#admin-accounts-post-tabularius-admin-v1-accounts-migrate-all) | Gives every account still on its FileMaker password (blank or not) a random temporary password, which it must change at its next sign-in. Account names and privilege sets stay as they are. |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/accounts/blank-password-lan`](#admin-accounts-get-tabularius-admin-v1-accounts-blank-password-lan) | Whether the file lets an account with an empty password sign in from this LAN, and not only from this computer. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/accounts/blank-password-lan`](#admin-accounts-post-tabularius-admin-v1-accounts-blank-password-lan) | Turns that LAN opt-in on or off for a file; a stopgap until every such account has a real password. |

<a id="admin-accounts-get-tabularius-admin-v1-passkeys"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/admin/v1/passkeys`

The passkeys registered for the console, newest first. Never the key material.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in.

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/admin/v1/passkeys
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "passkeys": [
    {
      "id": "AaBbCcDdEeFfGgHhIiJjKk",
      "label": "Office laptop",
      "created": "2026-10-01T09:30:00.000Z",
      "lastUsed": "2026-10-13T07:55:00.000Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

id is the credential id (base64url). label and lastUsed are left out when there are none.

<a id="admin-accounts-post-tabularius-admin-v1-passkeys-register-options"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/passkeys/register/options`

Starts registering a passkey for the console: a one-time challenge, good for five minutes.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/passkeys/register/options
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "challenge": "qT9mK2vN7xLd0aWc4Hs8ZyB1eRfU3pJg5oVnCiXtMkA",
  "rpId": "fm.example.com",
  "excludeCredentials": [
    "AaBbCcDdEeFfGgHhIiJjKk"
  ]
}
```

rpId is the host name the page was reached by (the passkey only works there); excludeCredentials lists the ids already registered, so the same device isn't added twice.

<a id="admin-accounts-post-tabularius-admin-v1-passkeys-register"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/passkeys/register`

Finishes registering a passkey: checks the browser's answer against the challenge and stores the new passkey.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `response` | body | object | yes | {attestationObject, clientDataJSON, challenge}: the WebAuthn registration with its fields in base64url, and the challenge from register/options. |
| `label` | body | string | no | A name to tell the passkey by. |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/passkeys/register
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "response": {
    "attestationObject": "o2NmbXRkbm9uZQ…",
    "clientDataJSON": "eyJ0eXBlIjoid2ViYXV0aG4uY3JlYXRl…",
    "challenge": "qT9mK2vN7xLd0aWc4Hs8ZyB1eRfU3pJg5oVnCiXtMkA"
  },
  "label": "Office laptop"
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "id": "AaBbCcDdEeFfGgHhIiJjKk"
}
```

A challenge that was not issued or is older than five minutes is 400 "The registration has expired; start again". A registration that doesn't verify is 400 "The passkey could not be registered: …".

<a id="admin-accounts-delete-tabularius-admin-v1-passkeys-id"></a>

### `DELETE /tabularius/admin/v1/passkeys/{id}`

Removes a console passkey.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | string | yes | The passkey's credential id. |

**Example:**

```http
DELETE /tabularius/admin/v1/passkeys/AaBbCcDdEeFfGgHhIiJjKk
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "removed": true
}
```

removed is false (still 200) when there is no such passkey.

<a id="admin-accounts-post-tabularius-admin-v1-accounts-set-password"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/accounts/set-password`

Sets a password for any existing account of a file, for an account that can't sign in to use Manage Security itself (such as a converted file's account whose FileMaker password couldn't carry over).

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | body | string | yes | Hosted file, any case. |
| `account` | body | string | yes | An account of the file, any case (400 "No account …" when there is none; this route never makes a new one). |
| `password` | body | string | yes | The new password (400 "password is required" when empty, or when it is shorter than the file's minimum length). |
| `mustChange` | body | boolean | no | true makes the account choose its own password at its next sign-in. |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/accounts/set-password
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "database": "Invoices",
  "account": "seller",
  "password": "a long new password",
  "mustChange": true
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "ok": true
}
```

Every session the account had signed in on the old password is ended. The change is written to the server's log, never the password.

<a id="admin-accounts-post-tabularius-admin-v1-accounts-unlock"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/accounts/unlock`

Lifts a sign-in lockout on an account, from every place it was blocked, or the block on an address.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | body | string | yes | Hosted file, any case. |
| `account` | body | string | no | An account of the file (400 "No account …" when there is none). Required unless address is given. |
| `address` | body | string | no | A client address blocked after 30 failed sign-ins across account names; given without account, lifts that block. |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/accounts/unlock
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "database": "Invoices",
  "account": "seller"
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "ok": true
}
```

For when the password is right and only the lockout is in the way.

<a id="admin-accounts-post-tabularius-admin-v1-accounts-migrate-all"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/accounts/migrate-all`

Gives every account still on its FileMaker password (blank or not) a random temporary password, which it must change at its next sign-in. Account names and privilege sets stay as they are.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | body | string | yes | Hosted file, any case. |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/accounts/migrate-all
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "database": "Invoices"
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "migrated": [
    {
      "account": "Admin",
      "password": "Xk4-7Qm-Lp2-9Zt"
    }
  ],
  "health": {
    "unusedDays": 90,
    "fullAccess": {
      "count": 1,
      "accounts": [
        "Admin"
      ]
    },
    "without2fa": [
      "Admin"
    ],
    "unused": [],
    "broadTokens": [],
    "staleTokens": [],
    "oversharingSets": [],
    "orphanedAccessKeys": [],
    "leakyStoredCalcs": [],
    "emptyPassword": [],
    "blankPasswordFromNetwork": false
  }
}
```

This answer is the only time the passwords are shown: they are not stored or logged in clear. migrated is empty when no account is waiting, and health is the file's new security health report (see POST /tabularius/admin/v1/health/fix-account). The account list a file needs this for is in its conversion report and its security health.

<a id="admin-accounts-get-tabularius-admin-v1-accounts-blank-password-lan"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/admin/v1/accounts/blank-password-lan`

Whether the file lets an account with an empty password sign in from this LAN, and not only from this computer.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | query | string | yes | Hosted file, any case. |

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/admin/v1/accounts/blank-password-lan?database=Invoices
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "database": "Invoices",
  "on": false
}
```

Off by default. The server's --allow-blank-passwords still allows it from anywhere and takes priority when it is set.

<a id="admin-accounts-post-tabularius-admin-v1-accounts-blank-password-lan"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/accounts/blank-password-lan`

Turns that LAN opt-in on or off for a file; a stopgap until every such account has a real password.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | body | string | yes | Hosted file, any case. |
| `on` | body | boolean | yes | true to allow, false (or left out) to limit them to this computer again. |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/accounts/blank-password-lan
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "database": "Invoices",
  "on": true
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "database": "Invoices",
  "on": true
}
```

The change is written to the server's log.

<a id="admin-sessions"></a>

## Admin console: sessions and connected clients

Who is signed in (web client and Data API sessions), signing sessions out, and showing a message to connected web clients. Sign in as for every console call; POSTs need x-tabularius-admin: 1. A client's id is the 12-character id that GET /tabularius/admin/v1/sessions and the status page list. Errors are {"error": "…"}.

Source: `packages/server/src/admin.ts`

| Method | Path | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/sessions`](#admin-sessions-get-tabularius-admin-v1-sessions) | Who is signed in: account, file, where from, device, how long idle. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/sessions/end`](#admin-sessions-post-tabularius-admin-v1-sessions-end) | Signs out one session by id, or every session of one account on a file. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/clients/{id}/disconnect`](#admin-sessions-post-tabularius-admin-v1-clients-id-disconnect) | Ends a session, releasing the records it was editing. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/clients/{id}/message`](#admin-sessions-post-tabularius-admin-v1-clients-id-message) | Shows a message to one connected web client. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/message`](#admin-sessions-post-tabularius-admin-v1-message) | Shows a message to every connected web client. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/block-new-users`](#admin-sessions-post-tabularius-admin-v1-block-new-users) | Blocks new users, or lets them in again: no new session starts while those already open carry on. The status's server.blockNewUsers says which. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/session-timeout`](#admin-sessions-post-tabularius-admin-v1-session-timeout) | Sets how many minutes a Data API session, and separately a web client session, may sit idle before it ends. The status's server.sessionIdleMinutes (the Data API, 15 by default) and server.webSessionIdleMinutes (the web client, which follows the Data API's value until it is given its own) say what they are now. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/responsive`](#admin-sessions-post-tabularius-admin-v1-responsive) | Sets the window width, in points, below which the web client shows a layout in one column when the layout has no breakpoint of its own. 640 by default; 0 stacks only layouts that ask to. The status's server.responsiveStackBelow says what it is now. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/notifications`](#admin-sessions-post-tabularius-admin-v1-notifications) | Emails the errors the server logs (and warnings too, when asked) to one address as a digest at most every five minutes. Off by default; an empty "to" turns it off. The status's server.notifications says what is set and whether mail can be sent. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/notifications/test`](#admin-sessions-post-tabularius-admin-v1-notifications-test) | Sends a test message to the notification address now. The answer says whether it went and why not when it did not. One test per 30 seconds. |

<a id="admin-sessions-get-tabularius-admin-v1-sessions"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/admin/v1/sessions`

Who is signed in: account, file, where from, device, how long idle.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | query | string | no | Only this file's sessions (any case). |

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/admin/v1/sessions?database=Invoices
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "sessions": [
    {
      "id": "3fa29c1b07de",
      "db": "Invoices",
      "account": "Ann",
      "idleSeconds": 12,
      "since": "2026-10-13T08:15:40.000Z",
      "client": "rest",
      "from": "192.168.1.20",
      "device": "TestAgent/1.0"
    }
  ]
}
```

client is rest or web; from, device and via are left out when not known.

<a id="admin-sessions-post-tabularius-admin-v1-sessions-end"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sessions/end`

Signs out one session by id, or every session of one account on a file.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | body | string | no | One session's id. |
| `database` | body | string | no | With account: the file (404 when it isn't hosted). |
| `account` | body | string | no | With database: the account whose sessions to end. |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sessions/end
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "database": "Invoices",
  "account": "Ann"
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "ended": 2
}
```

400 "give an id, or a database and account" with neither.

<a id="admin-sessions-post-tabularius-admin-v1-clients-id-disconnect"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/clients/{id}/disconnect`

Ends a session, releasing the records it was editing.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | string | yes | The client's id (hex). |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/clients/3fa29c1b07de/disconnect
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
```

Response `200`:

```json
{}
```

404 {} when no such session is connected.

<a id="admin-sessions-post-tabularius-admin-v1-clients-id-message"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/clients/{id}/message`

Shows a message to one connected web client.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | string | yes | The client's id (hex). |
| `text` | body | string | yes | The message (400 "a message is required" when empty). |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/clients/3fa29c1b07de/message
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "text": "Please save and log out in 5 minutes."
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "delivered": 1
}
```

delivered counts the live-update streams that got it. 404 {} when the client is no longer connected.

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/message`

Shows a message to every connected web client.

With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/message
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1

{

}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "delivered": 3

```

<a id="admin-sessions-post-tabularius-admin-v1-block-new-users"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/block-new-users`

Blocks new users, or lets them in again: no new session starts while those already open carry on. The status's server.blockNewUsers says which.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `on` | body | boolean | yes | true blocks, false lets new users in (400 "on is true or false" otherwise). |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/block-new-users
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "on": true
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "blockNewUsers": true
}
```

The same setting as the Admin API's /server/config/blocknewusers.

<a id="admin-sessions-post-tabularius-admin-v1-session-timeout"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/session-timeout`

Sets how many minutes a Data API session, and separately a web client session, may sit idle before it ends. The status's server.sessionIdleMinutes (the Data API, 15 by default) and server.webSessionIdleMinutes (the web client, which follows the Data API's value until it is given its own) say what they are now.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `minutes` | body | number | no | The Data API's limit: a whole number from 1 to 1440 (400 with the reason otherwise). At least one of minutes and webMinutes is required. |
| `webMinutes` | body | number | no | The web client's limit, a whole number from 1 to 1440, or null to make it follow the Data API's again (400 otherwise). The answer then includes webSessionIdleMinutes. |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/session-timeout
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "minutes": 30
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "sessionIdleMinutes": 30
}
```

Takes effect for the next call of every open session. Counterpart of the Admin API's session timeout settings.

<a id="admin-sessions-post-tabularius-admin-v1-responsive"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/responsive`

Sets the window width, in points, below which the web client shows a layout in one column when the layout has no breakpoint of its own. 640 by default; 0 stacks only layouts that ask to. The status's server.responsiveStackBelow says what it is now.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stackBelow` | body | number | yes | A whole number from 0 to 10000, or null for the default, 640 (400 with the reason otherwise). |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/responsive
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "stackBelow": 480
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "responsiveStackBelow": 480
}
```

A layout's own "Stack in one column below" (Layout Setup) wins over this; 0 there never stacks that layout. Open web client windows pick the new width up when they next open a layout.

<a id="admin-sessions-post-tabularius-admin-v1-notifications"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/notifications`

Emails the errors the server logs (and warnings too, when asked) to one address as a digest at most every five minutes. Off by default; an empty "to" turns it off. The status's server.notifications says what is set and whether mail can be sent.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `to` | body | string | yes | One plain email address, or an empty string to turn notifications off (400 for anything else). |
| `level` | body | string | no | "Error" (default) or "Warning" to include warnings (400 otherwise). |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/notifications
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "to": "ops@example.com",
  "level": "Error"
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "to": "ops@example.com",
  "level": "Error",
  "canSend": true
}
```

Mail goes through the server's Send Mail sender, so it needs sending switched on (or an email connection marked for Send Mail). In a cluster only the leader sends.

<a id="admin-sessions-post-tabularius-admin-v1-notifications-test"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/notifications/test`

Sends a test message to the notification address now. The answer says whether it went and why not when it did not. One test per 30 seconds.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/notifications/test
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
Content-Type: application/json
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "sent": true,
  "message": "Sent to ops@example.com."
}
```

<a id="admin-schedules"></a>

## Admin console: script schedules, server-side scripts and tests

Scripts run on the server on a timer, at a time of day, or each time a file opens, as a chosen account. Sign in as for every console call; all but GET need x-tabularius-admin: 1. A schedule's id is 12 hex characters. A bad schedule is 400 {"error": "…"} with the reason (no such script, the account can't run it, everyMinutes out of range, at not HH:MM, a capture-only file); an unknown id is 404 "no such schedule"; a method the path doesn't take is 405. Server-side scripts are the ones waiting for a turn or running (Perform Script on Server, schedules, automations and inbound hooks); script tests are a file's saved test cases, run on a copy of it.

Source: `packages/server/src/admin.ts`

| Method | Path | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/schedules`](#admin-schedules-get-tabularius-admin-v1-schedules) | Every schedule with its next run, last run, last failed run, and runs and failures since the server started. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/schedules`](#admin-schedules-post-tabularius-admin-v1-schedules) | Adds a schedule. |
| PATCH | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/schedules/{id}`](#admin-schedules-patch-tabularius-admin-v1-schedules-id) | Changes some of a schedule's settings; "" clears parameter or at. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/schedules/{id}/run`](#admin-schedules-post-tabularius-admin-v1-schedules-id-run) | Runs the schedule's script now and answers with the run. |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/schedules/{id}/runs`](#admin-schedules-get-tabularius-admin-v1-schedules-id-runs) | The schedule's recent runs (up to 50), newest first. |
| DELETE | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/schedules/{id}`](#admin-schedules-delete-tabularius-admin-v1-schedules-id) | Deletes a schedule and its run history. |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/server-scripts`](#admin-schedules-get-tabularius-admin-v1-server-scripts) | Server-side scripts running and waiting for a turn, and the last 100 that ended, from every worker of the server. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/server-scripts/{id}/cancel`](#admin-schedules-post-tabularius-admin-v1-server-scripts-id-cancel) | Cancels a server-side script: a waiting one never starts, a running one stops at its next step. |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/script-tests`](#admin-schedules-get-tabularius-admin-v1-script-tests) | Each hosted file that has saved script test cases, with how many there are for each script. Nothing runs. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/script-tests/run`](#admin-schedules-post-tabularius-admin-v1-script-tests-run) | Runs all of a file's saved script test cases, offline, on a throwaway copy of it (the hosted file never changes), and says which passed. |

<a id="admin-schedules-get-tabularius-admin-v1-schedules"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/admin/v1/schedules`

Every schedule with its next run, last run, last failed run, and runs and failures since the server started.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in.

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/admin/v1/schedules
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "schedules": [
    {
      "id": "9c2e71a4b0d3",
      "name": "Nightly totals",
      "database": "Invoices",
      "script": "Update Totals",
      "account": "Admin",
      "everyMinutes": 1440,
      "at": "02:00",
      "enabled": true,
      "next": "2026-10-14T02:00:00.000Z",
      "last": {
        "at": "2026-10-13T02:00:00.000Z",
        "error": 0,
        "result": "",
        "steps": 42,
        "ms": 380
      },
      "running": false,
      "runs": 1,
      "failures": 0
    }
  ]
}
```

<a id="admin-schedules-post-tabularius-admin-v1-schedules"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/schedules`

Adds a schedule.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | body | string | no | Its name (default the script's name). |
| `database` | body | string | yes | Hosted file. |
| `script` | body | string | yes | Script name. |
| `account` | body | string | yes | The account it runs as; it must be able to run the script. |
| `parameter` | body | string | no | Script parameter. |
| `everyMinutes` | body | number | no | Minutes between runs, 1 to 527040 (default 1440). |
| `at` | body | string | no | Local time of day, HH:MM, that runs line up with. |
| `onOpen` | body | boolean | no | Run each time the file opens instead of on a timer. |
| `enabled` | body | boolean | no | Default true. |
| `network` | body | boolean | no | Insert from URL may reach the network (only when the server allows it too). Turning it on also approves the file's scripts as they are for connections (see approveScripts). |
| `sync` | body | object | no | Makes this a sync of the file with its FileMaker Server copy instead of a script (no script, account, parameter, network or onOpen; set up in the Sync page first; at least 5 minutes apart). {} is a check, a dry run that reads both sides and writes neither. {"write": true} also sends this file's changes to FileMaker, and {"pull": true} also changes this file with FileMaker's; each needs the file's sync setup to allow it too. A scheduled run never includes deletions, and records changed on both sides stop it before anything moves: they show as "conflicts" on the run and in the health report's syncAlerts. |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/schedules
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "Nightly totals",
  "database": "Invoices",
  "script": "Update Totals",
  "account": "Admin",
  "everyMinutes": 1440,
  "at": "02:00"
}
```

Response `201`:

```json
{
  "id": "9c2e71a4b0d3",
  "name": "Nightly totals",
  "database": "Invoices",
  "script": "Update Totals",
  "account": "Admin",
  "everyMinutes": 1440,
  "enabled": true,
  "at": "02:00"
}
```

<a id="admin-schedules-patch-tabularius-admin-v1-schedules-id"></a>

### `PATCH /tabularius/admin/v1/schedules/{id}`

Changes some of a schedule's settings; "" clears parameter or at.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | string | yes | The schedule's id. |
| `(any of POST's fields)` | body | object | no | Only the fields given are changed. |
| `approveScripts` | body | boolean | no | true: the hosted files (scripts, formulas, layouts, menus, options, in every file) as they are now are fine for this schedule's connections. A network schedule whose files changed since it was created, switched to network or last approved is listed with "connectionsHeld": true and "connectionsChanged" (what changed), and its runs go ahead without connections or connection mail (the run's message says so) until this is sent. |

**Example:**

```http
PATCH /tabularius/admin/v1/schedules/9c2e71a4b0d3
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "enabled": false
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "id": "9c2e71a4b0d3",
  "name": "Nightly totals",
  "database": "Invoices",
  "script": "Update Totals",
  "account": "Admin",
  "everyMinutes": 1440,
  "enabled": false,
  "at": "02:00"
}
```

<a id="admin-schedules-post-tabularius-admin-v1-schedules-id-run"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/schedules/{id}/run`

Runs the schedule's script now and answers with the run.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | string | yes | The schedule's id. |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/schedules/9c2e71a4b0d3/run
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "at": "2026-10-13T08:50:00.000Z",
  "error": 0,
  "result": "",
  "steps": 42,
  "ms": 371,
  "manual": true
}
```

A script that fails still answers 200, with its error code and message. 400 "the schedule is already running".

With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in.

### `DELETE /tabularius/admin/v1/schedules/{id}`

Deletes a schedule and its run history.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | string | yes | The schedule's id. |

**Example:**

```http
DELETE /tabularius/admin/v1/schedules/9c2e71a4b0d3
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "deleted": true
}
```

<a id="admin-schedules-get-tabularius-admin-v1-server-scripts"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/admin/v1/server-scripts`

Server-side scripts running and waiting for a turn, and the last 100 that ended, from every worker of the server.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in.

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/admin/v1/server-scripts
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "workers": 1,
  "limit": 50,
  "running": [
    {
      "id": "k3j9x2m1",
      "file": "Invoices",
      "script": "Update Totals",
      "account": "Admin",
      "kind": "schedule",
      "state": "running",
      "queuedAt": "2026-10-13T02:00:00.000Z",
      "startedAt": "2026-10-13T02:00:00.010Z"
    }
  ],
  "queued": [
    {
      "id": "p8w4n7c5",
      "file": "Invoices",
      "script": "Send Reminders",
      "account": "Ann",
      "kind": "server",
      "state": "queued",
      "queuedAt": "2026-10-13T02:00:01.200Z"
    }
  ],
  "recent": [
    {
      "id": "h5t2b9d4",
      "file": "Invoices",
      "script": "Post Invoice",
      "account": "Ann",
      "kind": "automation",
      "queuedAt": "2026-10-13T01:59:40.000Z",
      "startedAt": "2026-10-13T01:59:40.020Z",
      "waitMs": 20,
      "ms": 310,
      "outcome": "ok"
    }
  ]
}
```

At most limit scripts run at once (for each worker the greater of 50 and its number of CPU cores, added up over workers); the rest wait, first come first served. kind is server (Perform Script on Server), schedule, automation or hook. recent is newest first, and each entry has waitMs (time waiting for a turn), ms (time running) and outcome: ok, error (the script ended with a script error, shown in error), failed or canceled (canceledBy says who). Names only: never a parameter or a result.

<a id="admin-schedules-post-tabularius-admin-v1-server-scripts-id-cancel"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/server-scripts/{id}/cancel`

Cancels a server-side script: a waiting one never starts, a running one stops at its next step.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | string | yes | The script's id from the list. With several workers, another worker's script stops when that worker hears of it, within a moment. |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/server-scripts/p8w4n7c5/cancel
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "canceled": true
}
```

404 {"error": "That script has already ended"} when no queue lists it. The cancel is written to the server's log.

<a id="admin-schedules-get-tabularius-admin-v1-script-tests"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/admin/v1/script-tests`

Each hosted file that has saved script test cases, with how many there are for each script. Nothing runs.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in.

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/admin/v1/script-tests
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "files": [
    {
      "database": "Invoices",
      "tests": 3,
      "scripts": [
        {
          "script": "Post Invoice",
          "tests": 2
        },
        {
          "script": "Update Totals",
          "tests": 1
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Files with no test cases are left out. running is added, with the file's name, while a test run (below) is under way. A case whose script was deleted is listed as "Script 12 (deleted)".

<a id="admin-schedules-post-tabularius-admin-v1-script-tests-run"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/script-tests/run`

Runs all of a file's saved script test cases, offline, on a throwaway copy of it (the hosted file never changes), and says which passed.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | body | string | yes | Hosted file (404 "No such hosted file" when it isn't). |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/script-tests/run
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "database": "Invoices"
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "database": "Invoices",
  "ran": 3,
  "passed": 2,
  "failed": 1,
  "ms": 940,
  "scripts": [
    {
      "script": "Post Invoice",
      "passed": 1,
      "failed": 1,
      "cases": [
        {
          "name": "Posts a paid invoice",
          "passed": true,
          "failures": [],
          "ms": 120
        },
        {
          "name": "Refuses an empty invoice",
          "passed": false,
          "failures": [
            {
              "what": "result",
              "expected": "Nothing to post",
              "actual": ""
            }
          ],
          "ms": 95
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "script": "Update Totals",
      "passed": 1,
      "failed": 0,
      "cases": [
        {
          "name": "Adds up a month",
          "passed": true,
          "failures": [],
          "ms": 210
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

One run at a time: 409 {"error": "The script tests of <file> are running; try again when they finish"} while another is under way. A file too big to copy (over 1 GB) is 400 with the reason. A case that failed lists what differed in failures ({what, expected, actual}); message is added when the script stopped with an error or the run itself failed. The run is written to the server's log.

<a id="admin-webhooks"></a>

## Admin console: webhooks, inbound hooks and the outbox

Webhooks post a hosted file's record changes to a URL (delivered only on a server started with --allow-webhooks). The outbox shows the mail and web requests scripts made in outbound test mode (serve --test-outbound), none of which reached anyone. Inbound hooks are the other direction: the addresses other services call to run a script (see Inbound hooks), set up here with a secret each. Sign in as for every console call; all but GET need x-tabularius-admin: 1. Errors are {"error": "…"}; a method the path doesn't take is 405.

Source: `packages/server/src/admin.ts`

| Method | Path | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/webhooks`](#admin-webhooks-get-tabularius-admin-v1-webhooks) | Every webhook (without its secret) with how delivery is going, and whether sending is allowed on this server. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/webhooks`](#admin-webhooks-post-tabularius-admin-v1-webhooks) | Adds a webhook; its signing secret is in this answer only. |
| PATCH | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/webhooks/{id}`](#admin-webhooks-patch-tabularius-admin-v1-webhooks-id) | Turns a webhook on or off. |
| DELETE | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/webhooks/{id}`](#admin-webhooks-delete-tabularius-admin-v1-webhooks-id) | Removes a webhook and anything queued for it. |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/inbound-hooks`](#admin-webhooks-get-tabularius-admin-v1-inbound-hooks) | Every inbound hook (without its secret) with its address and latest calls, and whether this server answers calls at all. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/inbound-hooks`](#admin-webhooks-post-tabularius-admin-v1-inbound-hooks) | Makes an inbound hook; its secret is in this answer only. |
| PATCH | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/inbound-hooks/{id}`](#admin-webhooks-patch-tabularius-admin-v1-inbound-hooks-id) | Changes a hook: turns it on or off, or changes its name, script, account, layout, rate or network use. Anything left out stays as it is. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/inbound-hooks/{id}/secret`](#admin-webhooks-post-tabularius-admin-v1-inbound-hooks-id-secret) | Makes a new secret for a hook; calls signed with the old one are refused from then on. |
| DELETE | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/inbound-hooks/{id}`](#admin-webhooks-delete-tabularius-admin-v1-inbound-hooks-id) | Removes a hook. |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/outbox`](#admin-webhooks-get-tabularius-admin-v1-outbox) | Outbound test mode's settings and the captured mail and web requests, newest first, without attachment contents. |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/outbox/{id}`](#admin-webhooks-get-tabularius-admin-v1-outbox-id) | One captured message or request, with its attachments (base64). |
| DELETE | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/outbox`](#admin-webhooks-delete-tabularius-admin-v1-outbox) | Empties the outbox. |

<a id="admin-webhooks-get-tabularius-admin-v1-webhooks"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/admin/v1/webhooks`

Every webhook (without its secret) with how delivery is going, and whether sending is allowed on this server.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in.

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/admin/v1/webhooks
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "allowed": true,
  "webhooks": [
    {
      "id": "5d0e9f1a2b3c",
      "url": "https://hooks.example.com/invoices",
      "database": "Invoices",

        "Invoices"
      ],

      "queued": 0,
      "lastOk": "2026-10-13T08:14:04.000Z",
```
