```json
    }
  ]
}
```

<a id="admin-webhooks-post-tabularius-admin-v1-webhooks"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/webhooks`

Adds a webhook; its signing secret is in this answer only.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | body | string | yes | http or https URL, with no credentials in it and not on the link-local range. |
| `database` | body | string | yes | Hosted file whose changes it gets. |
| `tables` | body | array of string | no | Only these tables (all when left out). |
| `enabled` | body | boolean | no | Default true. |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/webhooks
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "url": "https://hooks.example.com/invoices",
  "database": "Invoices",
  "tables": [
    "Invoices"
  ]
}
```

Response `201`:

```json
{
  "id": "5d0e9f1a2b3c",
  "url": "https://hooks.example.com/invoices",
  "database": "Invoices",
  "tables": [
    "Invoices"
  ],
  "secret": "pQ4v0x9Lk2mZc8Rt1yWb3nHs6dFg7aJe",
  "enabled": true
}
```

400 with the reason for a bad URL, a file that isn't hosted, or an unknown table.

<a id="admin-webhooks-patch-tabularius-admin-v1-webhooks-id"></a>

### `PATCH /tabularius/admin/v1/webhooks/{id}`

Turns a webhook on or off.

With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | string | yes | The webhook's id (400 "no such webhook"). |
| `enabled` | body | boolean | no | On or off. |

```http
PATCH /tabularius/admin/v1/webhooks/5d0e9f1a2b3c
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "enabled": false
}
```

```json
  "id": "5d0e9f1a2b3c",

  "tables": [
    "Invoices"
```

<a id="admin-webhooks-delete-tabularius-admin-v1-webhooks-id"></a>

### `DELETE /tabularius/admin/v1/webhooks/{id}`

Removes a webhook and anything queued for it.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

<a id="admin-webhooks-get-tabularius-admin-v1-inbound-hooks"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/admin/v1/inbound-hooks`

Every inbound hook (without its secret) with its address and latest calls, and whether this server answers calls at all.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in.

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/admin/v1/inbound-hooks
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "allowed": true,
  "hooks": [
    {
      "id": "9c2e5b7a1f40d3e816",
      "name": "Stripe payments",
      "database": "Invoices",
      "script": "Mark invoice paid",
      "account": "Hooks",
      "layout": "Invoices",
      "enabled": true,
      "perMinute": 60,
      "created": "2026-10-12T09:00:00.000Z",
      "path": "/tabularius/hooks/v1/9c2e5b7a1f40d3e816",
      "fullAccess": true,
      "calls": [
        {
          "at": "2026-10-13T08:40:12.000Z",
          "status": 200,
          "outcome": "ok",
          "ms": 140,
          "bytes": 312,
          "from": "54.187.174.169"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

allowed is false unless the server was started with --allow-inbound-hooks; calls are refused (404) until then. calls are the latest 20, newest first, with outcome ok, error or refused and, for the last two, a message; the body of a call is never kept. fullAccess is true when the hook's account has Full Access, which is a warning: anyone holding the secret gets the script's result. network is shown when the hook may use the network.

<a id="admin-webhooks-post-tabularius-admin-v1-inbound-hooks"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/inbound-hooks`

Makes an inbound hook; its secret is in this answer only.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | body | string | yes | A name to tell it by (up to 120 characters). |
| `database` | body | string | yes | Hosted file (400 "<name> is not hosted"; a capture-only file never has hooks). |
| `script` | body | string | yes | The script to run (400 "No script …" when the file has none by that name). |
| `account` | body | string | yes | The account it runs as; its privilege set applies (400 "No account …"). |
| `layout` | body | string | no | Where the script starts; without it, the file's first layout. |
| `perMinute` | body | number | no | Calls a minute it answers, a whole number from 1 to 6000 (default 60); more get 429. |
| `network` | body | boolean | no | true lets Insert from URL reach the network; it works only when the server also allows scripts the network. Default false. |
| `enabled` | body | boolean | no | Default true. |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/inbound-hooks
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "Stripe payments",
  "database": "Invoices",
  "script": "Mark invoice paid",
  "account": "Hooks",
  "layout": "Invoices"
}
```

Response `201`:

```json
{
  "id": "9c2e5b7a1f40d3e816",
  "name": "Stripe payments",
  "database": "Invoices",
  "script": "Mark invoice paid",
  "account": "Hooks",
  "layout": "Invoices",
  "enabled": true,
  "perMinute": 60,
  "secret": "pQ4v0x9Lk2mZc8Rt1yWb3nHs6dFg7aJeU5oVnCiXtMk",
  "created": "2026-10-12T09:00:00.000Z",
  "path": "/tabularius/hooks/v1/9c2e5b7a1f40d3e816"
}
```

The secret is shown here and when it is replaced, and never again. A call is signed with it (see Inbound hooks).

<a id="admin-webhooks-patch-tabularius-admin-v1-inbound-hooks-id"></a>

### `PATCH /tabularius/admin/v1/inbound-hooks/{id}`

Changes a hook: turns it on or off, or changes its name, script, account, layout, rate or network use. Anything left out stays as it is.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | string | yes | The hook's id (400 "No such hook"). |
| `enabled` | body | boolean | no | On or off. |
| `name` | body | string | no | As for POST. |
| `script` | body | string | no | As for POST. |
| `account` | body | string | no | As for POST. |
| `layout` | body | string | no | As for POST; null puts back the file's first layout. |
| `perMinute` | body | number | no | As for POST. |
| `network` | body | boolean | no | As for POST. |

**Example:**

```http
PATCH /tabularius/admin/v1/inbound-hooks/9c2e5b7a1f40d3e816
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "enabled": false
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "id": "9c2e5b7a1f40d3e816",
  "name": "Stripe payments",
  "database": "Invoices",
  "script": "Mark invoice paid",
  "account": "Hooks",
  "layout": "Invoices",
  "enabled": false,
  "perMinute": 60,
  "created": "2026-10-12T09:00:00.000Z"
}
```

The file a hook belongs to can't be changed. The answer has no secret.

<a id="admin-webhooks-post-tabularius-admin-v1-inbound-hooks-id-secret"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/inbound-hooks/{id}/secret`

Makes a new secret for a hook; calls signed with the old one are refused from then on.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | string | yes | The hook's id (400 "No such hook"). |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/inbound-hooks/9c2e5b7a1f40d3e816/secret
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "id": "9c2e5b7a1f40d3e816",
  "secret": "Zr7c2Wn9Lk4mQx1yBt8vHs3dFg6aJeU0oVnCiXtMkP"
}
```

<a id="admin-plugins"></a>

## Admin console: plug-ins

The plug-ins in the server's plugins folder (installed with tabularius plugins install): who made each one, what it asks for, which hosted files have it on, and the secrets it asked for. Turning one on or off takes effect at once and is kept in plugins/enabled.json for the next start. A secret's value is never returned or logged. Sign in as for every console call; all but GET need x-tabularius-admin: 1. Errors are {"error": "…"}; a method the path doesn't take is 405.

Source: `packages/server/src/admin.ts`

| Method | Path | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/plugins`](#admin-plugins-get-tabularius-admin-v1-plugins) | Every installed plug-in with its permissions, who signed its package, the files it is on for, and which secrets are set, plus the hosted files and anything that stopped a plug-in loading. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/plugins/{id}/enable`](#admin-plugins-post-tabularius-admin-v1-plugins-id-enable) | Turns a plug-in on for a hosted file, now and for the next start. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/plugins/{id}/disable`](#admin-plugins-post-tabularius-admin-v1-plugins-id-disable) | Turns a plug-in off for a hosted file. |
| PUT | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/plugins/{id}/secrets/{name}`](#admin-plugins-put-tabularius-admin-v1-plugins-id-secrets-name) | Sets a secret the plug-in asked for (such as an API key). Kept in a file only the server's user can read. |
| DELETE | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/plugins/{id}/secrets/{name}`](#admin-plugins-delete-tabularius-admin-v1-plugins-id-secrets-name) | Clears a secret. |

<a id="admin-plugins-get-tabularius-admin-v1-plugins"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/admin/v1/plugins`

Every installed plug-in with its permissions, who signed its package, the files it is on for, and which secrets are set, plus the hosted files and anything that stopped a plug-in loading.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in.

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/admin/v1/plugins
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "plugins": [
    {
      "id": "org.example.troi-file",
      "name": "Troi File",
      "version": "1.2.0",
      "publisher": "Example Co",
      "runtime": "js",
      "functions": [
        "TrFile_Exists",
        "TrFile_Read"
      ],
      "permissions": {
        "files": [
          "documents:read"
        ],
        "network": [
          "api.example.com"
        ],
        "mail": false
      },
      "package": {
        "signer": "a1b2c3d4:e5f60718:293a4b5c:6d7e8f90",
        "installedAt": "2026-10-13T08:00:00.000Z"
      },
      "enabledFor": [
        "Invoices"
      ],
      "secrets": [
        {
          "name": "API_KEY",
          "set": true
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "builtins": [
    {
      "id": "com.openhbam.baseelements",
      "name": "BaseElements",
      "publisher": "Goya",
      "description": "JSON, XML, XSLT, zip, file, text and container functions of the BaseElements plug-in, reimplemented in Tabularius",
      "enabledFor": [
        "Invoices",
        "Inventory"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "files": [
    "Invoices",
    "Inventory"
  ],
  "problems": []
}
```

builtins are the packs that ship inside Tabularius: on for every file until turned off for one. package is null for a plug-in put in the folder by hand, and its signer is null for an unsigned package. problems lists plug-ins that could not be loaded, such as a file changed since it was installed.

<a id="admin-plugins-post-tabularius-admin-v1-plugins-id-enable"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/plugins/{id}/enable`

Turns a plug-in on for a hosted file, now and for the next start.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | string | yes | The plug-in's id (404 "<id> isn't installed"). |
| `file` | body | string | yes | Hosted file (404 "that file is not hosted here"). |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/plugins/org.example.troi-file/enable
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "file": "Invoices"
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "plugins": [
    {
      "id": "org.example.troi-file",
      "enabledFor": [
        "Invoices"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "files": [
    "Invoices",
    "Inventory"
  ],
  "problems": []
}
```

The answer is the same listing as GET (trimmed here). 400 with the reason when the plug-in clashes with another one on for that file (the same function name). The id can be a built-in pack's (com.openhbam.baseelements): turned off for a file, its functions give ? there, as in FileMaker when a plug-in isn't installed. Built-in packs have no secrets (400).

<a id="admin-plugins-put-tabularius-admin-v1-plugins-id-secrets-name"></a>

### `PUT /tabularius/admin/v1/plugins/{id}/secrets/{name}`

Sets a secret the plug-in asked for (such as an API key). Kept in a file only the server's user can read.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | string | yes | The plug-in's id. |
| `name` | path | string | yes | One of the names in the plug-in's plugin.json (400 "doesn't ask for a secret called …" otherwise). |
| `value` | body | string | yes | The secret. Never returned or logged; an empty value is 400. |

**Example:**

```http
PUT /tabularius/admin/v1/plugins/org.example.troi-file/secrets/API_KEY
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "value": "sk-…"
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "plugins": [
    {
      "id": "org.example.troi-file",
      "secrets": [
        {
          "name": "API_KEY",
          "set": true
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "files": [
    "Invoices"
  ],
  "problems": []
}
```

The answer is the same listing as GET (trimmed here); it says whether each secret is set, never what it is. The plug-in reads it when it next asks, with no restart.

<a id="admin-connections"></a>

## Admin console: connections

Outside services (S3-compatible storage, any web API with a token, basic, key-header or OAuth 2 sign-in, and an outgoing mail account) that scripts, plug-ins and AI tools use by name. A connection's secrets are sealed on the server (AES-256-GCM, with a key from TABULARIUS_SECRETS_KEY or a key file only the server's user can read) and used only inside the server: no call here, no script, no plug-in and no AI tool is ever given one, and none is logged. A connection made by the AI is a draft until a person has set its secrets and approved it in the console. Sign in as for every console call; all but GET need x-tabularius-admin: 1. Errors are {"error": "…"}: 400 for a setting that can't work, 404 for a connection that isn't there, 405 for a method the path doesn't take.

Source: `packages/server/src/admin.ts`

| Method | Path | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/connections`](#admin-connections-get-tabularius-admin-v1-connections) | The connection types and every connection with its settings, state and which secrets are set (never their values). |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/connections`](#admin-connections-post-tabularius-admin-v1-connections) | Makes a connection as a draft. Its secrets are set separately, then it is approved. |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/connections/{id}`](#admin-connections-get-tabularius-admin-v1-connections-id) | One connection, as in the listing. |
| PATCH | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/connections/{id}`](#admin-connections-patch-tabularius-admin-v1-connections-id) | Changes a connection's name, settings, files or note, or turns an approved one on or off. Anything left out stays as it is. |
| PUT | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/connections/{id}/secrets/{field}`](#admin-connections-put-tabularius-admin-v1-connections-id-secrets-field) | Sets one of the connection's secrets (an access key, say). Sealed on the server; never returned or logged. |
| DELETE | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/connections/{id}/secrets/{field}`](#admin-connections-delete-tabularius-admin-v1-connections-id-secrets-field) | Clears a secret. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/connections/{id}/approve`](#admin-connections-post-tabularius-admin-v1-connections-id-approve) | A person's go-ahead: a draft becomes usable, once its required secrets are set. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/connections/{id}/test`](#admin-connections-post-tabularius-admin-v1-connections-id-test) | Asks the service something harmless with the connection's credentials (S3: lists one object in its folder) and says how it went. Works for a draft, so the person can check what they pasted before approving. |
| DELETE | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/connections/{id}`](#admin-connections-delete-tabularius-admin-v1-connections-id) | Removes a connection and deletes its sealed secrets. |

<a id="admin-connections-get-tabularius-admin-v1-connections"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/admin/v1/connections`

The connection types and every connection with its settings, state and which secrets are set (never their values).

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in.

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/admin/v1/connections
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "types": [
    {
      "id": "s3",
      "label": "S3-compatible storage",
      "description": "Amazon S3, Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2, MinIO, Wasabi or anything that speaks the S3 protocol",
      "config": [
        {
          "name": "bucket",
          "label": "Bucket",
          "required": true
        }
      ],
      "secrets": [
        {
          "name": "accessKey",
          "label": "Access key ID",
          "required": true
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "connections": [
    {
      "id": "3f9c1a7b2d40",
      "name": "invoices",
      "type": "s3",
      "status": "active",
      "config": {
        "bucket": "acme-invoices",
        "region": "us-east-1",
        "prefix": "tabularius"
      },
      "created": "2026-10-15T00:30:00.000Z",
      "createdBy": "console",
      "approved": "2026-10-15T00:31:00.000Z",
      "secrets": [
        {
          "name": "accessKey",
          "label": "Access key ID",
          "required": true,
          "set": true
        },
        {
          "name": "secretKey",
          "label": "Secret access key",
          "required": true,
          "set": true
        },
        {
          "name": "sessionToken",
          "label": "Session token",
          "required": false,
          "set": false
        }
```

status is draft (waiting for a person: made by the AI, or not yet approved), active or disabled. problem appears when the sealed secrets can't be opened (a missing or different TABULARIUS_SECRETS_KEY).

<a id="admin-connections-post-tabularius-admin-v1-connections"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/connections`

Makes a connection as a draft. Its secrets are set separately, then it is approved.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | body | string | yes | What scripts call it by: letters, digits, dashes or underscores, starting with a letter; unique ignoring case. |
| `type` | body | string | yes | A type from GET (s3). |
| `config` | body | object | yes | The type's settings. s3: bucket, region (default us-east-1), endpoint (empty for Amazon S3; https, or http on your own network) and prefix (a folder in the bucket that all use is kept inside). A setting that looks like a key or password is refused: secrets are not settings. |
| `files` | body | string[] | no | Hosted files that may use it; without it every file may, except capture-only ones. |
| `note` | body | string | no | A reminder of what it is for (500 characters at most). |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/connections
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "invoices",
  "type": "s3",
  "config": {
    "bucket": "acme-invoices",
    "prefix": "tabularius"
  }
}
```

Response `201`:

```json
    {
      "name": "accessKey",
      "label": "Access key ID",
      "required": true,
      "set": false
    }
  ],
  "ready": false
}
```

<a id="admin-connections-get-tabularius-admin-v1-connections-id"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/admin/v1/connections/{id}`

One connection, as in the listing.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | string | yes | The connection's id. |

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/admin/v1/connections/3f9c1a7b2d40
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "id": "3f9c1a7b2d40",
  "name": "invoices",
  "type": "s3",
  "status": "active",
  "config": {
    "bucket": "acme-invoices",
    "region": "us-east-1"
  },
  "ready": true
}
```

<a id="admin-connections-patch-tabularius-admin-v1-connections-id"></a>

### `PATCH /tabularius/admin/v1/connections/{id}`

Changes a connection's name, settings, files or note, or turns an approved one on or off. Anything left out stays as it is.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | string | yes | The connection's id. |
| `name` | body | string | no | A new name; scripts using the old one stop working. |
| `config` | body | object | no | All of the settings again, as when it was made. |
| `files` | body | string[] | no | Hosted files that may use it; an empty list means every file. |
| `note` | body | string | no | The reminder; empty clears it. |
| `enabled` | body | boolean | no | On or off. A draft has to be approved first (400). |

**Example:**

```http
PATCH /tabularius/admin/v1/connections/3f9c1a7b2d40
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "note": "Configured by the admin"
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "id": "3f9c1a7b2d40",
  "name": "invoices",
  "note": "Configured by the admin",
  "status": "draft"
}
```

<a id="admin-connections-put-tabularius-admin-v1-connections-id-secrets-field"></a>

### `PUT /tabularius/admin/v1/connections/{id}/secrets/{field}`

Sets one of the connection's secrets (an access key, say). Sealed on the server; never returned or logged.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | string | yes | The connection's id. |
| `field` | path | string | yes | A secret of its type: s3 has accessKey, secretKey and sessionToken (400 otherwise). |
| `value` | body | string | yes | The secret: one line of at most 4096 characters. |

**Example:**

```http
PUT /tabularius/admin/v1/connections/3f9c1a7b2d40/secrets/accessKey
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "value": "reference-access-key-placeholder"
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "id": "3f9c1a7b2d40",
  "name": "invoices",
  "secrets": [
    {
      "name": "accessKey",
      "label": "Access key ID",
      "required": true,
      "set": true
    }
  ],
  "ready": false
}
```

The answer says whether each secret is set, never what it is.

<a id="admin-connections-delete-tabularius-admin-v1-connections-id-secrets-field"></a>

### `DELETE /tabularius/admin/v1/connections/{id}/secrets/{field}`

Clears a secret.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | string | yes | The connection's id. |
| `field` | path | string | yes | The secret's name. |

**Example:**

```http
DELETE /tabularius/admin/v1/connections/3f9c1a7b2d40/secrets/sessionToken
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "id": "3f9c1a7b2d40",
  "name": "invoices",
  "secrets": [
    {
      "name": "sessionToken",
      "label": "Session token",
      "required": false,
      "set": false
    }
  ]
}
```

<a id="admin-connections-post-tabularius-admin-v1-connections-id-approve"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/connections/{id}/approve`

A person's go-ahead: a draft becomes usable, once its required secrets are set.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | string | yes | The connection's id. |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/connections/3f9c1a7b2d40/approve
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "id": "3f9c1a7b2d40",
  "name": "invoices",
  "status": "active",
  "approved": "2026-10-15T00:31:00.000Z"
}
```

400 "Set Access key ID and Secret access key first" while required secrets are missing, and when it is already approved. Only this console route approves: no script, plug-in or AI tool can.

<a id="admin-connections-post-tabularius-admin-v1-connections-id-test"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/connections/{id}/test`

Asks the service something harmless with the connection's credentials (S3: lists one object in its folder) and says how it went. Works for a draft, so the person can check what they pasted before approving.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | string | yes | The connection's id. |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/connections/3f9c1a7b2d40/test
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "at": "2026-10-15T00:31:00.000Z",
  "ok": true,
  "message": "Reached bucket acme-invoices under tabularius/; it has objects there. (84 ms)",
  "connection": {
    "id": "3f9c1a7b2d40",
    "name": "invoices"
  }
}
```

A refusal from the service comes back as ok: false with the service's own words (for example "403 SignatureDoesNotMatch"), still with status 200. The result is kept as the connection's lastTest.

<a id="admin-connections-delete-tabularius-admin-v1-connections-id"></a>

### `DELETE /tabularius/admin/v1/connections/{id}`

Removes a connection and deletes its sealed secrets.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | string | yes | The connection's id. |

**Example:**

```http
DELETE /tabularius/admin/v1/connections/3f9c1a7b2d40
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
```

Response `200`:

```json
{}
```

Scripts that used it fail from then on.

<a id="admin-ai"></a>

## Admin console: AI

The AI side of the console: the assistant's usage and cost, keeping a file's data from AI, swapping personal data for stand-ins before anything goes to AI, planning and making a new file from a description, scheduled digests, and API tokens for AI apps (MCP). Sign in as for every console call; all but GET need x-tabularius-admin: 1. Errors are {"error": "…"}; a method the path doesn't take is 405 (404 under digests).

Source: `packages/server/src/admin.ts`

| Method | Path | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/ai-policy/{database}`](#admin-ai-get-tabularius-admin-v1-ai-policy-database) | Reads the per-file AI-visible policy. New solutions default on; imported and existing files without the setting default off. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/ai-policy/{database}`](#admin-ai-post-tabularius-admin-v1-ai-policy-database) | Sets the AI-visible policy in file metadata. When on, AI refuses secret-bearing sources without explicit privilege-set exceptions and refuses uncertain read sets. |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/ai-usage`](#admin-ai-get-tabularius-admin-v1-ai-usage) | The assistant's tokens and approximate cost: today against its limit, this month against its budget, the latest questions (never their text) and the models in use. |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/ai-access/{database}`](#admin-ai-get-tabularius-admin-v1-ai-access-database) | Whether AI apps and the assistant may read the file, and why not. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/ai-access/{database}`](#admin-ai-post-tabularius-admin-v1-ai-access-database) | Turns AI on or off for a file; off keeps its data from AI apps, the assistant, digests' summaries and AI matching, whatever an account's privileges. Logged in the file's security events as "admin console". |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/pii/{database}`](#admin-ai-get-tabularius-admin-v1-pii-database) | Personal data isolation for a file: whether it is on, how each field is treated and why, and a few records as an AI model would get them. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/pii/{database}`](#admin-ai-post-tabularius-admin-v1-pii-database) | Turns personal data isolation on or off for a file. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/pii/{database}/field`](#admin-ai-post-tabularius-admin-v1-pii-database-field) | Marks one field as personal, as not personal, or back to what the server works out. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/solutions/plan`](#admin-ai-post-tabularius-admin-v1-solutions-plan) | Asks the assistant to plan a new file from a description: the design changes it would make, tried on an empty scratch file and with its starter scripts dry-run. Nothing is created. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/solutions`](#admin-ai-post-tabularius-admin-v1-solutions) | Makes a new hosted file from a plan's changes, all or nothing. |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/digests`](#admin-ai-get-tabularius-admin-v1-digests) | Every hosted file's scheduled digests, with their schedule in words, next run and last run. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/digests/{database}/{id}/run`](#admin-ai-post-tabularius-admin-v1-digests-database-id-run) | Runs a digest now, as its account, and answers with the run (without the dashboard data). |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/mcp`](#admin-ai-get-tabularius-admin-v1-mcp) | The tokens AI apps sign in to /mcp with (each file's API tokens that reach fmmcp, and older console tokens), and each file's accounts, the sets an AI agent may hold, and its layouts. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/mcp/tokens`](#admin-ai-post-tabularius-admin-v1-mcp-tokens) | Makes an API token for AI apps (surface fmmcp) for an account, or for a new AI agent account; the token is in this answer only. |
| DELETE | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/mcp/tokens/{id}`](#admin-ai-delete-tabularius-admin-v1-mcp-tokens-id) | Revokes an AI app token: an older console token, or a file's API token. |

<a id="admin-ai-get-tabularius-admin-v1-ai-policy-database"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/admin/v1/ai-policy/{database}`

Reads the per-file AI-visible policy. New solutions default on; imported and existing files without the setting default off.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | path | string | yes | Hosted file. |

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/admin/v1/ai-policy/Invoices
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "on": true
}
```

<a id="admin-ai-post-tabularius-admin-v1-ai-policy-database"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/ai-policy/{database}`

Sets the AI-visible policy in file metadata. When on, AI refuses secret-bearing sources without explicit privilege-set exceptions and refuses uncertain read sets.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | path | string | yes | Hosted file. |
| `on` | body | boolean | yes | true or false; other values return 400. |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/ai-policy/Invoices
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "on": true
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "on": true
}
```

Manage Security edits aiVisible on a privilege set: {"Payroll":["Password"]} marks fields; {"Payroll":true} marks a whole base table. Ordinary privileges still apply. The AI access switch is separate.

### `GET /tabularius/admin/v1/ai-usage`

The assistant's tokens and approximate cost: today against its limit, this month against its budget, the latest questions (never their text) and the models in use.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in.

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/admin/v1/ai-usage

```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "today": {
    "tokens": 18400
  },
  "month": {
    "month": "2026-10",
    "tokens": 412000,
    "costUsd": 1.83,
    "questions": 96,
```

<a id="admin-ai-get-tabularius-admin-v1-ai-access-database"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/admin/v1/ai-access/{database}`

Whether AI apps and the assistant may read the file, and why not.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | path | string | yes | Hosted file (404 "No such hosted file"). |

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/admin/v1/ai-access/Invoices
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "allowed": true,
  "turnedOff": false,
  "byServer": false
}
```

turnedOff: turned off for this file; byServer: the server's --ai-exclude names it; through: a hosted file it uses data from has AI off.

<a id="admin-ai-post-tabularius-admin-v1-ai-access-database"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/ai-access/{database}`

Turns AI on or off for a file; off keeps its data from AI apps, the assistant, digests' summaries and AI matching, whatever an account's privileges. Logged in the file's security events as "admin console".

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | path | string | yes | Hosted file. |
| `on` | body | boolean | yes | true or false (400 "Send {\"on\": true} or {\"on\": false}" otherwise). |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/ai-access/Payroll
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "on": false
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "allowed": false,
  "turnedOff": true,
  "byServer": false
}
```

<a id="admin-ai-get-tabularius-admin-v1-pii-database"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/admin/v1/pii/{database}`

Personal data isolation for a file: whether it is on, how each field is treated and why, and a few records as an AI model would get them.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | path | string | yes | Hosted file, any case (404 "No such hosted file"). |
| `layout` | query | string | no | The layout the sample records come from (default: the first layout that shows a table). |

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/admin/v1/pii/Contacts?layout=Contact%20List
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "on": true,
  "tables": [
    {
      "table": "Contacts",
      "fields": [
        {
          "field": "Name",
          "pii": true,
          "why": "its name says it holds a person's name"
        },
        {
          "field": "Status",
          "pii": false,
          "why": "it holds a few repeated values (3), like a category",
          "marked": true
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "sample": {
    "layout": "Contact List",
    "records": [
      {
        "recordId": 1,
        "fieldData": {
          "Name": "<PERSON_1>",
          "Status": "Active"
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

With isolation on, personal values (names, emails, phone numbers, addresses, ids, card numbers, dates of birth, free text, containers) become stand-ins like <PERSON_1> before a prompt or a tool result leaves the server, and are swapped back in what people see. Each field is worked out from its name, type and a sample of its values; fields it is unsure of count as personal. marked is there when an administrator set the field. through names the hosted file whose switch applies, when it is not this file's own (a file whose fields show here). sample is left out when there is no layout to draw it from; its stand-ins are forgotten once drawn.

<a id="admin-ai-post-tabularius-admin-v1-pii-database"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/pii/{database}`

Turns personal data isolation on or off for a file.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | path | string | yes | Hosted file, any case (404 "No such hosted file"). |
| `on` | body | boolean | yes | true or false (400 "Send {"on": true} or {"on": false}" otherwise). |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/pii/Contacts
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "on": true
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "on": true,
  "tables": [
    {
      "table": "Contacts",
      "fields": [
        {
          "field": "Name",
          "pii": true,
          "why": "its name says it holds a person's name"
        },
        {
          "field": "Status",
          "pii": false,
          "why": "it holds a few repeated values (3), like a category",
          "marked": true
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "sample": {
    "layout": "Contact List",
    "records": [
      {
        "recordId": 1,
        "fieldData": {
          "Name": "<PERSON_1>",
          "Status": "Active"
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

The answer is the same as GET's. Turning it off forgets the stand-ins kept for the file. The change is logged as a security event and in the server's log.

<a id="admin-ai-post-tabularius-admin-v1-pii-database-field"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/pii/{database}/field`

Marks one field as personal, as not personal, or back to what the server works out.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | path | string | yes | Hosted file, any case (404 "No such hosted file"). |
| `table` | body | string | yes | The table. |
| `field` | body | string | yes | The field (400 "No field Table::Field" when there is none). |
| `pii` | body | boolean | yes | true for personal, false for not, null to go back to the worked-out answer (400 "Send {"table", "field", "pii": true, false or null}" otherwise). |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/pii/Contacts/field
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "table": "Contacts",
  "field": "Status",
  "pii": false
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "on": true,
  "tables": [
    {
      "table": "Contacts",
      "fields": [
        {
          "field": "Name",
          "pii": true,
          "why": "its name says it holds a person's name"
        },
        {
          "field": "Status",
          "pii": false,
          "why": "it holds a few repeated values (3), like a category",
          "marked": true
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "sample": {
    "layout": "Contact List",
    "records": [
      {
        "recordId": 1,
        "fieldData": {
          "Name": "<PERSON_1>",
          "Status": "Active"
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

The answer is the same as GET's, without a sample. The change is logged as a security event. Any other method on /tabularius/admin/v1/pii/ is 405.

<a id="admin-ai-post-tabularius-admin-v1-solutions-plan"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/solutions/plan`

Asks the assistant to plan a new file from a description: the design changes it would make, tried on an empty scratch file and with its starter scripts dry-run. Nothing is created.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it). The assistant must be on (503 "The AI assistant is off on this server (start it with --ai and an API key)" otherwise), and it counts against the server's daily token limit and the monthly budget.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | body | string | yes | The new file's name: letters, digits, spaces, - and _ (400 otherwise, and when a file or a waiting .fmp12 already has it). |
| `description` | body | string | yes | What the solution is for (400 "Say what the solution is for" when empty); up to 4,000 characters are used. |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/solutions/plan
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "Studio CRM",
  "description": "Track companies, contacts and deals for a small design studio, with a pipeline view of deals by stage."
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "summary": "A CRM with companies, contacts and deals, a pipeline layout and three starter scripts.",
  "changes": [
    {
      "op": "createTable",
      "name": "Companies"
    },
    {
      "op": "createTable",
      "name": "Contacts"
    },
    {
      "op": "createTable",
      "name": "Deals"
    }
  ],
  "preview": [
    "New table Companies: CompanyID, Name, Created, Modified",
    "New table Contacts: ContactID, CompanyID, Name, Email",
    "New table Deals: DealID, CompanyID, Stage, Value",
    "New layout Pipeline (list of Deals)"
  ],
  "dryRuns": [
    {
      "script": "New Deal for Company",
      "run": {
        "note": "what the script did on the scratch file: its result, error and the records it changed"
      }
    }
  ],
  "layouts": [
    {
      "note": "each new or changed layout as it would be drawn"
    }
  ]
}
```

The model may be asked up to three times to fix a plan that doesn't apply or is too long; a plan that still doesn't is 502 with the reason. The changes are in the same form as the design tools take, and are sent back to POST /tabularius/admin/v1/solutions as they are, or edited first. dryRuns and layouts are left out when there are none (or when script dry runs are off). A failure reaching the model is 502.

<a id="admin-ai-post-tabularius-admin-v1-solutions"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/solutions`

Makes a new hosted file from a plan's changes, all or nothing.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | body | string | yes | The new file's name, as for the plan (400 if a file already has it). |
| `changes` | body | array of object | yes | The plan's changes (400 "Send the plan's changes" when empty). |
| `password` | body | string | no | A password for the file's Admin account. Without it the account has none. |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/solutions
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "Studio CRM",
  "changes": [
    {
      "op": "createTable",
      "name": "Companies"
    }
  ]
}
```

Response `201`:

```json
{
  "database": "Studio CRM",
  "changes": 1
}
```

If a change fails part way, no file is left behind (400 "The plan didn't apply, so no file was made: …"). The file is hosted at once and the creation is written to the server's log. This route does not need the assistant.

<a id="admin-ai-post-tabularius-admin-v1-mcp-tokens"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/mcp/tokens`

Makes an API token for AI apps (surface fmmcp) for an account, or for a new AI agent account; the token is in this answer only.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | body | string | yes | Hosted file (400 "No hosted file is named …"). |
| `account` | body | string | no | An active account of the file; or give agent. |
| `agent` | body | object | no | {name, privilegeSet, needsApproval}: adds an AI agent account first (no password, never [Full Access]; needsApproval holds its writes for a person to approve). |
| `label` | body | string | no | What it is for (default "AI app: <account> in <file>"; up to 200 characters). |
| `days` | body | number | no | Days until it expires, 1 to 3650; none for no expiry. |
| `readOnly` | body | boolean | no | The token can only read. |
| `layouts` | body | array of string | no | Only these layouts. |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/mcp/tokens
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "database": "Invoices",
  "account": "Clerk",
  "label": "Claude Desktop",
  "days": 30
}
```

Response `201`:

```json
{
  "id": "1a2b3c4d5e6f",
  "account": "Clerk",
  "readOnly": false,
  "created": "2026-10-13T09:05:00.000Z",
  "label": "Claude Desktop",
  "expires": "2026-11-12T09:05:00.000Z",
  "surfaces": [
    "fmmcp"
  ],
  "database": "Invoices",
  "token": "ohbt_1a2b3c4d5e6f.Zx8kQ2vN7pR4tY1wB6mC3hJ9sD5fG0aLe"
}
```

When the account's privilege set lacks the fmmcp extended privilege the token is still made, with warning: "The \"…\" privilege set doesn't have the fmmcp extended privilege (AI access), so this token can't be used until it does". An unknown account, bad days or a [Full Access] agent is 400 with the reason.

```http
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
```

<a id="admin-logs"></a>

## Admin console: server logs

The server's logs, as FileMaker Server keeps them: Event, Access, ScriptEvent, fmdapi and Admin (each console or Admin API change other than an upload piece, with its status). Each log rolls over into an older half (<name>-old.log). Sign in as for every console call; these are GET only (other methods are 404). An unknown log name is 404 {"error": "not found"}.

Source: `packages/server/src/admin.ts`

| Method | Path | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/logs`](#admin-logs-get-tabularius-admin-v1-logs) | The logs and their sizes, with their older halves. |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/logs/{name}`](#admin-logs-get-tabularius-admin-v1-logs-name) | A log's entries, newest first, from it and its older half, filtered. |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/logs/{name}/download`](#admin-logs-get-tabularius-admin-v1-logs-name-download) | The log file itself, tab-separated, as a download. |

<a id="admin-logs-get-tabularius-admin-v1-logs"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/admin/v1/logs`

The logs and their sizes, with their older halves.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in.

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/admin/v1/logs
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
```

<a id="admin-logs-get-tabularius-admin-v1-logs-name"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/admin/v1/logs/{name}`

A log's entries, newest first, from it and its older half, filtered.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | path | string | yes | Event, Access, ScriptEvent, fmdapi or Admin. |
| `from` | query | string | no | Earliest time: milliseconds since 1970 or a date the server can read. |
| `to` | query | string | no | Latest time, the same way. |
| `type` | query | string | no | Information, Warning or Error. |
| `q` | query | string | no | Text in the entry (any case). |
| `limit` | query | number | no | At most 5000 (default 500). |

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/admin/v1/logs/Access?type=Warning&limit=1
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "entries": [
    {
      "at": "2026-10-13 08:11:40.512 +0000",
      "type": "Warning",
      "source": "192.168.1.20",
      "message": "Ann could not sign in to Invoices: wrong account or password"
    }

  "more": false
}
```

### `GET /tabularius/admin/v1/logs/{name}/download`

The log file itself, tab-separated, as a download.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | path | string | yes | Event, Access, ScriptEvent, fmdapi or Admin. |
| `old` | query | string | no | 1 for the older half (<name>-old.log). |

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/admin/v1/logs/Access/download
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
```

Response `200`:

```text
(text/tab-separated-values, Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="Access.log": one entry per line, time, type, source and message separated by tabs; empty when the file doesn't exist)
```

<a id="scim"></a>

## Provisioning from an identity provider (SCIM 2.0)

SCIM 2.0 (RFC 7643/7644) for one hosted file at /tabularius/scim/v2/databases/{database}, so an identity provider such as Okta or Microsoft Entra ID adds, deactivates and removes people and moves them between privilege sets. A User is an external account named by the person's email (the userName), with no password; single sign-on matches them to it. A Group is one of the file's privilege sets, never [Full Access]; a member gets that set (one set per account, the last group added wins) and on removal gets another group's set, else the file's default provisioning set, else none. Accounts with a password, AI agents, file accounts and accounts an admin gave full access are never touched (409, or 403 for a change); another external account named by the email is taken over. Groups can't be created, renamed or deleted: POST links to the set of that name, DELETE takes the set from the people SCIM gave it to. Filters: attribute eq "value" (Users: userName, externalId, id, emails.value; Groups: displayName, id); paging with startIndex and count (at most 200). Responses are application/scim+json; errors are the SCIM error body with status, scimType and detail. Changes are in the file's security log as made by "SCIM". The admin console issues and revokes the file's token and sets the default set.

Source: `packages/server/src/scim.ts`

| Method | Path | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET, POST | [`/tabularius/scim/v2/databases/{database}/Users`](#scim-get-post-tabularius-scim-v2-databases-database-users) | Lists the people SCIM manages (GET, with ?filter=userName eq "…"), or adds one (POST, 201 with a Location). |
| GET, PUT, PATCH, DELETE | [`/tabularius/scim/v2/databases/{database}/Users/{id}`](#scim-get-put-patch-delete-tabularius-scim-v2-databases-database-users-id) | Reads, replaces (PUT), changes (PATCH, a PatchOp) or removes (DELETE, 204) one person. active=false deactivates the account and signs it out; Tabularius revokes its API tokens, including person-bound tokens delegated through a shared mapping. Reactivation does not restore those tokens. DELETE leaves the account deactivated with no set, so no domain or group signs them in again. |
| GET, POST | [`/tabularius/scim/v2/databases/{database}/Groups`](#scim-get-post-tabularius-scim-v2-databases-database-groups) | Lists the privilege sets a provider may use as groups (GET, with ?filter=displayName eq "…" and ?excludedAttributes=members), or links a group to the set of its name (POST, 201). |
| GET, PUT, PATCH, DELETE | [`/tabularius/scim/v2/databases/{database}/Groups/{id}`](#scim-get-put-patch-delete-tabularius-scim-v2-databases-database-groups-id) | Reads one group, replaces its members (PUT), adds or removes members (PATCH), or takes the set from everyone SCIM gave it to (DELETE, 204; the set itself stays). |
| GET | [`/tabularius/scim/v2/databases/{database}/{discovery}`](#scim-get-tabularius-scim-v2-databases-database-discovery) | The discovery documents: ServiceProviderConfig, ResourceTypes[/{name}] and Schemas[/{urn}]. |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/scim`](#scim-get-tabularius-admin-v1-scim) | Whether provisioning is on for a file, since when, its default set, how many people it manages, the path to give the provider and the sets it may use. |
| POST, DELETE | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/scim/token`](#scim-post-delete-tabularius-admin-v1-scim-token) | POST turns provisioning on with a new token (shown once; the old one stops working); DELETE (?database=) turns it off. The accounts it made stay. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/scim/settings`](#scim-post-tabularius-admin-v1-scim-settings) | Sets (or with null clears) the privilege set people get when no group gives them one. |

<a id="scim-get-post-tabularius-scim-v2-databases-database-users"></a>

### `GET, POST /tabularius/scim/v2/databases/{database}/Users`

Lists the people SCIM manages (GET, with ?filter=userName eq "…"), or adds one (POST, 201 with a Location).

**Permissions:** The file's provisioning token: Authorization: Bearer ohsc_…, issued in the admin console (POST /tabularius/admin/v1/scim/token). Anything else, or a file that isn't hosted, answers 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | path | string | yes | Hosted file, any case. |
| `filter` | query | string | no | attribute eq "value": userName (any case), externalId, id or emails.value. |
| `userName` | body | string | yes | POST: the person's email address; it names the account. |
| `active` | body | boolean | no | POST: false adds the account deactivated. "True"/"False" are accepted. |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/scim/v2/databases/Invoices/Users
Authorization: Bearer ohsc_Qm9hcmQQm9hcmQQm9hcmQQm9hcmQQm9hcmQQm9hcmQ
Content-Type: application/scim+json

{
  "schemas": [
    "urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User"
  ],
  "userName": "pat@example.com",
  "name": {
    "givenName": "Pat",
    "familyName": "Lee"
  },
  "active": true,
  "externalId": "00u1"
}
```

Response `201`:

```json
{
  "schemas": [
    "urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User"
  ],
  "id": "2f0c6a38-6a0e-4c1b-9d55-3a6c1d2b7e10",
  "externalId": "00u1",
  "userName": "pat@example.com",
  "name": {
    "givenName": "Pat",
    "familyName": "Lee"
  },
  "active": true,
  "groups": [],
  "meta": {
    "resourceType": "User",
    "created": "2026-10-14T15:00:00.000Z",
    "lastModified": "2026-10-14T15:00:00.000Z",
    "location": "https://files.example.com/tabularius/scim/v2/databases/Invoices/Users/2f0c6a38-6a0e-4c1b-9d55-3a6c1d2b7e10"
  }
}
```

A new account has no privilege set (it opens nothing) until a group gives one, unless the file has a default provisioning set. A name already used by an account with its own sign-in answers 409 scimType "uniqueness"; a userName that isn't an email answers 400.

<a id="scim-get-put-patch-delete-tabularius-scim-v2-databases-database-users-id"></a>

### `GET, PUT, PATCH, DELETE /tabularius/scim/v2/databases/{database}/Users/{id}`

Reads, replaces (PUT), changes (PATCH, a PatchOp) or removes (DELETE, 204) one person. active=false deactivates the account and signs it out; Tabularius revokes its API tokens, including person-bound tokens delegated through a shared mapping. Reactivation does not restore those tokens. DELETE leaves the account deactivated with no set, so no domain or group signs them in again.

**Permissions:** The file's provisioning token: Authorization: Bearer ohsc_…, issued in the admin console (POST /tabularius/admin/v1/scim/token). Anything else, or a file that isn't hosted, answers 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | path | string | yes | Hosted file, any case. |
| `id` | path | string | yes | The id SCIM gave the user. |

**Example:**

```http
PATCH /tabularius/scim/v2/databases/Invoices/Users/2f0c6a38-6a0e-4c1b-9d55-3a6c1d2b7e10
Authorization: Bearer ohsc_Qm9hcmQQm9hcmQQm9hcmQQm9hcmQQm9hcmQQm9hcmQ
Content-Type: application/scim+json

{
  "schemas": [
    "urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"
  ],
  "Operations": [
    {
      "op": "replace",
      "value": {
        "active": false
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "schemas": [
    "urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User"
  ],
  "id": "2f0c6a38-6a0e-4c1b-9d55-3a6c1d2b7e10",
  "externalId": "00u1",
  "userName": "pat@example.com",
  "name": {
    "givenName": "Pat",
    "familyName": "Lee"
  },
  "active": false,
  "groups": [],
  "meta": {
    "resourceType": "User",
    "created": "2026-10-14T15:00:00.000Z",
    "lastModified": "2026-10-14T15:05:00.000Z",
    "location": "https://files.example.com/tabularius/scim/v2/databases/Invoices/Users/2f0c6a38-6a0e-4c1b-9d55-3a6c1d2b7e10"
  }
}
```

PATCH takes Okta's and Entra's spellings: ops in any case, a value object without a path, paths such as active, displayName, name.givenName and emails[type eq "work"].value, and "True"/"False". Attributes the file doesn't keep are accepted and dropped. userName can't change (400 scimType "mutability"). A person whose own account is deactivated can't sign in through their email domain or a group either.

<a id="scim-get-post-tabularius-scim-v2-databases-database-groups"></a>

### `GET, POST /tabularius/scim/v2/databases/{database}/Groups`

Lists the privilege sets a provider may use as groups (GET, with ?filter=displayName eq "…" and ?excludedAttributes=members), or links a group to the set of its name (POST, 201).

**Permissions:** The file's provisioning token: Authorization: Bearer ohsc_…, issued in the admin console (POST /tabularius/admin/v1/scim/token). Anything else, or a file that isn't hosted, answers 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | path | string | yes | Hosted file, any case. |
| `filter` | query | string | no | displayName eq "…" (any case) or id eq "…". |
| `excludedAttributes` | query | string | no | members leaves the member lists out. |

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/scim/v2/databases/Invoices/Groups?filter=displayName%20eq%20%22Sales%22
Authorization: Bearer ohsc_Qm9hcmQQm9hcmQQm9hcmQQm9hcmQQm9hcmQQm9hcmQ
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "schemas": [
    "urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:ListResponse"
  ],
  "totalResults": 1,
  "startIndex": 1,
  "itemsPerPage": 1,
  "Resources": [
    {
      "schemas": [
        "urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:Group"
      ],
      "id": "U2FsZXM",
      "displayName": "Sales",
      "members": [
        {
          "value": "2f0c6a38-6a0e-4c1b-9d55-3a6c1d2b7e10",
          "display": "pat@example.com",
          "$ref": "https://files.example.com/tabularius/scim/v2/databases/Invoices/Users/2f0c6a38-6a0e-4c1b-9d55-3a6c1d2b7e10"
        }
      ],
      "meta": {
        "resourceType": "Group",
        "location": "https://files.example.com/tabularius/scim/v2/databases/Invoices/Groups/U2FsZXM"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Members are only the people SCIM manages. POST with a name that is no privilege set, or a full-access one, answers 400.

<a id="scim-get-put-patch-delete-tabularius-scim-v2-databases-database-groups-id"></a>

### `GET, PUT, PATCH, DELETE /tabularius/scim/v2/databases/{database}/Groups/{id}`

Reads one group, replaces its members (PUT), adds or removes members (PATCH), or takes the set from everyone SCIM gave it to (DELETE, 204; the set itself stays).

**Permissions:** The file's provisioning token: Authorization: Bearer ohsc_…, issued in the admin console (POST /tabularius/admin/v1/scim/token). Anything else, or a file that isn't hosted, answers 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | path | string | yes | Hosted file, any case. |
| `id` | path | string | yes | The group id: the privilege set's name, base64url. |

**Example:**

```http
PATCH /tabularius/scim/v2/databases/Invoices/Groups/U2FsZXM
Authorization: Bearer ohsc_Qm9hcmQQm9hcmQQm9hcmQQm9hcmQQm9hcmQQm9hcmQ
Content-Type: application/scim+json

{
  "schemas": [
    "urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"
  ],
  "Operations": [
    {
      "op": "add",
      "path": "members",
      "value": [
        {
          "value": "2f0c6a38-6a0e-4c1b-9d55-3a6c1d2b7e10"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "schemas": [
    "urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:Group"
  ],
  "id": "U2FsZXM",
  "displayName": "Sales",
  "members": [
    {
      "value": "2f0c6a38-6a0e-4c1b-9d55-3a6c1d2b7e10",
      "display": "pat@example.com",
      "$ref": "https://files.example.com/tabularius/scim/v2/databases/Invoices/Users/2f0c6a38-6a0e-4c1b-9d55-3a6c1d2b7e10"
    }
  ],
  "meta": {
    "resourceType": "Group",
    "location": "https://files.example.com/tabularius/scim/v2/databases/Invoices/Groups/U2FsZXM"
  }
}
```

Removal takes Okta's path form members[value eq "…"] and Entra's value list. A group can't be renamed (400 scimType "mutability").

The discovery documents: ServiceProviderConfig, ResourceTypes[/{name}] and Schemas[/{urn}].

<a id="scim-get-tabularius-admin-v1-scim"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/admin/v1/scim`

Whether provisioning is on for a file, since when, its default set, how many people it manages, the path to give the provider and the sets it may use.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | query | string | yes | Hosted file, any case. |

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/admin/v1/scim?database=Invoices
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "database": "Invoices",
  "on": true,
  "defaultPrivilegeSet": "Readers",
  "path": "/tabularius/scim/v2/databases/Invoices",
  "users": 0,
  "privilegeSets": [
    "Sales",
    "Readers"
  ]
}
```

An unknown file answers 404 {"error": "…"}.

<a id="scim-post-delete-tabularius-admin-v1-scim-token"></a>

### `POST, DELETE /tabularius/admin/v1/scim/token`

POST turns provisioning on with a new token (shown once; the old one stops working); DELETE (?database=) turns it off. The accounts it made stay.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | body | string | yes | Hosted file, any case (DELETE: ?database=). |
| `defaultPrivilegeSet` | body | string | no | POST: the set people get when no group gives one; never a full-access set (400). |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/scim/token
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "database": "Invoices"
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "database": "Invoices",
  "on": true,
  "path": "/tabularius/scim/v2/databases/Invoices",
  "users": 0,
  "privilegeSets": [
    "Sales",
    "Readers"
  ],
  "token": "ohsc_Qm9hcmQQm9hcmQQm9hcmQQm9hcmQQm9hcmQQm9hcmQ"
}
```

Only the token's hash is kept, in the file. Issuing and revoking are in the security log.

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/scim/settings`

Sets (or with null clears) the privilege set people get when no group gives them one.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/scim/settings

{
  "database": "Invoices",
```

```json
{
  "database": "Invoices",
  "on": true,
  "defaultPrivilegeSet": "Readers",

  "users": 0,
```
