<a id="admin-sync"></a>

## Admin console: keeping a file in step with a FileMaker Server copy

The console's Sync page: a hosted file's saved setup (the FileMaker Server, its file, the account and each table's layout, UUID and modification-timestamp fields), a check (a dry run), the conflicts it found, applying the result, and the log of what was sent and brought in. Sign in as for every console call; all but GET need x-tabularius-admin: 1. Nothing is sent to FileMaker or changed here without the setup allowing it (allowWrites, allowPulls) and the request asking for it (write, pull). The FileMaker password is never saved in the setup: it is read from a file in the server's secrets folder (the setup's passwordFile; <hosted folder>/.openhbam-secrets, or TABULARIUS_SYNC_SECRETS), or from TABULARIUS_FMS_PASSWORD for a server the operator named in TABULARIUS_SYNC_HOSTS, or typed for one run. With TABULARIUS_SYNC_HOSTS set (host or host:port, comma separated) no other server is reached; without it this machine and link-local addresses are refused. FileMaker's refusals are reported in FileMaker's words for the error code, never the other server's text, and a failed connection says only that it failed. A capture-only file never syncs. Errors are {"error": "…"}: 400 a bad setup or request, 403 not allowed by the setup, 404 no such file or setup, 409 a sync of that file is already running, 502 FileMaker Server could not be reached or refused the sign-in.

Source: `packages/server/src/admin.ts`

| Method | Path | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/sync`](#admin-sync-get-tabularius-admin-v1-sync) | Every file with a sync set up: its setup, whether a run is going, the latest check or apply, and whether a password is available without typing one. |
| GET, PUT, DELETE | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/sync/{database}`](#admin-sync-get-put-delete-tabularius-admin-v1-sync-database) | GET one file's setup and latest run; PUT saves its setup (replacing the old one); DELETE forgets it. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/sync/{database}/check`](#admin-sync-post-tabularius-admin-v1-sync-database-check) | A dry run: reads both sides, writes to neither, and says what a sync would send and bring in and which records conflict. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/sync/{database}/apply`](#admin-sync-post-tabularius-admin-v1-sync-database-apply) | Sends this file's changes to FileMaker (write) and/or brings FileMaker's changes here (pull). Any conflict not settled by a choice below stops it with nothing changed. |
| GET | [`/tabularius/admin/v1/sync/{database}/log`](#admin-sync-get-tabularius-admin-v1-sync-database-log) | The log of what was sent to FileMaker and brought in, oldest first: each change is recorded before it is made and finished after, with the field names (never the values). |

<a id="admin-sync-get-tabularius-admin-v1-sync"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/admin/v1/sync`

Every file with a sync set up: its setup, whether a run is going, the latest check or apply, and whether a password is available without typing one.

<a id="admin-sync-get-put-delete-tabularius-admin-v1-sync-database"></a>

### `GET, PUT, DELETE /tabularius/admin/v1/sync/{database}`

GET one file's setup and latest run; PUT saves its setup (replacing the old one); DELETE forgets it.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | path | string | yes | Hosted file (404 when it isn't hosted or, for GET and DELETE, has no setup; 400 for a capture-only file). |
| `server` | body | string | yes | PUT: the FileMaker Server, https://host (a bare host is read as https; plain http only for this machine). |
| `database` | body | string | yes | PUT: the file's name on that server. |
| `user` | body | string | yes | PUT: the FileMaker account (needs the fmrest privilege and to see every record in the tables). |
| `tables` | body | array | yes | PUT: one { localTable, remoteLayout?, uuidField, modTimestampField, policy? } per table (the layout defaults to the table's name; policy is flag, filemaker-wins, tabularius-wins or newer-wins). |
| `passwordFile` | body | string | no | PUT: the name of a file in the secrets folder holding the account's password, read at each run (400 for a path outside that folder; links out of it are not followed). |
| `insecure` | body | boolean | no | PUT: accept a new FileMaker Server's self-signed certificate. |
| `allowWrites` | body | boolean | no | PUT: the console may send this file's changes to FileMaker (default false). |
| `allowPulls` | body | boolean | no | PUT: the console may change this file with FileMaker's changes (default false). |
| `allowContainers` | body | boolean | no | PUT: a run may also move container files, up to 50 MB each: a pull brings them (fetched only from the server signed in to) and a write sends them (default false). |

**Example:**

```http
PUT /tabularius/admin/v1/sync/Invoices
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "server": "https://fms.example.com",
  "database": "Invoices",
  "user": "sync",
  "passwordFile": "fms-password",
  "tables": [
    {
      "localTable": "Invoices",
      "uuidField": "uuid",
      "modTimestampField": "modified"
    }
  ]
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "database": "Invoices",
  "running": false,
  "passwordSaved": true,
  "setup": {
    "server": "https://fms.example.com",
    "database": "Invoices",
    "user": "sync",
    "passwordFile": "fms-password",
    "tables": [
      {
        "localTable": "Invoices",
        "remoteLayout": "Invoices",
        "uuidField": "uuid",
        "modTimestampField": "modified"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

An unknown setting is 400. Database names use the hosted file’s canonical spelling, including setups, schedules, status and locks. PUT and DELETE return 409 during a run. Destination (server/database) or table mapping changes use a separate sync baseline: records from the previous destination cannot be treated as deletions in the new one. Legacy unscoped history is not reused. Matching saved case aliases are consolidated; conflicting aliases require a fresh PUT. The setup is kept in .openhbam-sync.json in the folder, readable by its owner only.

<a id="admin-sync-post-tabularius-admin-v1-sync-database-check"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sync/{database}/check`

A dry run: reads both sides, writes to neither, and says what a sync would send and bring in and which records conflict.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | path | string | yes | Hosted file with a setup. |
| `password` | body | string | no | The FileMaker account's password for this run only (never kept); without it the setup's passwordFile, or TABULARIUS_FMS_PASSWORD when the server is one TABULARIUS_SYNC_HOSTS names (400 when neither is there). |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sync/Invoices/check
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "at": "2026-10-15T01:00:00.000Z",
  "trigger": "manual",
  "interrupted": 0,
  "moreConflicts": 0,
  "runId": "3f6c…",
  "tables": [
    {
      "localTable": "Invoices",
      "layout": "Invoices",
      "created": 1,
      "updated": 0,
      "deleted": 0,
      "adopted": 4,
      "heldDeletes": 0,
      "pulled": {
        "created": 0,
        "updated": 2,
        "deleted": 0
      },
      "heldPullDeletes": 0,
      "pendingPulls": 0,
      "pendingPushes": 0,
      "unsentFields": [],
      "failed": []
    }
  ],
  "conflicts": [
    {
      "table": "Invoices",
      "uuid": "8C1E…",
      "reviewToken": "opaque-token-from-check",
      "kind": "both-changed",
      "clashes": [
        {
          "field": "Status",
          "here": "Paid",
          "filemaker": "Open"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "refused": "1 conflict held for review, so nothing would be written: Invoices 8C1E…: changed on both sides (Status)."
}
```

kind is both-changed, deleted-here (changed on FileMaker) or deleted-on-filemaker (changed here). At most 500 conflicts are listed; moreConflicts counts the rest. Each conflict includes an authenticated reviewToken binding the setup and both record versions/deletion states; return it unchanged with the choice in apply. Tokens are valid only in the issuing server process; check again after a restart. A check logs nothing.

<a id="admin-sync-post-tabularius-admin-v1-sync-database-apply"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sync/{database}/apply`

Sends this file's changes to FileMaker (write) and/or brings FileMaker's changes here (pull). Any conflict not settled by a choice below stops it with nothing changed.

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in. Not a GET, so it also needs the header x-tabularius-admin: 1 (403 "missing x-tabularius-admin header" without it).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | path | string | yes | Hosted file with a setup. |
| `write` | body | boolean | no | Send to FileMaker (403 unless the setup has allowWrites). |
| `pull` | body | boolean | no | Change this file from FileMaker (403 unless the setup has allowPulls). One of write and pull is required (400). |
| `containers` | body | boolean | no | Also move container files: a pull brings them, a write sends them (403 unless the setup has allowContainers). |
| `allowDeletes` | body | boolean | no | Carry deletions out too (otherwise they are held and counted). |
| `keepRelated` | body | boolean | no | With `pull`: a deletion brought here deletes only that record, not the records this file’s “delete related records” relationships would delete with it (the report counts those otherwise, as `pulled.related`). |
| `resolutions` | body | array | no | One { table, uuid, keep, reviewToken } per conflict: keep "mine" sends this file's version to FileMaker (needs write), "theirs" brings FileMaker's here (needs pull). Return the opaque reviewToken from that conflict in /check. It binds the setup identity and both record versions, including deletion states. Missing tokens are 400; a stale, manufactured or altered token refuses the entire run before record writes, even if the UUID still conflicts. Reviewed local states are revalidated after awaits and before their writes; a change during apply refuses further record writes, while completed writes remain recorded. Tokens expire when the issuing server process restarts. Check and review again. |
| `release` | body | boolean | no | Let tables an earlier run held back (their UUID field would not keep the key) write again first. |
| `password` | body | string | no | The FileMaker account's password for this run only (never kept). |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sync/Invoices/apply
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
x-tabularius-admin: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "write": true,
  "pull": true,
  "resolutions": [
    {
      "table": "Invoices",
      "uuid": "8C1E…",
      "keep": "theirs",
      "reviewToken": "opaque-token-from-check"
    }
  ]
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "at": "2026-10-15T01:05:00.000Z",
  "trigger": "apply",
  "interrupted": 0,
  "moreConflicts": 0,
  "runId": "a91d…",
  "tables": [
    {
      "localTable": "Invoices",
      "layout": "Invoices",
      "created": 1,
      "updated": 0,
      "deleted": 0,
      "adopted": 4,
      "heldDeletes": 0,
      "pulled": {
        "created": 0,
        "updated": 3,
        "deleted": 0
      },
      "heldPullDeletes": 0,
      "pendingPulls": 0,
      "pendingPushes": 0,
      "unsentFields": [],
      "failed": []
    }
  ],
  "conflicts": []
}
```

The answer has the same shape as a check's, with refused when nothing was changed because of a conflict and stopped when the run ended early (run it again to carry on); failed lists records one at a time that were refused. Each change is in the log. Applies require an open database (409 while paused or closed). Pausing or closing during an awaited request cancels further local writes, including bookkeeping, even if the file is reopened. A remote request already in flight may finish; its unfinished audit attempt is reconciled on the next run.

<a id="admin-sync-get-tabularius-admin-v1-sync-database-log"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/admin/v1/sync/{database}/log`

The log of what was sent to FileMaker and brought in, oldest first: each change is recorded before it is made and finished after, with the field names (never the values).

**Permissions:** Admin console: a console sign-in (the tabularius_admin cookie from POST /tabularius/admin/v1/sign-in), or the admin password by HTTP Basic (any user name), or the folder's local channel token in x-tabularius-local (Tabularius commands on the server machine). With no admin password set, only requests from this machine (loopback) are let in.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | path | string | yes | Hosted file with a setup. |
| `run` | query | string | no | Only that run's rows (a runId from a check or apply). |
| `limit` | query | number | no | Default 200, maximum 10,000, also with run. Without run, the most recent rows; with run, the first rows of that run. Nonpositive or invalid values use the default; positive fractions are floored (minimum 1). |

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/admin/v1/sync/Invoices/log?limit=2
Cookie: tabularius_admin=6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e6b1f0c2e
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "log": [
    {
      "id": 41,
      "runId": "a91d…",
      "at": "2026-10-15T01:05:00.100Z",
      "table": "Invoices",
      "layout": "Invoices",
      "uuid": "5B07…",
      "op": "create",
      "status": "ok",
      "remoteRecordId": "812",
      "modIdBefore": null,
      "modIdAfter": "1",
      "fields": [
        "uuid",
        "Status",
        "Total"
      ],
      "detail": null
    },
    {
      "id": 42,
      "runId": "a91d…",
      "at": "2026-10-15T01:05:00.300Z",
      "table": "Invoices",
      "layout": "Invoices",
      "uuid": "8C1E…",
      "op": "pull-update",
      "status": "ok",
      "remoteRecordId": "77",
      "modIdBefore": "3",
      "modIdAfter": "4",
      "fields": [
        "Status"
      ],
      "detail": null
    }
  ]
}
```

op is create, update or delete (sent to FileMaker), pull-create, pull-update or pull-delete (made here), adopt (the same on both sides, recorded) or run. status is ok, noop, failed, interrupted (a run that died mid-change) or, for run rows, started, finished, refused or stopped.

<a id="server"></a>

## Server

The small routes the server answers itself, before and after the other handlers. None of them needs a sign-in: container links are protected by their signature instead. A path nothing answers gets a bare 404, or an error page when a browser asks for HTML; an unexpected failure gets 500 the same way.

Source: `packages/server/src/index.ts`

| Method | Path | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | [`/tabularius/health`](#server-get-tabularius-health) | Says the server is serving, for load balancers and orchestrators. |
| GET, HEAD | [`/tabularius/containers/{database}/{id}/{name}`](#server-get-head-tabularius-containers-database-id-name) | Downloads a container field's file through the signed link the Data API and other APIs hand out. |
| GET | [`/docs`](#server-get-docs) | The index of the guides in docs/ (and docs/reference/), as an HTML page. |
| GET | [`/docs/{guide}`](#server-get-docs-guide) | One guide (docs/<guide>.md, or docs/reference/<name>.md) as an HTML page, for example /docs/connect-ai. |
| GET | [`/`](#server-get) | Names the server, and the files it hosts when the server lists them publicly. |

<a id="server-get-tabularius-health"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/health`

Says the server is serving, for load balancers and orchestrators.

**Permissions:** None. It says nothing about the hosted files.

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/health
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "status": "ok",
  "uptimeSeconds": 3600,
  "serverTime": "2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z"
}
```

Answered for any method, with cache-control: no-store.

<a id="server-get-head-tabularius-containers-database-id-name"></a>

### `GET, HEAD /tabularius/containers/{database}/{id}/{name}`

Downloads a container field's file through the signed link the Data API and other APIs hand out.

**Permissions:** None: the sig (and exp) query parameters are the credential. They are an HMAC of the file name, container id and expiry, made by the server; a wrong or expired signature is answered 404, as is an unknown file.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | path | string | yes | The hosted file's name (URL-encoded). |
| `id` | path | number | yes | The container id. |
| `name` | path | string | no | The file name, for the browser; ignored when matching. It may be left off: /tabularius/containers/{database}/{id} works too. |
| `sig` | query | string | yes | The link's signature. |
| `exp` | query | number | no | When the link stops working, in Unix seconds. Links last TABULARIUS_CONTAINER_TTL seconds (default 3600); with 0 they carry no exp and never expire. |
| `as` | query | string | no | The account the link was made for, when it was made for one. The signature covers the account's entry in the file, and the link stops working while that account is blocked or removed. |
| `thumb` | query | number | no | Asks for a thumbnail this many pixels across (16 to 1024; 256 when not a number) instead of the file. |
| `Range` | header | string | no | One byte range; answered 206 with Content-Range, or 416 when it can't be met. Several ranges in one header are not served as multipart: the whole file is sent with 200 (416 only when none of them can be met). |
| `If-None-Match` | header | string | no | The ETag from an earlier download; answered 304 when it matches. |

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/containers/Invoices/42/scan.pdf?sig=3q2Z8l0yQXk6m1t0kQf7m1j1y2l5p8r9s0t1u2v3w4x&exp=1791900000
```

Response `200`:

```text
(the file, with its Content-Type, Content-Disposition: inline, an ETag and Accept-Ranges: bytes)
```

A file stored outside the FileMaker file that was not copied over is answered 404 with "externally stored file not found: <path>". A thumbnail asked of a kind of file that has none is 404 "No thumbnail for this kind of file".

<a id="server-get-docs"></a>

### `GET /docs`

The index of the guides in docs/ (and docs/reference/), as an HTML page.

**Permissions:** None.

**Example:**

```http
GET /docs
```

Response `200`:

```text
(a page listing every guide, linked)
```

/docs/ is answered the same way. Guide pages carry X-Frame-Options: DENY, Referrer-Policy: no-referrer and a Content-Security-Policy that allows no scripts.

<a id="server-get-docs-guide"></a>

### `GET /docs/{guide}`

One guide (docs/<guide>.md, or docs/reference/<name>.md) as an HTML page, for example /docs/connect-ai.

**Permissions:** None.

**Example:**

```http
GET /docs/connect-ai
```

Response `200`:

```text
(the "Connect an AI app" guide as an HTML page)
```

A guide that does not exist is answered 404.

<a id="server-get"></a>

### `GET /`

Names the server, and the files it hosts when the server lists them publicly.

**Permissions:** None. The files are named only on a server started with --list-files-publicly (TABULARIUS_LIST_FILES_PUBLICLY); otherwise the answer is {"name": "tabularius"}, and the Data API and OData lists answer 404.

**Example:**

```http
GET /
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "name": "tabularius",
  "databases": [
    "Invoices",
    "Contacts"
  ]
}
```

Answered for any method. A request whose Accept header names text/html is answered by the web client instead (webclient.ts): 302 to /app/, whatever the method.

<a id="mcp"></a>

## MCP over HTTP

POST /mcp is a Model Context Protocol endpoint (Streamable HTTP) for AI apps. It is stateless: each request gets a fresh MCP server, no session id is issued, and answers come back as plain JSON-RPC (not an event stream). The tools, and what each checks, are in the MCP tools reference. A request no credential below accepts is answered 401 {"error":"unauthorized"} with WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="tabularius" (a browser asking for HTML with no Authorization header gets the 401 error page instead).

Source: `packages/server/src/index.ts`, `packages/server/src/mcp-tokens.ts`

| Method | Path | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| POST | [`/mcp`](#mcp-post-mcp) | Sends one MCP JSON-RPC message (initialize, tools/list, tools/call and so on) and returns its answer. |

<a id="mcp-post-mcp"></a>

### `POST /mcp`

Sends one MCP JSON-RPC message (initialize, tools/list, tools/call and so on) and returns its answer.

**Permissions:** One of, in this order: (1) HTTP Basic with an account and password: the account is checked in each file a tool touches (wrong password counts toward lockout) and its privilege set needs the fmmcp extended privilege there; files it can't use are left out of list_databases. (2) Bearer ohbt_… API token of a file (Manage Security, or the admin console's Connect an AI app): one account of that one file, its privilege set narrowed to the token's scope (read-only, layouts). It is not accepted when the token's surfaces leave out fmmcp, or the account may not sign in from the client's address. (3) Bearer ohm_… token made in the admin console (older AI app tokens): signs in as its account in its file only, until it expires; the privilege set needs fmmcp. (4) Otherwise the server administrator, with every file: when the server was started with --mcp-token (or TABULARIUS_MCP_TOKEN), only a Bearer token equal to it; without one, any request from loopback (127.0.0.1, ::1). Whoever it is, a file with AI turned off is refused to every MCP client, the administrator included.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Authorization` | header | string | no | Basic <account:password>, or Bearer <ohbt_ token \| ohm_ token \| --mcp-token>. Leave it off on loopback when no --mcp-token is set. |
| `Content-Type` | header | string | yes | application/json |
| `Accept` | header | string | yes | application/json, text/event-stream (the MCP transport wants both listed). |
| `MCP-Protocol-Version` | header | string | no | The MCP protocol version, e.g. 2025-06-18. |
| `jsonrpc` | body | string | yes | "2.0" |
| `id` | body | number | no | The request id, echoed in the answer. |
| `method` | body | string | yes | The MCP method, e.g. tools/list or tools/call. |
| `params` | body | object | no | For tools/call: {name, arguments}. |

**Example:**

```http
POST /mcp
Authorization: Basic Q2xlcms6c2VjcmV0
Content-Type: application/json
Accept: application/json, text/event-stream
MCP-Protocol-Version: 2025-06-18

{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "method": "tools/call",
  "params": {
    "name": "list_databases",
    "arguments": {}
  }
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "result": {
    "content": [
      {
        "type": "text",
        "text": "[\"Invoices\"]"
      }
    ]
  },
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1
}
```

A tool that is refused (no fmmcp, outside the account's privileges, AI turned off for the file) still answers 200, with a result whose isError is true and whose text says why. Other methods on /mcp go to the same MCP transport, which in this stateless mode has no use for them.

<a id="local-tls"></a>

## Trusting the local certificate authority

With --https local the server makes its own small certificate authority, constrained to this machine's names, and each device trusts it once. These routes say how and hand out the authority's certificate. They need no sign-in, as a device needs them before it can trust the server. When the server does not use its own authority, every one of them answers 404 "This server does not use its own certificate authority (start it with --https local)."; any other path under /tabularius/tls/ is a bare 404.

Source: `packages/server/src/local-tls.ts`, `packages/server/src/index.ts`

| Method | Path | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | [`/tabularius/tls/`](#local-tls-get-tabularius-tls) | A page saying how to trust the authority on iPhone and iPad, Mac, Windows and Android, with its SHA-256 fingerprint. |
| GET | [`/tabularius/tls/ca.cer`](#local-tls-get-tabularius-tls-ca-cer) | The authority's certificate, DER-encoded, as a download named tabularius-ca.cer. |
| GET | [`/tabularius/tls/tabularius.mobileconfig`](#local-tls-get-tabularius-tls-tabularius-mobileconfig) | The same certificate as a configuration profile for iPhone, iPad and Mac. |

<a id="local-tls-get-tabularius-tls"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/tls/`

A page saying how to trust the authority on iPhone and iPad, Mac, Windows and Android, with its SHA-256 fingerprint.

**Permissions:** None.

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/tls/
```

Response `200`:

```text
(the "Trust this server" HTML page)
```

/tabularius/tls (no slash) answers the same. The method is not checked.

<a id="local-tls-get-tabularius-tls-ca-cer"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/tls/ca.cer`

The authority's certificate, DER-encoded, as a download named tabularius-ca.cer.

**Permissions:** None.

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/tls/ca.cer
```

Response `200`:

```text
(the certificate, Content-Type: application/x-x509-ca-cert)
```

<a id="local-tls-get-tabularius-tls-tabularius-mobileconfig"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/tls/tabularius.mobileconfig`

The same certificate as a configuration profile for iPhone, iPad and Mac.

**Permissions:** None.

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/tls/tabularius.mobileconfig
```

Response `200`:

```text
(the profile, Content-Type: application/x-apple-aspen-config)
```

<a id="acme"></a>

## ACME challenge

With --https <name> the server gets its certificate from Let's Encrypt (or another ACME authority) and listens on plain HTTP, port 80 by default, so the authority can check it owns the name (the http-01 challenge). That listener answers only this route; every other request to it is redirected (301) to the same path on https, under a name the certificate covers.

Source: `packages/server/src/acme.ts`

| Method | Path | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | [`/.well-known/acme-challenge/{token}`](#acme-get-well-known-acme-challenge-token) | Answers the certificate authority's challenge with the key authorization for a token it is checking. |

<a id="acme-get-well-known-acme-challenge-token"></a>

### `GET /.well-known/acme-challenge/{token}`

Answers the certificate authority's challenge with the key authorization for a token it is checking.

**Permissions:** None. Only on the plain-HTTP port, and only while a certificate is being got.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `token` | path | string | yes | The challenge token (letters, digits, _ and -). |

**Example:**

```http
GET /.well-known/acme-challenge/LoqXcYV8q5ONbJQxbmR7SCTNo3tiAXDfowyjxAjEuX0
```

Response `200`:

```text
(the key authorization as text/plain: the token, a dot, and the account key's thumbprint)
```

A token not being checked is a bare 404. The method is not checked.

<a id="admin-api"></a>

## FileMaker Admin API

FileMaker Server's Admin API (v2) under /fmi/admin/api/v2, so tools written for it (fmcsadmin, Claris Connect, scripts) can manage tabularius: files, clients and FileMaker script schedules. Sign in with POST /user/auth and the admin password; every other route takes the token it returns as Authorization: Bearer. Tokens expire after 15 minutes idle or eight hours from issuance, even with continued use. Setting or changing the admin password invalidates existing tokens; sign in again for a new token. Every answer is {"response": …, "messages": [{"code": "0", "text": "OK"}]} with string codes; a missing or expired token is 401 code 9 "Access denied", an unknown route 404 code 3 "Unavailable command", a body that is not JSON 400 code 960. Like the admin console's own API (/tabularius/admin/), every request here other than GET, HEAD and PUT is written to the Admin log: method, path and status, never the body. FileMaker-compatible local timestamps keep their offset-free form. Read-only response fields serverHostTimeISO, connectTimeISO, lastRunISO, and nextRunISO give the same instant with the host's UTC offset, including during a repeated daylight-saving hour. An empty lastRun or nextRun has an empty ISO companion too.

Source: `packages/server/src/adminapi.ts`, `packages/server/src/index.ts`

| Method | Path | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| POST | [`/fmi/admin/api/v2/user/auth`](#admin-api-post-fmi-admin-api-v2-user-auth) | Signs in with the admin password and returns a token for the other routes. |
| DELETE | [`/fmi/admin/api/v2/user/auth/{token}`](#admin-api-delete-fmi-admin-api-v2-user-auth-token) | Signs out: the token named in the path stops working. |
| GET | [`/fmi/admin/api/v2/server/metadata`](#admin-api-get-fmi-admin-api-v2-server-metadata) | The server's name, id, address, Admin API version and local time. |
| GET | [`/fmi/admin/api/v2/server/status`](#admin-api-get-fmi-admin-api-v2-server-status) | Whether the server is running or was stopped through this API. |
| PATCH | [`/fmi/admin/api/v2/server/status`](#admin-api-patch-fmi-admin-api-v2-server-status) | STOPPED closes every open file (ending their sessions); RUNNING opens again the files it closed. |
| GET | [`/fmi/admin/api/v2/server/config/blocknewusers`](#admin-api-get-fmi-admin-api-v2-server-config-blocknewusers) | Whether new users are blocked. |
| PATCH | [`/fmi/admin/api/v2/server/config/blocknewusers`](#admin-api-patch-fmi-admin-api-v2-server-config-blocknewusers) | Blocks new users, or lets them in again. While blocked, no new session starts (web client and Data API sign-ins, identity-provider sign-ins, AI app sign-ins, SQL connections); sessions already open carry on, AI apps already signed in keep refreshing, and administrators still sign in. |
| GET | [`/fmi/admin/api/v2/server/config/{setting}`](#admin-api-get-fmi-admin-api-v2-server-config-setting) | FileMaker Server settings Tabularius has no counterpart for, answered as the values that describe it, so fmcsadmin's get serverconfig and get serverprefs work. |
| PATCH | [`/fmi/admin/api/v2/server/config/{setting}`](#admin-api-patch-fmi-admin-api-v2-server-config-setting) | Accepts the same values back (fmcsadmin's set serverconfig sends every one); a changed value is 400 code 21 "Not Supported: …" with the reason, an unknown key 400 code 960. |
| PATCH | [`/fmi/admin/api/v2/server/certificate/csr`](#admin-api-patch-fmi-admin-api-v2-server-certificate-csr) | Makes a new RSA key and a certificate request (fmcsadmin certificate create) to send to a certificate authority. The key is kept in the folder (.openhbam-tls/imported), encrypted with the password. |
| PATCH | [`/fmi/admin/api/v2/server/certificate/import`](#admin-api-patch-fmi-admin-api-v2-server-certificate-import) | Puts a certificate in place (fmcsadmin certificate import): checked, saved with its key in the folder, and named in the folder's settings for the next start. A server serving https by itself uses it for new connections at once. |
| DELETE | [`/fmi/admin/api/v2/server/certificate/delete`](#admin-api-delete-fmi-admin-api-v2-server-certificate-delete) | Removes the imported certificate, its key and any waiting request (fmcsadmin certificate delete); the folder's settings go back to the certificate they named before the first import (migrate-fms's, say), or to none, for the next start. |
| GET | [`/fmi/admin/api/v2/php/config`](#admin-api-get-fmi-admin-api-v2-php-config) | FileMaker Server's PHP publishing settings, answered as off: Tabularius has no PHP publishing. Also /xml/config ({enabled: true}: the XML interface at /fmi/xml is served, reads only) and /fmclients/httpstunneling ({enableHTTPSTunneling: false}). |
| GET | [`/fmi/admin/api/v2/plugins`](#admin-api-get-fmi-admin-api-v2-plugins) | Installed plug-ins (the server folder's plugins/), as fmcsadmin list plugins shows them; enabled when any hosted file has it turned on. |
| GET | [`/fmi/admin/api/v2/databases`](#admin-api-get-fmi-admin-api-v2-databases) | The hosted files, with their status, size, connected clients and the extended privileges their privilege sets use. |
| PATCH | [`/fmi/admin/api/v2/databases`](#admin-api-patch-fmi-admin-api-v2-databases) | Opens, closes, pauses or resumes every hosted file. |
| PATCH | [`/fmi/admin/api/v2/databases/{id}`](#admin-api-patch-fmi-admin-api-v2-databases-id) | Opens, closes, pauses or resumes one hosted file. |
| GET | [`/fmi/admin/api/v2/clients`](#admin-api-get-fmi-admin-api-v2-clients) | The connected clients: Data API and web client sessions. |
| DELETE | [`/fmi/admin/api/v2/clients/{id}`](#admin-api-delete-fmi-admin-api-v2-clients-id) | Disconnects a client: its session ends. |
| POST | [`/fmi/admin/api/v2/clients/{id}/message`](#admin-api-post-fmi-admin-api-v2-clients-id-message) | Sends a message to one client. |
| GET | [`/fmi/admin/api/v2/schedules`](#admin-api-get-fmi-admin-api-v2-schedules) | The script schedules. |
| POST | [`/fmi/admin/api/v2/schedules`](#admin-api-post-fmi-admin-api-v2-schedules) | Duplicates a schedule, named "<name> Copy". |
| POST | [`/fmi/admin/api/v2/schedules/{type}`](#admin-api-post-fmi-admin-api-v2-schedules-type) | Creates a schedule; the filemakerscript, backup and message types exist. |
| GET | [`/fmi/admin/api/v2/schedules/{id}`](#admin-api-get-fmi-admin-api-v2-schedules-id) | One schedule. |
| PATCH | [`/fmi/admin/api/v2/schedules/{id}`](#admin-api-patch-fmi-admin-api-v2-schedules-id) | Changes a schedule's settings, turns it on or off, or runs it now. |
| DELETE | [`/fmi/admin/api/v2/schedules/{id}`](#admin-api-delete-fmi-admin-api-v2-schedules-id) | Deletes a schedule and returns it as it was. |

<a id="admin-api-post-fmi-admin-api-v2-user-auth"></a>

### `POST /fmi/admin/api/v2/user/auth`

Signs in with the admin password and returns a token for the other routes.

**Permissions:** An Authorization: Basic header is always needed. Its password is checked against the server's admin password (any user name), unless the request is let through as the admin console would let it: a Tabularius command on this machine, a current console sign-in cookie, or, while no admin password is set, a loopback client (from elsewhere that is 401 code 9).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Authorization` | header | string | yes | Basic <name:admin password>. Without a Basic header: 401 code 1702. |

**Example:**

```http
POST /fmi/admin/api/v2/user/auth
Authorization: Basic YWRtaW46c2VjcmV0
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "response": {
    "token": "p4Xo2c9yQm1bT8sV0nKe3jLwR6uZaHfD5gC7iEqY1xM"
  },
  "messages": [
    {
      "code": "0",
      "text": "OK"
    }
  ]
}
```

A wrong password is 401 code 212; too many failures 429 code 214 with Retry-After. At most 100 tokens are live at once (401 code 956 beyond that).

<a id="admin-api-delete-fmi-admin-api-v2-user-auth-token"></a>

### `DELETE /fmi/admin/api/v2/user/auth/{token}`

Signs out: the token named in the path stops working.

**Permissions:** A live Admin API token (Bearer).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `token` | path | string | yes | The token to end. |

**Example:**

```http
DELETE /fmi/admin/api/v2/user/auth/p4Xo2c9yQm1bT8sV0nKe3jLwR6uZaHfD5gC7iEqY1xM
Authorization: Bearer p4Xo2c9yQm1bT8sV0nKe3jLwR6uZaHfD5gC7iEqY1xM
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "response": {},
  "messages": [
    {
      "code": "0",
      "text": "OK"
    }
  ]
}
```

<a id="admin-api-get-fmi-admin-api-v2-server-metadata"></a>

### `GET /fmi/admin/api/v2/server/metadata`

The server's name, id, address, Admin API version and local time.

**Permissions:** A live Admin API token (Bearer).

**Example:**

```http
GET /fmi/admin/api/v2/server/metadata
Authorization: Bearer p4Xo2c9yQm1bT8sV0nKe3jLwR6uZaHfD5gC7iEqY1xM
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "response": {
    "serverName": "files",
    "serverID": "9F86D081-884C-7D65-9A2F-EAA0C55AD015",
    "serverIP": "192.168.1.20",
    "serverVersion": "21.0.1.0",
    "ServerVersion": "21.0.1.0",
    "serverHostTime": "2026-10-13T09:30:00",
    "serverHostTimeISO": "2026-10-13T09:30:00-04:00",
    "product": "tabularius"
  },
  "messages": [
    {
      "code": "0",
      "text": "OK"
    }
  ]
}
```

serverVersion is the Admin API level answered as; ServerVersion repeats it for fmcsadmin. serverID is derived from the hosted folder.

<a id="admin-api-get-fmi-admin-api-v2-server-status"></a>

### `GET /fmi/admin/api/v2/server/status`

Whether the server is running or was stopped through this API.

**Permissions:** A live Admin API token (Bearer).

**Example:**

```http
GET /fmi/admin/api/v2/server/status
Authorization: Bearer p4Xo2c9yQm1bT8sV0nKe3jLwR6uZaHfD5gC7iEqY1xM
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "response": {
    "status": "RUNNING"
  },
  "messages": [
    {
      "code": "0",
      "text": "OK"
    }
  ]
}
```

<a id="admin-api-patch-fmi-admin-api-v2-server-status"></a>

### `PATCH /fmi/admin/api/v2/server/status`

STOPPED closes every open file (ending their sessions); RUNNING opens again the files it closed.

**Permissions:** A live Admin API token (Bearer).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `status` | body | string | yes | RUNNING or STOPPED (any case); anything else is 400 code 960. |
| `messageText` | body | string | no | With STOPPED: a message sent to each file's connected clients first (at most 200 characters). |

**Example:**

```http
PATCH /fmi/admin/api/v2/server/status
Authorization: Bearer p4Xo2c9yQm1bT8sV0nKe3jLwR6uZaHfD5gC7iEqY1xM
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "status": "STOPPED",
  "messageText": "Back in ten minutes"
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "response": {
    "status": "STOPPED"
  },
  "messages": [
    {
      "code": "0",
      "text": "OK"
    }
  ]
}
```

The process keeps running: only the files close.

<a id="admin-api-get-fmi-admin-api-v2-server-config-blocknewusers"></a>

### `GET /fmi/admin/api/v2/server/config/blocknewusers`

Whether new users are blocked.

**Permissions:** A live Admin API token (Bearer).

**Example:**

```http
GET /fmi/admin/api/v2/server/config/blocknewusers
Authorization: Bearer p4Xo2c9yQm1bT8sV0nKe3jLwR6uZaHfD5gC7iEqY1xM
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "response": {
    "blockNewUsers": false
  },
  "messages": [
    {
      "code": "0",
      "text": "OK"
    }
  ]
}
```

<a id="admin-api-patch-fmi-admin-api-v2-server-config-blocknewusers"></a>

### `PATCH /fmi/admin/api/v2/server/config/blocknewusers`

Blocks new users, or lets them in again. While blocked, no new session starts (web client and Data API sign-ins, identity-provider sign-ins, AI app sign-ins, SQL connections); sessions already open carry on, AI apps already signed in keep refreshing, and administrators still sign in.

**Permissions:** A live Admin API token (Bearer).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `blockNewUsers` | body | boolean | yes | Missing: 400 code 958; not true or false: 400 code 960. |

**Example:**

```http
PATCH /fmi/admin/api/v2/server/config/blocknewusers
Authorization: Bearer p4Xo2c9yQm1bT8sV0nKe3jLwR6uZaHfD5gC7iEqY1xM
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "blockNewUsers": true
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "response": {
    "blockNewUsers": true
  },
  "messages": [
    {
      "code": "0",
      "text": "OK"
    }
  ]
}
```

Kept in the folder's .openhbam-settings.json, so it lasts across restarts and every worker of a cluster follows it. A refused Data API sign-in is 503 with code 812 (the code FileMaker Server uses here is unconfirmed); a SQL connection gets 57P03. Calls that carry their credentials on each request (OData, MCP with an account and password, API tokens) start no session and are not blocked. The admin console has the same switch (POST /tabularius/admin/v1/block-new-users).

<a id="admin-api-get-fmi-admin-api-v2-server-config-setting"></a>

### `GET /fmi/admin/api/v2/server/config/{setting}`

FileMaker Server settings Tabularius has no counterpart for, answered as the values that describe it, so fmcsadmin's get serverconfig and get serverprefs work.

**Permissions:** A live Admin API token (Bearer).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `setting` | path | string | yes | general: {cacheSize: 512, maxFiles: 256, maxProConnections: 2000, maxPSOS: 500, onlyOpenLastOpenedDatabases: false} (no limits, so FileMaker Server's highest; every hosted file opens; no startupRestorationEnabled, as FileMaker Server 19.1.2 and later answer, which is how fmcsadmin knows not to send it). security: {requireSecureDB}, false when a hosted file allows empty passwords from the LAN. authenticatedstream: {authenticatedStream: 1} (container URLs are signed and expire rather than tied to a session). parallelbackup: {parallelBackupEnabled: false}. persistentcache: {persistentCache: false, persistentCacheSync: false, databaseServerAutoRestart: false}. Any other: 404 code 3. |

**Example:**

```http
GET /fmi/admin/api/v2/server/config/general
Authorization: Bearer p4Xo2c9yQm1bT8sV0nKe3jLwR6uZaHfD5gC7iEqY1xM
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "response": {
    "cacheSize": 512,
    "maxFiles": 256,
    "maxProConnections": 2000,
    "maxPSOS": 500,
    "onlyOpenLastOpenedDatabases": false
  },
  "messages": [
    {
      "code": "0",
      "text": "OK"
    }
  ]
}
```

<a id="admin-api-patch-fmi-admin-api-v2-server-config-setting"></a>

### `PATCH /fmi/admin/api/v2/server/config/{setting}`

Accepts the same values back (fmcsadmin's set serverconfig sends every one); a changed value is 400 code 21 "Not Supported: …" with the reason, an unknown key 400 code 960.

**Permissions:** A live Admin API token (Bearer).

**Example:**

```http
PATCH /fmi/admin/api/v2/server/config/general
Authorization: Bearer p4Xo2c9yQm1bT8sV0nKe3jLwR6uZaHfD5gC7iEqY1xM
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "cacheSize": 1024
}
```

Response `400`:

```json
{
  "response": {},
  "messages": [
    {
      "code": "21",
      "text": "Not Supported: Tabularius has no cache size or limits on files, connections or server scripts to set, always recovers its files, and opens every hosted file at start"
    }
  ]
}
```

<a id="admin-api-patch-fmi-admin-api-v2-server-certificate-csr"></a>

### `PATCH /fmi/admin/api/v2/server/certificate/csr`

Makes a new RSA key and a certificate request (fmcsadmin certificate create) to send to a certificate authority. The key is kept in the folder (.openhbam-tls/imported), encrypted with the password.

**Permissions:** A live Admin API token (Bearer). Not where the server gets its certificate another way (--https, or --tls-cert files not named in the folder's settings): 400 code 21 with the reason.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `subject` | body | string | yes | The subject, base64-encoded as fmcsadmin sends it (or plain): /CN=name/O=organization/OU=…/L=…/ST=…/C=two-letter country. One CN is needed; it is also the request's DNS name (or IP address) when it is one. |
| `password` | body | string | yes | Encrypts the new key until the certificate is imported (4 to 1023 characters). |

**Example:**

```http
PATCH /fmi/admin/api/v2/server/certificate/csr
Authorization: Bearer p4Xo2c9yQm1bT8sV0nKe3jLwR6uZaHfD5gC7iEqY1xM
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "subject": "L0NOPWZpbGVzLmV4YW1wbGUuY29tL089RXhhbXBsZQ==",
  "password": "key-pass"
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "response": {
    "csr": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE REQUEST-----\nMIIC…\n-----END CERTIFICATE REQUEST-----\n"
  },
  "messages": [
    {
      "code": "0",
      "text": "OK"
    }
  ]
}
```

The answer carries the request (FileMaker Server leaves it on the server's disk; here it is also in .openhbam-tls/imported/request.csr). While one waits for its certificate, another is 400 code 1712.

<a id="admin-api-patch-fmi-admin-api-v2-server-certificate-import"></a>

### `PATCH /fmi/admin/api/v2/server/certificate/import`

Puts a certificate in place (fmcsadmin certificate import): checked, saved with its key in the folder, and named in the folder's settings for the next start. A server serving https by itself uses it for new connections at once.

**Permissions:** As for csr.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `certificate` | body | string | yes | The certificate (PEM); a full chain (fullchain.pem) is taken as the certificate and its intermediates. |
| `privateKey` | body | string | no | Its key (PEM). Left out: the key the last csr call made. |
| `intermediateCertificates` | body | string | no | The authority's intermediate certificates (PEM), each signing the one before; served with the certificate. |
| `password` | body | string | no | Opens an encrypted key (the csr call's password). |

**Example:**

```http
PATCH /fmi/admin/api/v2/server/certificate/import
Authorization: Bearer p4Xo2c9yQm1bT8sV0nKe3jLwR6uZaHfD5gC7iEqY1xM
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "certificate": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nMIIE…",
  "intermediateCertificates": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nMIIF…",
  "password": "key-pass"
}
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "response": {
    "subject": "CN=files.example.com, O=Example",
    "expires": "2027-11-14T23:59:59.000Z",
    "restartRequired": false
  },
  "messages": [
    {
      "code": "0",
      "text": "OK"
    }
  ]
}
```

Refused with 400 code 960 and the reason: not a certificate, a key that doesn't open or doesn't go with it, expired or not yet valid, or an intermediate that didn't sign the one before. restartRequired is true where the front process of a cluster, or a server without https, serves it from the next start. The key is saved decrypted, readable by the server's own user only.

<a id="admin-api-delete-fmi-admin-api-v2-server-certificate-delete"></a>

### `DELETE /fmi/admin/api/v2/server/certificate/delete`

Removes the imported certificate, its key and any waiting request (fmcsadmin certificate delete); the folder's settings go back to the certificate they named before the first import (migrate-fms's, say), or to none, for the next start.

**Permissions:** As for csr.

**Example:**

```http
DELETE /fmi/admin/api/v2/server/certificate/delete
Authorization: Bearer p4Xo2c9yQm1bT8sV0nKe3jLwR6uZaHfD5gC7iEqY1xM
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "response": {
    "restartRequired": true
  },
  "messages": [
    {
      "code": "0",
      "text": "OK"
    }
  ]
}
```

Nothing imported: 404 code 1700.

<a id="admin-api-get-fmi-admin-api-v2-php-config"></a>

### `GET /fmi/admin/api/v2/php/config`

FileMaker Server's PHP publishing settings, answered as off: Tabularius has no PHP publishing. Also /xml/config ({enabled: true}: the XML interface at /fmi/xml is served, reads only) and /fmclients/httpstunneling ({enableHTTPSTunneling: false}).

**Permissions:** A live Admin API token (Bearer).

**Example:**

```http
GET /fmi/admin/api/v2/php/config
Authorization: Bearer p4Xo2c9yQm1bT8sV0nKe3jLwR6uZaHfD5gC7iEqY1xM
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "response": {
    "enabled": false,
    "characterEncoding": "UTF-8",
    "errorMessageLanguage": "en",
    "dataPreValidation": false,
    "useFileMakerPhp": false
  },
  "messages": [
    {
      "code": "0",
      "text": "OK"
    }
  ]
}
```

PATCH accepts the same values back; changing one (turning PHP or tunneling on, or the XML interface off) answers 400 code 21 "Not Supported: …" (use the Data API or OData). fmcsadmin's get cwpconfig and get serverprefs EnableHttpProtocolNetwork read these.

<a id="admin-api-get-fmi-admin-api-v2-plugins"></a>

### `GET /fmi/admin/api/v2/plugins`

Installed plug-ins (the server folder's plugins/), as fmcsadmin list plugins shows them; enabled when any hosted file has it turned on.

**Permissions:** A live Admin API token (Bearer).

**Example:**

```http
GET /fmi/admin/api/v2/plugins
Authorization: Bearer p4Xo2c9yQm1bT8sV0nKe3jLwR6uZaHfD5gC7iEqY1xM
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "response": {
    "plugins": [
      {
        "id": "1",
        "pluginName": "Text Tools",
        "filename": "com.example.text-tools",
        "version": "1.2.0",
        "enabled": true
      }
    ]
  },
  "messages": [
    {
      "code": "0",
      "text": "OK"
    }
  ]
}
```

Plug-ins are turned on for each file in plugins/enabled.json, not through this API.

<a id="admin-api-get-fmi-admin-api-v2-databases"></a>

### `GET /fmi/admin/api/v2/databases`

The hosted files, with their status, size, connected clients and the extended privileges their privilege sets use.

**Permissions:** A live Admin API token (Bearer).

**Example:**

```http
GET /fmi/admin/api/v2/databases
```

### `POST /fmi/admin/api/v2/schedules/{type}`

Creates a schedule; the filemakerscript, backup and message types exist.

**Permissions:** A live Admin API token (Bearer).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | path | string | yes | filemakerscript, backup or message. Any other (verify, systemscript, …) is 400 code 21 "Not Supported". The body must carry the matching filemakerScriptType, backupType or messageType (else 958). |
| `name` | body | string | yes | 1 to 100 characters. |
| `enabled` | body | boolean | no | Default false. |
| `filemakerScriptType` | body | object | no | For filemakerscript: {resource: "file:Name.fmp12", fmScriptName, fmScriptParam, fmScriptAccount}. |
| `messageType` | body | object | no | For message: {resourceType: "ALL_CLIENTS" (others 21), text (1 to 200 characters)}. Each run sends the text to every connected client, as the clients message call does, and records how many it reached. |
| `backupType` | body | object | no | For backup: {resourceType: "ALL_DB" (every hosted file; others 21), backupTarget (a folder; the backups folder when omitted), retainBackups (1 to 1000, default 7)}. clone and verifyBackup true are 21. Each run makes a new set under the target and removes the oldest beyond retainBackups. |
| `everyndaysType` | body | object | no | {startTimeStamp (its time of day is used), dailyDays, repeatTask: {repeatFrequency, repeatInterval: HOURS \| MINUTES}}. Default every day. |

<a id="replication"></a>

## Replication (standby servers)

A standby server (tabularius standby) keeps a live copy of every hosted file: it copies each file once, then follows its changes, taken every second. These routes exist only when the server was started with --replication-token; each takes that token as Authorization: Bearer (otherwise 401 {"error":"replication token needed"}) and answers GET only (otherwise 405 {"error":"GET only"}). Errors are JSON {"error": …}. Changes are numbered within a run (one per server start, per file), and the last ten minutes of them are kept in memory.

Source: `packages/server/src/replication.ts`

| Method | Path | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | [`/tabularius/replication/v1/files`](#replication-get-tabularius-replication-v1-files) | The hosted files, each with its current run and the number of its latest change. |
| GET | [`/tabularius/replication/v1/files/{database}/copy`](#replication-get-tabularius-replication-v1-files-database-copy) | The whole file as it is now, made with SQLite's online backup so people keep working. |
| GET | [`/tabularius/replication/v1/files/{database}/changes`](#replication-get-tabularius-replication-v1-files-database-changes) | The file's changes after a given number, waiting for some when there are none yet. |

<a id="replication-get-tabularius-replication-v1-files"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/replication/v1/files`

The hosted files, each with its current run and the number of its latest change.

**Permissions:** The replication token (Bearer).

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/replication/v1/files
Authorization: Bearer 7c1f0e4b9a2d4e8f8b3a6c5d2e1f0a9b
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "files": [
    {
      "name": "Invoices",
      "run": "5f3a9c0e1b2d4a6f",
      "seq": 1284
    }
  ]
}
```

Files hosted since the last call are followed from now on.

<a id="replication-get-tabularius-replication-v1-files-database-copy"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/replication/v1/files/{database}/copy`

The whole file as it is now, made with SQLite's online backup so people keep working.

**Permissions:** The replication token (Bearer).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | path | string | yes | The hosted file's name; unknown or not yet followed: 404 {"error":"no such file (or its changes are not followed yet)"}. |

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/replication/v1/files/Invoices/copy
Authorization: Bearer 7c1f0e4b9a2d4e8f8b3a6c5d2e1f0a9b
```

Response `200`:

```text
(the file, Content-Type: application/vnd.sqlite3, with headers X-Tabularius-Run, X-Tabularius-Seq (the change it is from) and X-Tabularius-Whole-After (the change after which the copy is consistent); the same three also as X-Openhbam-Run, -Seq and -Whole-After, for a standby from before the rename)
```

<a id="replication-get-tabularius-replication-v1-files-database-changes"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/replication/v1/files/{database}/changes`

The file's changes after a given number, waiting for some when there are none yet.

**Permissions:** The replication token (Bearer).

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | path | string | yes | The hosted file's name. |
| `run` | query | string | yes | The run the standby is following; another run is 409 "the server restarted since: copy the file again". |
| `after` | query | number | yes | The last change the standby has; one this run never had is 409. |
| `wait` | query | number | no | Seconds to wait for a change when there is none yet (0 to 30, default 0). |

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/replication/v1/files/Invoices/changes?run=5f3a9c0e1b2d4a6f&after=1280&wait=0
Authorization: Bearer 7c1f0e4b9a2d4e8f8b3a6c5d2e1f0a9b
```

Response `200`:

```text
(the encoded change records after `after`, at most 32 MB, Content-Type: application/octet-stream, with X-Tabularius-Run and X-Tabularius-Seq (the latest change), also sent as X-Openhbam-Run and X-Openhbam-Seq; empty when the wait ran out)
```

Errors carry the current run and seq: {"error", "run", "seq"}. 410 "too far behind: copy the file again" when the changes asked for are no longer kept; 409 "the file was taken up again: copy it again" when the file was reopened while waiting; 503 "the server is stopping".

<a id="oidc"></a>

## Sign-in through an identity provider (OpenID Connect)

Web client sign-in through Microsoft Entra ID, Google, Okta, Apple or another OpenID Connect provider, set up on the server. The provider vouches for an email address (and groups), and the file's external accounts (named by email, @domain or group) give the privilege set. These routes need no sign-in. When something goes wrong, the start and callback routes redirect (302) to /app/#error=<message> for the web client to show. With providers set up, any other path under /tabularius/auth/v1/ is 404 {"error":"not found"}. Pending state lives in .openhbam-oidc/pending.sqlite in the hosted folder, inside a private directory, allowing sign-ins to survive restarts and several processes serving that folder to share pending state. Cluster routing already sends every /tabularius/auth/ request, including starts and callbacks, to the leader; the database is not needed to route callbacks across workers. AI-app resume handlers are process-local on the leader and do not survive a restart, so an interrupted AI-app sign-in must be started again. SQLite lock contention returns a temporary-unavailable sign-in error; moving database waits off the request event loop with asynchronous retry remains future work. Data API apps sign in through the same providers with FileMaker Server's OAuth routes (/fmws/oauthproviderinfo and /oauth/getoauthurl), then log in to the Data API with the X-FM-Data-OAuth-Request-Id and X-FM-Data-OAuth-Identifier headers. Their pending sign-ins and the identifiers they hand out are kept in the same shared database, so any process serving the folder can finish the login, once.

Source: `packages/server/src/oidc.ts`, `packages/server/src/index.ts`

| Method | Path | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | [`/tabularius/auth/v1/providers`](#oidc-get-tabularius-auth-v1-providers) | The providers set up, for the sign-in screen's buttons. |
| GET | [`/tabularius/auth/v1/oidc/start/{provider}`](#oidc-get-tabularius-auth-v1-oidc-start-provider) | Starts a sign-in to a file: redirects to the provider's authorization page (code flow with PKCE and a nonce). |
| GET | [`/tabularius/auth/v1/oidc/callback`](#oidc-get-tabularius-auth-v1-oidc-callback) | Where the provider sends people back: exchanges the code, checks the ID token and opens a web client session. |
| POST | [`/tabularius/auth/v1/oidc/callback`](#oidc-post-tabularius-auth-v1-oidc-callback) | The same callback for providers that reply with form_post (Apple): the state and code come as a form body. |
| GET | [`/fmws/oauthproviderinfo`](#oidc-get-fmws-oauthproviderinfo) | The providers set up, as FileMaker Server lists them for Data API apps. |
| GET | [`/oauth/getoauthurl`](#oidc-get-oauth-getoauthurl) | Starts a Data API app's sign-in: answers the provider's authorization address to open, as FileMaker Server does. |

<a id="oidc-get-tabularius-auth-v1-providers"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/auth/v1/providers`

The providers set up, for the sign-in screen's buttons.

**Permissions:** None.

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/auth/v1/providers
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "providers": [
    {
      "name": "Google",
      "slug": "google",
      "start": "/tabularius/auth/v1/oidc/start/google"
    },
    {
      "name": "Apple",
      "slug": "apple",
      "start": "/tabularius/auth/v1/oidc/start/apple"
    }
  ]
}
```

With none set up the server answers {"providers":[]} (for any method).

<a id="oidc-get-tabularius-auth-v1-oidc-start-provider"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/auth/v1/oidc/start/{provider}`

Starts a sign-in to a file: redirects to the provider's authorization page (code flow with PKCE and a nonce).

**Permissions:** None.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `provider` | path | string | no | The provider's slug from /providers. Left off (/oidc/start), the sole provider is used; with several that is an error ("Choose a sign-in provider"). An unknown slug: "Unknown sign-in provider". |
| `db` | query | string | yes | The hosted file to sign in to; unknown: 'No hosted database named "…"'. |

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/auth/v1/oidc/start/google?db=Invoices
```

Response `302`:

```text
(a redirect to the provider's authorization endpoint with response_type=code, client_id, redirect_uri=<server>/tabularius/auth/v1/oidc/callback, scope "openid email profile" plus any extra, state, nonce, code_challenge and code_challenge_method=S256; response_mode=form_post for providers set up with it, such as Apple)
```

A sign-in must come back within 10 minutes.

<a id="oidc-get-tabularius-auth-v1-oidc-callback"></a>

### `GET /tabularius/auth/v1/oidc/callback`

Where the provider sends people back: exchanges the code, checks the ID token and opens a web client session.

**Permissions:** None: the state from the start route and the provider's code are the credential. The ID token's signature (the provider's published keys), issuer, audience, expiry and nonce are checked, and the email (or a group) must match an external account in the file.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `state` | query | string | yes | From the start route; used once. |
| `code` | query | string | yes | The provider's authorization code. |
| `error` | query | string | no | Sent by the provider instead of a code; shown with error_description. |

**Example:**

```http
GET /tabularius/auth/v1/oidc/callback?code=4%2F0AVG7fiQ&state=r2D9kq3Vx7mN1pL5sT8wY0zA4bC6eF2h
```

Response `302`:

```text
(a redirect to /app/#db=Invoices&token=<session token>: the session goes to the web client in the URL fragment)
```

Errors include "The sign-in took too long or was already used; please try again" and "<email> has no external account in <file>".

<a id="oidc-post-tabularius-auth-v1-oidc-callback"></a>

### `POST /tabularius/auth/v1/oidc/callback`

The same callback for providers that reply with form_post (Apple): the state and code come as a form body.

**Permissions:** None, as for GET.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `state` | body | string | yes | Form field (application/x-www-form-urlencoded). |
| `code` | body | string | yes | Form field. |

**Example:**

```http
POST /tabularius/auth/v1/oidc/callback
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

state=r2D9kq3Vx7mN1pL5sT8wY0zA4bC6eF2h&code=c1a2b3d4e5f6
```

Response `302`:

```text
(a redirect to /app/#db=Invoices&token=<session token>)
```

The body is limited to 1 MB.

<a id="oidc-get-fmws-oauthproviderinfo"></a>

### `GET /fmws/oauthproviderinfo`

The providers set up, as FileMaker Server lists them for Data API apps.

**Permissions:** None.

**Example:**

```http
GET /fmws/oauthproviderinfo
```

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "Name": "Google",
      "Slug": "google"
    },
    {
      "Name": "Apple",
      "Slug": "apple"
    }
  ]
}
```

Served only when providers are set up.

<a id="oidc-get-oauth-getoauthurl"></a>

### `GET /oauth/getoauthurl`

Starts a Data API app's sign-in: answers the provider's authorization address to open, as FileMaker Server does.

**Permissions:** None. Where the person is sent back must be this server's own address or one the provider's dataApiReturnUrls lists (an origin, or an address and the paths below it); this computer (localhost) only when listed.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `trackingID` | query | string | yes | The app's own id for this sign-in, sent back with the identifier (at most 256 characters). |
| `provider` | query | string | no | The provider's Name or Slug from /fmws/oauthproviderinfo. Left off, the sole provider is used. |
| `X-FMS-Return-URL` | header | string | yes | Where the app wants the person sent back after signing in. |

**Example:**

```http
GET /oauth/getoauthurl?trackingID=7f3a9c&provider=Google
X-FMS-Return-URL: https://app.example.com/back
```

Response `200`:

```text
(the provider's authorization address as text/plain, also in the X-FMS-Return-URL response header, with X-FMS-Request-ID: <request id>)
```

After signing in (choosing the account at the provider), the person is redirected to the return address with ?trackingID=<id>&identifier=<identifier>, or &error=<message>. The app then calls POST /fmi/data/vLatest/databases/{db}/sessions with X-FM-Data-OAuth-Request-Id: <request id> and X-FM-Data-OAuth-Identifier: <identifier>; the pair works once, within 5 minutes. Errors are 400 {"error":"…"}, such as "trackingID is required" and "Unknown sign-in provider".
